#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) fn claim(
    tx: &mut impl AuthorizationRequestsTx,
    pairing_request: &PairingRequest,
    session_ttl: Duration,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<Option<Self>, AuthorizationServerError> {
    let Ok(claimed) = pairing_request.claim(now) else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    let Some(approval) = claimed.state.approval() else {
        return Ok(None);
    };
    if !tx.replace_pairing_request(pairing_request, &claimed)? {
        return Ok(None);
    }
    Ok(Some(ClaimedBrowserPairing {
        session: BrowserSession::new_paired_session(
            claimed.browser_name.clone(),
            approval.granted_scopes.clone(),
            session_ttl,
            now,
        ),
    }))
}
}

Token Entitlement

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/authority/token_entitlement.rs

An access token says who it was issued to, what it may do, for which patient, and in which browser session. None of that is ever assembled by a caller. A token entitlement is the proof a token is minted under: one variant per proof on the pages before this one that a token may be minted for. The access-token minter takes nothing else, so a token’s claims are always the ones a check produced.

Each variant reads its claims off the proof it holds:

  • a redeemed sign-in code or a claimed pairing gives the browser-session client, and the session’s scopes and sid;
  • a redeemed code, a claimed device request or a validated refresh token gives the redeeming app, and the scopes, patient and sid of the record redeemed.

The entitlement has no unit test of its own. The access-token minter’s test, on the Access Token Minter page, shows a token carrying exactly what a redeemed code’s entitlement holds.

domain::authority::token_entitlement

TokenEntitlement

The proof a token is minted under. The variants are the whole answer to “what can a token be minted for?” — an enum, not a trait, for the reason in the module docs.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) enum TokenEntitlement<'a> {
    /// A redeemed same-device sign-in code: the token is the Owner's, for
    /// the same-device session the sign-in starts.
    SameDeviceSignIn(&'a RedeemedSameDeviceSignInCode),
    /// A claimed browser pairing: the token is the paired browser's, for the
    /// paired session the claim starts, with the scopes the Owner granted.
    BrowserPairing(&'a ClaimedBrowserPairing),
    /// An authorization code redeemed at `/oauth/token`: the token carries
    /// the scopes, patient and browser session the code was issued with.
    AuthorizationCode(&'a RedeemedAuthorizationCode),
    /// An approved device request claimed by its poll: the token carries what
    /// the Owner approved, and no browser session.
    DeviceCode(&'a ConsumedDeviceRequest),
    /// A live refresh token, validated before its rotation: the token carries
    /// what its family was started with.
    RefreshToken(&'a ValidatedRefreshToken),
}
}

    match self {
        TokenEntitlement::SameDeviceSignIn(redeemed_sign_in_code) => {
            Some(redeemed_sign_in_code.session().sid.as_str())
        }
        TokenEntitlement::BrowserPairing(claimed_pairing) => {
            Some(claimed_pairing.session().sid.as_str())
        }
        TokenEntitlement::AuthorizationCode(redeemed_code) => Some(redeemed_code.sid()),
        TokenEntitlement::DeviceCode(_) => None,
        TokenEntitlement::RefreshToken(validated_refresh_token) => {
            validated_refresh_token.sid()
        }
    }
}
}

Writers

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/writers/mod.rs

Some writes hand out authority: approving a request, issuing an authorization code, recording or widening a standing grant, widening an app’s registration, reading a private key to sign a token with, issuing a refresh token, starting a browser session. Every one of them happens in a writer, and every writer method takes an authority proof as the price of admission. A proof can only be had from its one constructor, which runs the check it stands for, so a write that holds the proof is a write whose check ran.

A writer is not a gate of its own. It is built over the caller’s open scope (within(tx)), so what it writes lands with the rest of the operation or not at all, and the gate is the proof each method demands. The capabilities in the next part decide what is being done and obtain the proof; the Grant Store holds the rows. The writers sit between them: the only code that may make the privileged store calls.

  • Request Approver: approves a pending request of any flow, on delegated scopes, and for the code flow issues its code, on delegated scopes or a standing grant, bounded by the requesting browser’s session.
  • Grant Recorder: records the standing grant an approval leaves behind, and registers or widens an app trusted on first use, on delegated scopes.
  • Refresh Family Writer: starts a refresh-token family for a redemption that earns one, and rotates a validated refresh token, expiring the family on a replay.
  • Access Token Minter: reads the active signing key and signs an access token carrying exactly a token entitlement’s claims.
  • Browser Session Writer: stores the session a same-device sign-in or a claimed pairing starts.
  • Test Fixtures: the helpers the writers’ tests share.

domain::capabilities::writers::tests

A privileged write outside the writers fails the unit tests. A new flow that reached around a writer would reach around the proof the writer’s method demands, so the rule is pinned by a source guard rather than left to review. The guard holds two lists, each against the paths allowed it, and scans production code only (production_lines).

What makes an authorization request approved or claimed, and where each may appear. An approved request is what a code, a device grant or a paired session is issued against, so only these may build one:

  • each flow’s approve transition, called only by the writers, under the proof they demand;
  • each polled flow’s claim transition, called only by the writers and by the two authority proofs whose single-use redemption it is (ConsumedDeviceRequest and ClaimedBrowserPairing);
  • the Approved( and Claimed( states, built only by the entity’s transitions and the flow’s row conversion that reads them back (any file may match on them);
  • a flow’s struct literal (CodeRequest {, …), which could carry another request’s state over, built only there too.

holds

Whether line holds needle, at the start of a name when the needle starts with one. A type named where a type goes, after ->, for or impl, builds nothing.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn holds(line: &str, needle: &str) -> bool {
    let starts_a_name = needle.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_alphabetic());
    line.match_indices(needle).any(|(at, _)| {
        if !starts_a_name {
            return true;
        }
        let before = &line[..at];
        let mid_name = before
            .chars()
            .next_back()
            .is_some_and(|c| c.is_alphanumeric() || c == '_' || c == '<');
        let names_a_type = before.trim_end().ends_with("->")
            || before
                .split_whitespace()
                .next_back()
                .is_some_and(|word| word == "for" || word == "impl");
        !mid_name && !names_a_type
    })
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/writers/mod.rs lines 169–187 · authorization-server in the code index

violations

Every privileged call or approval construction in the production lines of source, the file at relative under src/, that its location doesn’t allow, as relative:line needle.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn violations(relative: &str, source: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    let privileged_calls_allowed = ALLOWED_PREFIXES
        .iter()
        .any(|prefix| relative.starts_with(prefix));
    for (n, line) in production_lines(source) {
        if !privileged_calls_allowed {
            for needle in PRIVILEGED_CALLS {
                if holds(&line, needle) {
                    found.push(format!("{relative}:{n} {needle}"));
                }
            }
        }
        for construction in APPROVAL_CONSTRUCTIONS {
            if construction
                .allowed
                .iter()
                .any(|prefix| relative.starts_with(prefix))
            {
                continue;
            }
            let built_in = match line.find("=>") {
                Some(arrow) if construction.read_in_match_arms => &line[arrow + 2..],
                _ => line.as_str(),
            };
            if holds(built_in, construction.needle) {
                found.push(format!("{relative}:{n} {}", construction.needle));
            }
        }
    }
    found
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/writers/mod.rs lines 192–223 · authorization-server in the code index

The guard trips on every approval construction outside its allowed files, and on none inside them; a match arm’s pattern reading a state doesn’t trip it, nor does a name that merely ends like a needle.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn the_guard_catches_every_approval_construction_outside_its_files() {
    const FLOW: &str = "domain/capabilities/oauth/flow.rs";
    for construction in APPROVAL_CONSTRUCTIONS {
        let needle = construction.needle;
        let receiver = if needle.starts_with('.') {
            "request"
        } else {
            "flow::"
        };
        let built = format!("fn f() {{\n    let x = {receiver}{needle}y;\n}}\n");
        assert_eq!(
            violations(FLOW, &built).len(),
            1,
            "{needle} outside its files"
        );
        let built_in_an_arm = format!("fn f() {{\n    a => {receiver}{needle}y,\n}}\n");
        assert_eq!(
            violations(FLOW, &built_in_an_arm).len(),
            1,
            "{needle} built in a match arm"
        );
        let read_in_an_arm = format!("fn f() {{\n    {receiver}{needle}y) => a,\n}}\n");
        assert_eq!(
            violations(FLOW, &read_in_an_arm).is_empty(),
            construction.read_in_match_arms,
            "{needle} in a match arm's pattern"
        );
        for prefix in construction.allowed {
            let relative = if prefix.ends_with(".rs") {
                (*prefix).to_owned()
            } else {
                format!("{prefix}inner.rs")
            };
            assert!(
                violations(&relative, &built).is_empty(),
                "{needle} in {relative}"
            );
        }
    }
    assert!(violations(
        FLOW,
        "fn f() -> CodeRequest {\n    let r = ResolvedCodeRequest {\n        a: NotApproved(1),\n    };\n}\nimpl Polled for DeviceRequest {\n}\n",
    )
    .is_empty());
    assert_eq!(
        violations(FLOW, "fn f() {\n    tx.insert_browser_session(&s);\n}\n").len(),
        1
    );
}
}

privileged_store_calls_happen_only_in_writers

Default-safety guard: a privileged store method is called only inside a writer (or the adapter / port / fake / seeding files that define it), and an approved or claimed request is built only where APPROVAL_CONSTRUCTIONS allows. A new flow that reaches around the writers — and so around the proof its method would have demanded — fails here. Comments and unit-test modules are skipped (see production_lines): prose may name the methods, and a test may plant rows to arrange its state. A floor on the number of files checked catches the guard walking an empty tree.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn privileged_store_calls_happen_only_in_writers() {
    let src = std::path::Path::new(concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/src"));
    let mut checked = 0;
    let mut found = Vec::new();
    for path in rs_files_under(src).expect("enumerate src") {
        let relative = relative_to(&path, src).expect("enumerated under src");
        let source =
            std::fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("read {relative}: {e}"));
        found.extend(violations(&relative, &source));
        checked += 1;
    }
    assert!(
        found.is_empty(),
        "privileged calls or approval constructions outside where they belong; obtain the \
         authority proof and go through `domain::capabilities::writers`: {found:#?}",
    );
    assert!(
        checked >= 40,
        "only {checked} source files enumerated — did src/ move?",
    );
}
}

Request Approver

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/writers/request_approver.rs

The request approver moves a pending authorization request to approved, through the flow’s own transition (code, device, pairing) written with the guarded replace. For the code flow it also issues the authorization code the app redeems at /oauth/token.

The scopes a request records are exactly the proof’s, never a list the flow put together. A device request and a browser pairing are approved on delegated scopes: the approver’s ticks, clamped to what it may delegate. A code request may also be approved with no one at the prompt, on a standing grant that already covers it, so it takes either of two proofs.

A code is bound to the browser session the request was made in, not the approver’s. The Owner may approve from another browser, but revoking the browser the app runs in still ends what the code starts, and the code carries only what that browser holds (session_bounded_scopes).

The tests park requests and approve them with the request-approver fixtures.

CodeAuthority

On whose authority a code-flow request is approved — the two proofs that may issue an authorization code. Listing them here is the point: a reader auditing “who can issue a code with no human?” finds StandingGrant by name — an enum, not a trait, for the reason in the authority module docs.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) enum CodeAuthority<'a> {
    /// An approver (the Owner, or a browser the Owner paired) approved the
    /// prompt, delegating these scopes.
    OwnerDelegated(&'a DelegatedScopes),
    /// A standing grant already covered every requested scope, so the code is
    /// issued with nobody asked, and the grant is stamped used.
    StandingGrant(&'a StandingGrantCoverage),
}
}

authorized_scopes

The scopes this authority lets a code carry.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn authorized_scopes(&self) -> &[String] {
    match self {
        CodeAuthority::OwnerDelegated(delegated) => delegated.scopes(),
        CodeAuthority::StandingGrant(standing_grant_coverage) => {
            standing_grant_coverage.covered_scopes()
        }
    }
}
}

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) enum CodeApproval {
    /// The request was approved and this code issued for it.
    Issued(Box<AuthorizationCode>),
    /// The request was no longer pending (a concurrent decision or expiry
    /// won); nothing changed.
    RequestNotPending,
    /// The browser session the request was made in has ended — revoked,
    /// expired, stale, or no longer stored — so it bounds no code: the
    /// request was denied instead, and no code issued.
    BrowserSessionEnded,
}
}

RequestApprover

Approve pending requests of all three flows and, for the code flow, issue the request’s authorization code, inside the caller’s transaction. The gate is the proof each method takes: a DelegatedScopes for a device request or a browser pairing, a CodeAuthority (delegated scopes or a StandingGrantCoverage) for a code.

}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/writers/request_approver.rs lines 81–83 · authorization-server in the code index

approve_for_code

The session is checked with is_live_at, under the stale-session cutoff, and the code lives for AUTHORIZATION_CODE_TTL.

Approve the pending code-flow request under authority and issue code for it, bound to the request’s client, redirect, and PKCE challenge, to the browser session the request was made in (not the approver’s, so revoking the browser the app runs in ends it), and to the SMART-on-FHIR patient context (if any), expiring AUTHORIZATION_CODE_TTL after now. The flow generates code (a CSPRNG opaque token) so tests can inject a known value.

The request records the authority’s scopes; the code carries only those the request’s browser session also allows (session_bounded_scopes), so a browser paired with less than the Owner holds earns no app more than it holds, whoever approved.

Under a CodeAuthority::StandingGrant, issuing the code also stamps that grant’s last_used_at with now: the grant just stood in for the Owner.

The approval and the code land in the caller’s transaction, which first loads the request’s browser session. A request whose session is no longer live at now under stale_session_cutoff (revoked, expired, stale, or no longer stored) is denied rather than approved (CodeApproval::BrowserSessionEnded), so the client hears access_denied rather than earning a code no live session bounds. A request no longer pending issues nothing (CodeApproval::RequestNotPending); the flow maps that to its own not-found outcome.

Errors

AuthorizationServerError::Infrastructure on a store failure.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) fn approve_for_code(
    &mut self,
    authority: CodeAuthority<'_>,
    request: &CodeRequest,
    patient: Option<&str>,
    code: String,
    stale_session_cutoff: &StaleSessionCutoff,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<CodeApproval, AuthorizationServerError> {
    let authorized_scopes = authority.authorized_scopes();
    let Some(browser_session) = self
        .tx
        .browser_session_by_sid(&request.sid)?
        .filter(|browser_session| browser_session.is_live_at(now, stale_session_cutoff))
    else {
        let Ok(denied) = request.deny(now) else {
            return Ok(CodeApproval::RequestNotPending);
        };
        return Ok(if self.tx.replace_code_request(request, &denied)? {
            CodeApproval::BrowserSessionEnded
        } else {
            CodeApproval::RequestNotPending
        });
    };
    let approval = Approval {
        granted_scopes: authorized_scopes.to_vec(),
        patient: patient.map(str::to_owned),
    };
    let Ok(approved) = request.approve(approval, now) else {
        return Ok(CodeApproval::RequestNotPending);
    };
    if !self.tx.replace_code_request(request, &approved)? {
        return Ok(CodeApproval::RequestNotPending);
    }
    let authorization_code = AuthorizationCode {
        code,
        request_id: request.id.clone(),
        client_id: request.client_id.clone(),
        redirect_uri: request.redirect_uri.clone(),
        code_challenge: request.code_challenge.clone(),
        granted_scopes: session_bounded_scopes(
            authorized_scopes,
            &Grant::parse(&browser_session.scopes),
        ),
        patient: patient.map(str::to_owned),
        issued_at: now,
        expires_at: now + AUTHORIZATION_CODE_TTL,
        sid: browser_session.sid,
    };
    self.tx.issue_authorization_code(&authorization_code)?;
    if let CodeAuthority::StandingGrant(standing_grant_coverage) = authority {
        self.tx
            .stamp_authorization_code_grant_used(standing_grant_coverage.grant_id(), now)?;
    }
    Ok(CodeApproval::Issued(Box::new(authorization_code)))
}
}

The code flow: the request is approved with the proof’s scopes and the patient, and the issued code is bound to the request’s client, redirect, and challenge with the same scopes.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn approve_for_code_records_the_proofs_scopes_on_request_and_code() {
    let store = FakeGrantStore::default();
    let pending_request = pending_code_request(&store, "req-1");
    let now = Utc::now();
    let CodeApproval::Issued(issued_code) = RequestApprover::within(&mut store.tx())
        .approve_for_code(
            CodeAuthority::OwnerDelegated(&delegated_scopes(&["patient/Patient.r"])),
            &pending_request,
            Some("pat-1"),
            "the-code".to_owned(),
            &StaleSessionCutoff::none(),
            now,
        )
        .unwrap()
    else {
        panic!("request was pending");
    };
    assert_eq!(
        *issued_code,
        AuthorizationCode {
            code: "the-code".to_owned(),
            request_id: "req-1".to_owned(),
            client_id: "client".to_owned(),
            redirect_uri: pending_request.redirect_uri.clone(),
            code_challenge: pending_request.code_challenge.clone(),
            granted_scopes: owned_scopes(&["patient/Patient.r"]),
            patient: Some("pat-1".to_owned()),
            issued_at: now,
            expires_at: now + AUTHORIZATION_CODE_TTL,
            sid: pending_request.sid.clone(),
        }
    );
    assert_eq!(
        stored(&store, "req-1"),
        AuthorizationRequest::Code(CodeRequest {
            state: CodeRequestState::Approved(Approval {
                granted_scopes: owned_scopes(&["patient/Patient.r"]),
                patient: Some("pat-1".to_owned()),
            }),
            ..pending_request
        })
    );
    assert_eq!(
        store
            .tx()
            .authorization_code_by_request_id("req-1")
            .unwrap(),
        Some(*issued_code)
    );
}
}

A code issued under a standing grant stamps that grant used at the issuing instant; one the Owner approved leaves it alone, and so does a request denied because its browser session ended.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn approve_for_code_stamps_only_the_standing_grant_it_issues_under() {
    let store = FakeGrantStore::default();
    let pending_request = pending_code_request(&store, "req-1");
    let coverage = standing_grant_coverage(&store, &pending_request);

    let owner_approved = pending_code_request(&store, "req-owner");
    assert!(matches!(
        approve(&store, &owner_approved),
        CodeApproval::Issued(_)
    ));
    assert_eq!(grant_last_used_at(&store), None);

    let signed_out = pending_code_request_in_session(&store, "req-signed-out", "gone");
    assert_eq!(
        RequestApprover::within(&mut store.tx())
            .approve_for_code(
                CodeAuthority::StandingGrant(&coverage),
                &signed_out,
                None,
                "no-code".to_owned(),
                &StaleSessionCutoff::none(),
                Utc::now(),
            )
            .unwrap(),
        CodeApproval::BrowserSessionEnded
    );
    assert_eq!(grant_last_used_at(&store), None);

    let now = Utc::now();
    assert!(matches!(
        RequestApprover::within(&mut store.tx())
            .approve_for_code(
                CodeAuthority::StandingGrant(&coverage),
                &pending_request,
                None,
                "the-code".to_owned(),
                &StaleSessionCutoff::none(),
                now,
            )
            .unwrap(),
        CodeApproval::Issued(_)
    ));
    assert_eq!(grant_last_used_at(&store), Some(now));
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/writers/request_approver.rs lines 443–462 · authorization-server in the code index

A request made in a browser session that has since been revoked, that has expired without being revoked, that the cutoff makes stale, or that names no session, is denied and earns no code; one whose session stands is approved.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn approve_for_code_denies_a_request_whose_browser_session_has_ended() {
    let store = FakeGrantStore::default();
    let now = Utc::now();
    let stale_session_cutoff =
        StaleSessionCutoff::new(now - Duration::minutes(30), HashSet::new());
    let standing = BrowserSession::new_same_device_session(vec![], Duration::hours(8), now);
    let revoked = BrowserSession::new_same_device_session(vec![], Duration::hours(8), now);
    let expired = BrowserSession::new_same_device_session(
        vec![],
        Duration::hours(8),
        now - Duration::hours(9),
    );
    let stale = BrowserSession::new_same_device_session(
        vec![],
        Duration::hours(8),
        now - Duration::hours(1),
    );
    for session in [&standing, &revoked, &expired, &stale] {
        store.tx().insert_browser_session(session).unwrap();
    }
    assert!(store
        .tx()
        .revoke_browser_session(&revoked.sid, now)
        .unwrap());

    for (id, sid) in [
        ("req-revoked", revoked.sid.as_str()),
        ("req-expired", expired.sid.as_str()),
        ("req-stale", stale.sid.as_str()),
        ("req-missing", "no-such-sid"),
    ] {
        let pending_request = pending_code_request_in_session(&store, id, sid);
        assert_eq!(
            approve_under(&store, &pending_request, &stale_session_cutoff),
            CodeApproval::BrowserSessionEnded,
            "{id}"
        );
        assert_eq!(stored(&store, id).status(), RequestStatus::Denied, "{id}");
        assert_eq!(
            store.tx().authorization_code_by_request_id(id).unwrap(),
            None,
            "{id}"
        );
    }

    let pending_request =
        pending_code_request_in_session(&store, "req-standing", &standing.sid);
    assert!(matches!(
        approve_under(&store, &pending_request, &stale_session_cutoff),
        CodeApproval::Issued(issued_code) if issued_code.sid == standing.sid
    ));
}
}

pub(crate) fn approve_for_device(
    &mut self,

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn approve_for_device_records_scopes_and_name_only_while_pending() {
    let store = FakeGrantStore::default();
    let read = device_request("dev-1", "CODE", RequestStatus::Pending);
    store.tx().insert_device_request(&read).unwrap();
    let mut tx = store.tx();
    let mut approver = RequestApprover::within(&mut tx);
    let scopes = delegated_scopes(&["patient/Patient.r"]);
    let now = Utc::now();
    assert!(approver
        .approve_for_device(&scopes, &read, None, Some("Kitchen iPad"), now)
        .unwrap());
    let AuthorizationRequest::Device(request) = stored(&store, "dev-1") else {
        panic!("a device request");
    };
    assert_eq!(request.state.status(), RequestStatus::Approved);
    assert!(matches!(request.state, PolledState::Approved(_)));
    assert_eq!(request.device_name.as_deref(), Some("Kitchen iPad"));
    assert!(
        !approver
            .approve_for_device(&scopes, &read, None, None, now)
            .unwrap(),
        "an already-approved request is not approved twice"
    );
}
}

Grant Recorder

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/writers/grant_recorder.rs

When the Owner approves an app, the approval leaves a standing grant behind, so the app’s next request for the same access goes through without asking. The grant recorder writes it: it creates the grant, or widens the one already standing. For an app trusted on first use it also writes the app’s registration, which the approval is what justifies.

Both writes take delegated scopes. A grant row and a widened registration only ever carry scopes an approver was entitled to delegate, and a scope the Owner unticked is added to neither. The proof also says whether to write the registration at all (would_write_registration).

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/writers/grant_recorder.rs lines 30–32 · authorization-server in the code index

record_code_grant

One grant per app and redirect: a re-approval widens the grant that stands, never adds a second. The widening is the grant’s own absorb_reapproval.

Register (or widen) the client and insert or cumulatively update the standing authorization-code grant for (client_id, redirect_uri), in the caller’s write scope: write the clients row when the proof writes the registration, then read the standing grant — if present, fold the re-approval in via CumulativeConsent::absorb_reapproval and write it back; otherwise mint a fresh grant. The scope holds the write lock from before the read, so two concurrent approvals serialise at the read rather than both reading the pre-merge row and one losing its scope union, and the registration lands with the grant it justifies or not at all.

For a client trusted on first use the clients row, as read inside the transaction, is created when absent, otherwise widened in place, and the approved redirect joins its allowlist exactly when the row doesn’t already allow it. The proof’s approver held both wildflower/Client.c and wildflower/Client.u, so whichever the row calls for is covered. A fixed registration, which an approval never writes, gets no clients row at all.

The grant (and any widened registration) records exactly the proof’s scopes, so a scope the approver pruned is never added to either.

Errors

AuthorizationServerError::Infrastructure on a store failure, which rolls the caller’s scope back.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) fn record_code_grant(
    &mut self,
    client_id: &str,
    redirect_uri: &Url,
    delegated_scopes: &DelegatedScopes,
    patient: Option<&str>,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<(), AuthorizationServerError> {
    let delegated = delegated_scopes.scopes();
    if delegated_scopes.would_write_registration() {
        write_registration(self.tx, client_id, redirect_uri, delegated, now)?;
    }
    match self
        .tx
        .grant_by_client_and_redirect(client_id, redirect_uri)?
    {
        Some(mut grant) => {
            grant.absorb_reapproval(delegated, patient, now);
            self.tx.update_authorization_code_grant(&grant)
        }
        None => self
            .tx
            .create_authorization_code_grant(&AuthorizationCodeGrant {
                id: Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
                client_id: client_id.to_owned(),
                scopes: delegated.to_vec(),
                granted_at: now,
                last_used_at: None,
                patient: patient.map(str::to_owned),
                redirect_uri: redirect_uri.clone(),
            }),
    }
}
}

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn record_code_grant_inserts_then_unions_scopes() {
    let store = FakeGrantStore::default();
    let mut tx = store.tx();
    let mut recorder = GrantRecorder::within(&mut tx);
    recorder
        .record_code_grant(
            "client-a",
            &redirect(),
            &delegated_scopes(&["patient/Patient.r"]),
            Some("pat-1"),
            Utc::now(),
        )
        .unwrap();
    let first = store
        .tx()
        .grant_by_client_and_redirect("client-a", &redirect())
        .unwrap()
        .expect("grant inserted");
    assert_eq!(first.scopes, ["patient/Patient.r"]);

    recorder
        .record_code_grant(
            "client-a",
            &redirect(),
            &delegated_scopes(&["patient/Patient.r", "patient/Observation.r"]),
            Some("pat-2"),
            Utc::now(),
        )
        .unwrap();
    let merged = store
        .tx()
        .grant_by_client_and_redirect("client-a", &redirect())
        .unwrap()
        .expect("grant present");
    assert_eq!(
        merged.id, first.id,
        "the same grant is updated, not duplicated"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        merged.scopes,
        ["patient/Patient.r", "patient/Observation.r"]
    );
    assert_eq!(merged.patient.as_deref(), Some("pat-2"));

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) fn record_device_grant(
    &mut self,
    client_id: &str,
    device_name: &str,
    delegated_scopes: &DelegatedScopes,
    patient: Option<&str>,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<(), AuthorizationServerError> {
    let delegated = delegated_scopes.scopes();
    match self
        .tx
        .device_grant_by_client_and_device_name(client_id, device_name)?
    {
        Some(mut grant) => {
            grant.absorb_reapproval(delegated, patient, now);
            self.tx.update_device_grant(&grant)
        }
        None => self.tx.create_device_grant(&DeviceGrant {
            id: Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
            client_id: client_id.to_owned(),
            scopes: delegated.to_vec(),
            granted_at: now,
            last_used_at: None,
            patient: patient.map(str::to_owned),
            device_name: device_name.to_owned(),
        }),
    }
}
}

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn a_new_grant_starts_unused_and_a_reapproval_keeps_its_last_use() {
    let store = FakeGrantStore::default();
    let record = || {
        let mut tx = store.tx();
        let mut recorder = GrantRecorder::within(&mut tx);
        recorder
            .record_code_grant(
                "client-a",
                &redirect(),
                &delegated_scopes(&["openid"]),
                None,
                Utc::now(),
            )
            .unwrap();
        recorder
            .record_device_grant(
                "client-a",
                "Kitchen iPad",
                &delegated_scopes(&["openid"]),
                None,
                Utc::now(),
            )
            .unwrap();
    };
    let code_grant = || {
        store
            .tx()
            .grant_by_client_and_redirect("client-a", &redirect())
            .unwrap()
            .expect("code grant")
    };
    let device_grant = || {
        store
            .tx()
            .device_grant_by_client_and_device_name("client-a", "Kitchen iPad")
            .unwrap()
            .expect("device grant")
    };

    record();
    assert_eq!(code_grant().last_used_at, None);
    assert_eq!(device_grant().last_used_at, None);

    let used_at = Utc::now();
    store
        .tx()
        .stamp_authorization_code_grant_used(&code_grant().id, used_at)
        .unwrap();
    store
        .tx()
        .stamp_device_grant_used(&device_grant().id, used_at)
        .unwrap();
    record();
    assert_eq!(code_grant().last_used_at, Some(used_at));
    assert_eq!(device_grant().last_used_at, Some(used_at));
}
}

write_registration

The store’s upsert updates the row in place, keeping its registration time and any disabled_at, so a widening never brings a disabled app back.

Create the clients row for client_id, or widen the existing one, by the delegated scopes and (when the row doesn’t allow it yet) the redirect — inside the caller’s transaction, after reading the row under its write lock, so the write follows the row as it stands, not as an earlier read saw it. The store’s upsert keeps the row’s registration time and disabled_at, so a widening never brings a disabled client back.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn write_registration<T: GrantTx>(
    tx: &mut T,
    client_id: &str,
    redirect_uri: &Url,
    delegated: &[String],
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<(), AuthorizationServerError> {
    let row = match tx.client_by_id(client_id)? {
        Some(existing_client) => {
            let adds_redirect = !existing_client.allows_redirect_uri(redirect_uri);
            widen_registration(existing_client, redirect_uri, delegated, adds_redirect)
        }
        None => new_registration(client_id, redirect_uri, delegated, now),
    };
    // `upsert_client` updates in place, preserving `registered_at` and any admin
    // `disabled_at` — a widening never resurrects a disabled client.
    tx.upsert_client(&row)
}
}

new_registration

The clients row a first approval of an unregistered client creates: a public client named after its own client_id (there is no registrar to have supplied a display name), holding only the redirect it just used and the scopes the approver actually granted.

The scopes go in collapsed, through the same widened_scopes the widening path uses (against an empty registration), so a row created by a first approval and a row widened into the same state are byte-identical — the approval order can’t leave two clients with differently-spelled but equivalent ceilings.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn new_registration(
    client_id: &str,
    redirect_uri: &Url,
    granted_scopes: &[String],
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Client {
    Client {
        client_id: client_id.to_owned(),
        name: client_id.to_owned(),
        kind: ClientKind::Public,
        redirect_uris: vec![redirect_uri.clone()],
        allowed_scopes: widened_scopes(&[], granted_scopes),
        allowed_grant_types: AllowedGrantType::ALL.to_vec(),
        secret_hash: None,
        registered_at: now,
        disabled_at: None,
        registration_source: RegistrationSource::TrustedOnFirstUse,
    }
}
}

widen_registration

The scopes widen by meaning, through widened_scopes, and the row is only ever read by coverage, as in PresentedClientChange, so a collapsed row admits exactly what the uncollapsed one would.

Widen an existing registration by what the approver just approved: append the redirect_uri as an absolute entry when it resolved to none of the existing ones, and widen allowed_scopes by the granted scopes. Everything else on the row (its name, kind, secret, registration time) is left exactly as it was.

The scope half is wildflowerhealthio_scopes::widened_scopes, not a string union: the granted scopes are parsed, so an approval that grants patient/Patient.cruds replaces a registered patient/Patient.r instead of leaving the row carrying both, and granting again what the row already covers leaves it untouched. allowed_scopes is only ever read through wildflowerhealthio_scopes::allowed_scope_covers (at /authorize, at /device_authorization, and in PresentedClientChange::from_presented_registration), so a collapsed row admits exactly the requests the un-collapsed one did.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn widen_registration(
    mut client: Client,
    redirect_uri: &Url,
    granted_scopes: &[String],
    adds_redirect: bool,
) -> Client {
    if adds_redirect {
        client.redirect_uris.push(redirect_uri.clone());
    }
    client.allowed_scopes = widened_scopes(&client.allowed_scopes, granted_scopes);
    client
}
}

Refresh Family Writer

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/writers/refresh_family_writer.rs

A refresh token is a standing credential: with it, an app gets fresh access tokens long after the person who approved it has left. Refresh tokens come in families. A family starts with one token when a grant is redeemed, and each refresh consumes the token presented and adds its successor, so one token in a family is live at a time. The family holds what every token in it is good for: the app, the scopes, the patient, the deadline.

The refresh-family writer starts families and rotates tokens. Both take a redemption proof: a GrantRedemption to start a family, so a refresh token is only ever minted for scopes a consumed code or a claimed device request recorded; a ValidatedRefreshToken to rotate one, so a token is only ever rotated within a family that validated for the app presenting it.

A rotation is also a use. An app refreshing is its browser session in use, so the session’s last_seen_at moves, and a device refreshing is its pairing in use, so the device grant that earned the family is stamped used. A code grant isn’t stamped on a refresh: it is used when it stands in for the Owner at /oauth/authorize, which the request approver stamps.

domain::capabilities::writers::refresh_family_writer

The rotation tests validate their tokens with the refresh-family fixture, and start from a redeemed code built by the test fake’s redeemed_code.

start_family

A family comes only with offline_access: the token exchange asks the redemption’s is_refresh_token_earned first, and the writer itself doesn’t ask. The family’s deadline is REFRESH_TOKEN_FAMILY_TTL from now, and rotation never extends it.

Mint a new family with its first token and return the token’s plaintext. The caller checks is_refresh_token_earned first. The family records the redemption’s scopes and patient verbatim, the code it consumed (so a replay of that code can revoke the lineage), the standing grant behind it, and the browser session it was made under (so revoking that session ends it).

Errors

AuthorizationServerError::Infrastructure on a store failure.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) fn start_family(
    &mut self,
    redemption: GrantRedemption<'_>,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<String, AuthorizationServerError> {
    let plaintext = generate_refresh_token();
    let family = RefreshTokenFamily {
        family_id: Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
        client_id: redemption.client_id().to_owned(),
        scopes: redemption.granted_scopes().to_vec(),
        patient: redemption.patient().map(str::to_owned),
        issued_at: now,
        expires_at: now + REFRESH_TOKEN_FAMILY_TTL,
        authorization_code_hash: redemption.authorization_code().map(token_storage_hash),
        grant_id: redemption.grant_id().map(str::to_owned),
        sid: redemption.sid().map(str::to_owned),
    };
    let first_token = RefreshToken {
        token_hash: token_storage_hash(&plaintext),
        family_id: family.family_id.clone(),
        issued_at: now,
        consumed_at: None,
    };
    self.tx.insert_refresh_token_family_row(&family)?;
    self.tx.insert_refresh_token(&first_token)?;
    Ok(plaintext)
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/writers/refresh_family_writer.rs lines 156–182 · authorization-server in the code index

rotate

The consume is the single-use claim (consume_refresh_token).

Consume the presented token and, only if that consume won, insert its successor and return the successor’s plaintext. A family made under a browser session moves that session’s last_seen_at to now: an app refreshing is the session in use. A family a device grant earned stamps that grant’s last_used_at with now: a device refreshing is the pairing in use.

A refusal is the inner Err, so the caller’s scope keeps what it wrote: InvalidGrantReason::RefreshTokenReplayed when the token had already been consumed — a leak or a badly broken client, either way an unsafe lineage, so the whole family is expired at now first; and InvalidGrantReason::RefreshTokenVanished when it disappeared between validation and rotation (nothing to revoke).

Errors

AuthorizationServerError::Infrastructure on a store failure.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) fn rotate(
    &mut self,
    validated_refresh_token: &ValidatedRefreshToken,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<Result<String, TokenExchangeError>, AuthorizationServerError> {
    let family_id = validated_refresh_token.family_id();
    match consume_refresh_token(self.tx, validated_refresh_token.presented_hash(), now)? {
        RefreshTokenConsumeOutcome::Consumed => {
            let successor = generate_refresh_token();
            self.tx.insert_refresh_token(&RefreshToken {
                token_hash: token_storage_hash(&successor),
                family_id: family_id.to_owned(),
                issued_at: now,
                consumed_at: None,
            })?;
            if let Some(sid) = validated_refresh_token.sid() {
                self.tx.touch_browser_session_last_seen(sid, now, now)?;
            }
            if let Some(grant_id) = validated_refresh_token.device_grant_id() {
                self.tx.stamp_device_grant_used(grant_id, now)?;
            }
            Ok(Ok(successor))
        }
        RefreshTokenConsumeOutcome::Replayed => {
            self.tx.expire_refresh_token_family(family_id, now)?;
            Ok(Err(TokenExchangeError::InvalidGrant(
                InvalidGrantReason::RefreshTokenReplayed {
                    family_id: family_id.to_owned(),
                    client_id: validated_refresh_token.client_id().to_owned(),
                },
            )))
        }
        RefreshTokenConsumeOutcome::NotFound => Ok(Err(TokenExchangeError::InvalidGrant(
            InvalidGrantReason::RefreshTokenVanished {
                family_id: family_id.to_owned(),
            },
        ))),
    }
}
}

    let redeemed_code = redeemed_code(&store, "client", &["offline_access"]);
    let first = writer
        .start_family(GrantRedemption::AuthorizationCode(&redeemed_code), now)
        .unwrap();
    let presented = validated(&store, &first);

    let successor = writer
        .rotate(&presented, now)
        .unwrap()
        .expect("first rotation rotates");
    assert!(store
        .tx()
        .refresh_token_with_family_by_hash(&token_storage_hash(&successor))
        .unwrap()
        .is_some());

    assert!(matches!(
        writer.rotate(&presented, now).unwrap(),
        Err(TokenExchangeError::InvalidGrant(
            InvalidGrantReason::RefreshTokenReplayed { .. }
        ))
    ));
    let (_, family) = store
        .tx()
        .refresh_token_with_family_by_hash(&token_storage_hash(&successor))
        .unwrap()
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(family.expires_at, now, "the whole family is expired");
}
}

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn rotate_marks_the_family_s_browser_session_seen() {
    use crate::domain::browser_session::BrowserSession;

    let store = FakeGrantStore::default();
    let mut tx = store.tx();
    let mut writer = RefreshFamilyWriter::within(&mut tx);
    let signed_in_at = Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::hours(1);
    let session = BrowserSession::new_same_device_session(
        vec![],
        chrono::Duration::hours(8),
        signed_in_at,
    );
    store.tx().insert_browser_session(&session).unwrap();
    for (family_id, sid) in [("under-session", Some(&session.sid)), ("no-session", None)] {
        store
            .tx()
            .insert_refresh_token_family_row(&RefreshTokenFamily {
                family_id: family_id.to_owned(),
                client_id: "client".to_owned(),
                scopes: vec!["offline_access".to_owned()],
                patient: None,
                issued_at: signed_in_at,
                expires_at: signed_in_at + REFRESH_TOKEN_FAMILY_TTL,
                authorization_code_hash: None,
                grant_id: None,
                sid: sid.cloned(),
            })
            .unwrap();
        store
            .tx()
            .insert_refresh_token(&RefreshToken {
                token_hash: token_storage_hash(family_id),
                family_id: family_id.to_owned(),
                issued_at: signed_in_at,
                consumed_at: None,
            })
            .unwrap();
    }
    let last_seen = || {
        store
            .tx()
            .browser_session_by_sid(&session.sid)
            .unwrap()
            .unwrap()
            .last_seen_at
    };

    let rotated_at = Utc::now();
    writer
        .rotate(&validated(&store, "no-session"), rotated_at)
        .unwrap()
        .expect("rotates");
    assert_eq!(
        last_seen(),
        signed_in_at,
        "a family with no session touches none"
    );

    writer
        .rotate(&validated(&store, "under-session"), rotated_at)
        .unwrap()
        .expect("rotates");
    assert_eq!(last_seen(), rotated_at);
}
}

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn rotate_stamps_the_device_grant_that_earned_the_family() {
    use crate::domain::grant::{DeviceGrant, Grant};

    let store = FakeGrantStore::default();
    let issued_at = Utc::now() - chrono::Duration::hours(1);
    store
        .tx()
        .create_device_grant(&DeviceGrant {
            id: "device-grant".to_owned(),
            client_id: "client".to_owned(),
            scopes: vec!["offline_access".to_owned()],
            granted_at: issued_at,
            last_used_at: None,
            patient: None,
            device_name: "Reception iPad".to_owned(),
        })
        .unwrap();
    store
        .tx()
        .create_authorization_code_grant(&code_grant("code-grant", "client"))
        .unwrap();
    for (family_id, grant_id, authorization_code_hash) in [
        ("device-family", "device-grant", None),
        (
            "code-family",
            "code-grant",
            Some(token_storage_hash("code")),
        ),
    ] {
        store
            .tx()
            .insert_refresh_token_family_row(&RefreshTokenFamily {
                family_id: family_id.to_owned(),
                client_id: "client".to_owned(),
                scopes: vec!["offline_access".to_owned()],
                patient: None,
                issued_at,
                expires_at: issued_at + REFRESH_TOKEN_FAMILY_TTL,
                authorization_code_hash,
                grant_id: Some(grant_id.to_owned()),
                sid: None,
            })
            .unwrap();
        store
            .tx()
            .insert_refresh_token(&RefreshToken {
                token_hash: token_storage_hash(family_id),
                family_id: family_id.to_owned(),
                issued_at,
                consumed_at: None,
            })
            .unwrap();
    }
    let last_used_at = |id: &str| match store.tx().grant_by_id(id).unwrap() {
        Some(Grant::AuthorizationCode(grant)) => grant.last_used_at,
        Some(Grant::DeviceCode(grant)) => grant.last_used_at,
        None => panic!("grant {id} present"),
    };

    let rotated_at = Utc::now();
    for family_id in ["device-family", "code-family"] {
        RefreshFamilyWriter::within(&mut store.tx())
            .rotate(&validated(&store, family_id), rotated_at)
            .unwrap()
            .expect("rotates");
    }
    assert_eq!(last_used_at("device-grant"), Some(rotated_at));
    assert_eq!(last_used_at("code-grant"), None);
}
}

Access Token Minter

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/writers/access_token_minter.rs

Every access token the server hands out is signed here: an app’s at /oauth/token, a same-device session’s at sign-in, a paired browser’s when its pairing is claimed. What a token claims comes from a token entitlement, never from a list a caller put together, so what a token can be minted for is that enum’s closed set of variants. The lifetime is the caller’s: an app’s ACCESS_TOKEN_TTL, or the lifetime of the browser session the token is minted for.

Mint access tokens for one server with the signing key that was active when the minter was loaded; the gate is the TokenEntitlement proof mint takes. Loaded and used inside the caller’s scope: reading the key’s private material is the privileged read, and signing is pure computation over it, so a signing failure rolls the scope back with everything else.

}

Browser Session Writer

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/writers/browser_session_writer.rs

A browser session holds a grant, and the tokens minted under it name it as their sid. Starting one takes the proof that the browser may hold it. There are two ways in: the Owner signs in on the same device with a code the base minted, or a browser the Owner approved claims its pairing. Each has its proof, and the session the writer stores is the one the proof carries, built by the proof’s constructor. The writer adds nothing to it.

In both flows the same write scope then mints the session’s token with the access-token minter, so a session is never stored without its token, nor a token minted for a session that wasn’t stored.

Capabilities

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/mod.rs

A capability is a narrow door from the HTTP layer into the grant store, built for one purpose: list the grants, decide a consent prompt, redeem a code at /oauth/token. A handler holds a capability, never the store, so what it can do to the data is exactly what the capability offers. The door is the gate: whatever unlocks a capability is checked before the handler can hold one, so a handler that forgets a check has no way to reach the data at all.

Capabilities are grouped by what unlocks them:

GroupUnlocked byWho is calling
Accessthe caller’s scopesthe Owner’s UI, or a paired browser, on /authorization
OAuththe client, through the authenticated client proof, or nothing at allan app, a device, or a browser on its way through /oauth
Sessionthe caller’s own credential: a verified token, or the browser’s own cookieanyone signed in, acting on themselves
Writersan authority proofthe other capabilities, inside their own store scope

The writers have their own part, before this one, because every other capability composes them rather than calling the store’s privileged writes directly.

The one shape

Every public method of a capability opens one store scope at its top, runs the flow inside it to an outcome, and acts on the outcome once the scope has closed. An operation that only reads opens a read scope; one that writes opens a write scope. The proofs and writers beneath take the scope’s transaction, never the store, so everything one operation writes lands together or not at all. What can’t sit inside the scope runs after it: republishing the Owner prompt to the host, writing to the revocation store.

An error rolls the scope back. So a refusal that must keep what it wrote is an outcome, not an error: a spent code, a stamped poll, a request denied for a reason the app is told. The scope commits it, and the caller reads the outcome. The consent approval shows the pattern plainly: an approval that grants nothing ends as a committed ConsentOutcome::Denied, while an approver short of a scope gets an error and nothing is written.

Every capability is generic over the GrantStore port and holds the handles it needs, lifted from the router state when it is built, never the state itself, which keeps its logic unit-testable against the in-memory test fake. The bindings that name the SQLite store and build each capability from the state are in the Assembly part, so nothing here depends on an adapter or on HTTP.

The helpers the unit tests in this part share are on the Test Fixtures page.

domain::capabilities

source_guards

Two tests make “the capability is the only door” structural. They read the source of the route handlers and the authentication middleware, with comments, string literals and test code blanked out by the source guard helpers, and fail if a file reaches past a capability. The token verifier they name is on the Token Verifier page.

Default-safety guard: every handler file reaches the store only through a capability extractor — Scoped<…> (scope-gated), Authenticated<…> (the caller’s own session), or Live<…> (the pre-auth front door, whose gate is the proof its methods take) — never a raw State<Arc<AuthorizationServerState>> or a state field. This test fails if one appears, so a forgotten gate can’t ship silently. It also fails when it finds fewer handler files than expected, so a moved directory can’t make it pass by scanning nothing.

The routes tree is enumerated at test time, so a NEW handler file is guarded by default; only module glue (mod.rs) is exempt. (Advisory- strength, deliberately: the needles are textual; comments and unit-test modules are skipped.)

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn handlers_reach_the_state_only_through_capabilities() {
    // Raw router state, or any field of it — the only ways to reach data
    // or a seam without a capability.
    const FORBIDDEN: &[&str] = &[
        "State<",
        ".store",
        ".revocation_store",
        ".owner_approval_tx",
        ".pending_consents_recomputed_tx",
        ".server_origin",
        ".owner_grant",
        ".same_device_sign_in_codes",
        ".sign_in_destinations",
    ];

    let routes_dir =
        std::path::Path::new(concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/src/http/routes"));
    let mut checked = 0;
    for path in rs_files_under(routes_dir).expect("enumerate routes_dir") {
        let relative = relative_to(&path, routes_dir).expect("enumerated under routes_dir");
        if relative.ends_with("mod.rs") {
            continue;
        }
        let source = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("read handler source {relative}: {e}"));
        for (n, line) in production_lines(&source) {
            for needle in FORBIDDEN {
                assert!(
                    !line.contains(needle),
                    "handler `{relative}:{n}` reaches the state directly (`{needle}`); \
                     acquire a capability through `Scoped<…>`, `Authenticated<…>`, or \
                     `Live<…>` instead",
                );
            }
        }
        checked += 1;
    }

The authN gates verify a token through the TokenVerifier capability, not against the stores directly: no file under src/http/middleware/ names the store or the revocation store, so the verification policy has exactly one home. Same textual strength, and the same floor on files scanned, as the handler guard.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn middleware_verifies_only_through_the_token_verifier() {
    const FORBIDDEN: &[&str] = &[".store", ".revocation_store"];
    let middleware_dir =
        std::path::Path::new(concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/src/http/middleware"));
    let mut checked = 0;
    for path in rs_files_under(middleware_dir).expect("enumerate middleware_dir") {
        let relative =
            relative_to(&path, middleware_dir).expect("enumerated under middleware_dir");
        let source = std::fs::read_to_string(&path)
            .unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!("read middleware source {relative}: {e}"));
        for (n, line) in production_lines(&source) {
            for needle in FORBIDDEN {
                assert!(
                    !line.contains(needle),
                    "middleware `{relative}:{n}` reaches a store directly (`{needle}`); \
                     verify through `LiveTokenVerifier` instead",
                );
            }
        }
        checked += 1;
    }
    assert!(
        checked >= 3,
        "only {checked} middleware files enumerated — did src/http/middleware move?",
    );
}
}

In this part

  • Access: the scope-gated /authorization surface the Owner’s UI drives: consent prompts, grants, clients, browser sessions, token revocation.
  • OAuth: the /oauth front door: starting an authorization, pairing a browser, signing the Owner in, the device flow, the token endpoint, the JWKS.
  • Session: verifying a token, and what a caller may do with its own credential: read it back, log out, sign out.
  • Test Fixtures: the helpers the part’s unit tests share.

Access

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/access/mod.rs

The /authorization surface is where the server is administered: the Owner’s UI decides a consent prompt, lists the standing grants and revokes one, disables an app, signs a browser out, revokes a token. A paired browser reaches the same surface, holding less. What a caller may do here is exactly what its token’s scopes cover. The scopes are Wildflower resource scopes (wildflower/Grant.r to read the grants, wildflower/Grant.d to revoke one), and the Owner’s token carries wildflower/*.cruds, which covers every one of them.

The Scoped<…> extractor

A handler on this surface takes its capability as Scoped<…>, never the store. The extractor reads the verified claims the bearer gate left on the request, checks that they cover every scope the capability requires, and only then builds the capability. A token short of a scope gets a 403 naming the scopes it lacks, and the handler never runs.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
let required_scopes = F::required_scopes();
// An empty fixed requirement is the same kind of wiring bug: it would
// admit any authenticated caller while looking gated — fail closed.
if F::REQUIRES_SCOPES && required_scopes.is_empty() {
    return Err(InternalError::new(
        "scoped capability",
        "a FixedScopeCapability must require at least one scope; make the \
         capability data-dependent (impl Capability directly, storing the \
         Grant) if its check is per-resource",
    )
    .into_response());
}
let granted = claims.granted();
let missing: Vec<Scope> = required_scopes
    .into_iter()
    .filter(|required| !granted.covers(required))
    .collect();
if missing.is_empty() {
    Ok(Scoped(F::build(state.clone(), granted)))
} else {
    Err(F::Error::from(MissingScopes::uncovered(&missing)).into_response())
}
}

scope-capabilities-rust/src/lib.rs lines 250–271 · scope-capabilities in the code index

The extractor and its traits are shared with other slices, in the scope-capabilities crate. A capability comes in one of two flavours:

  • Fixed-scope: one static scope set gates the whole capability. Most capabilities here are this flavour.
  • Data-dependent: the static gate admits the caller, and the capability keeps the caller’s own grant to check more on each call. The consent reader and decider are this flavour, since approving a request takes scopes that depend on the request (the approval scopes).

Each capability’s file declares its gate as a *_scopes() function, which the capability’s binding enforces:

CapabilityRouteGate
ConsentReaderGET /authorization/oauth-consents/{id}, GET /authorization/devices/{userCode}wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.r, plus the caller’s grant
ConsentRaiserPOST /authorization/oauth-consents/{id}/ask-ownerwildflower/AuthorizationRequest.r
ConsentDeciderPOST …/approve and POST …/deny on both consent routeswildflower/AuthorizationRequest.u, plus the approval scopes per call
GrantsReaderGET /authorization/grants, GET /authorization/grants/{id}wildflower/Grant.r
GrantsRevokerDELETE /authorization/grants/{id}wildflower/Grant.d
ClientsReaderGET /authorization/clientswildflower/Client.r

BrowserSessionsReaderGET /authorization/browser-sessionswildflower/BrowserSession.r
BrowserSessionsRevokerDELETE /authorization/browser-sessions/{sid}wildflower/BrowserSession.d

grantable_admin_scopes

Each scope this surface checks is spelt in exactly one place, its *_scopes() function, and this list reads every one of them, so what a token can be given and what it is checked against can’t drift apart. A misspelt scope would parse as an unknown scope that the Owner’s wildflower/*.cruds can’t cover, locking the Owner out of that route; the second test rules that out.

The admin scopes the /authorization surface enforces, deduplicated in declaration order — the registry mapping capability → required scope. Because it reads the very *_scopes() functions the Capability bindings enforce, what a token can be granted and what it is checked against come from one source. Exported as the intended vocabulary for the consent surfaces; nothing consumes it yet (the tests below pin it until the consent UI does).

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub fn grantable_admin_scopes() -> Vec<Scope> {
    let declared = [
        grants::grants_reader_scopes(),
        grants::grants_revoker_scopes(),
        clients::clients_reader_scopes(),
        clients::clients_disabler_scopes(),
        consents::consent_reader_scopes(),
        consents::consent_decider_scopes(),
        consents::grant_creating_approval_scopes(),
        consents::client_registering_approval_scopes(),
        tokens::token_revoker_scopes(),
        browser_sessions::browser_sessions_reader_scopes(),
        browser_sessions::browser_sessions_revoker_scopes(),
    ];
    let mut seen = HashSet::new();
    declared
        .into_iter()
        .flatten()
        .filter(|scope| seen.insert(scope.clone()))
        .collect()
}
}

Registry-completeness guard: every scope a capability checks is declared by one *_scopes() function (a capability’s gate, or a per-call requirement such as the consent approval scopes), and grantable_admin_scopes’s declared array must list all of them. A scope checked without registering is one the grantable vocabulary never offers — a silent lock-out. Counting the scope functions textually keeps honest additions honest.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn every_capability_scope_fn_is_registered_in_the_grantable_vocabulary() {
    const CAPABILITY_SOURCES: &[&str] = &[
        include_str!("grants.rs"),
        include_str!("clients.rs"),
        include_str!("consents/mod.rs"),
        include_str!("tokens.rs"),
        include_str!("browser_sessions.rs"),
    ];
    let scope_fns: usize = CAPABILITY_SOURCES
        .iter()
        .map(|source| source.matches("_scopes() -> Vec<Scope>").count())
        .sum();
    // One `declared` entry per scope function. Update BOTH when adding a
    // checked scope: its `*_scopes()` fn and the `declared` array.
    let declared_entries = 11;
    assert_eq!(
        scope_fns, declared_entries,
        "found {scope_fns} capability scope functions but grantable_admin_scopes() declares \
         {declared_entries}; register the new capability in its `declared` array",
    );
}
}

Consents

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/access/consents/mod.rs

A consent prompt is a pending request put to whoever may decide it: the Owner, or a paired browser holding enough. There are two surfaces. The authorization-code prompt (/authorization/oauth-consents/{id}) is an app asking, through a browser, for a code. The device page’s prompt (/authorization/devices/{userCode}) is keyed by the code a device or a browser shows: a device request or a browser pairing. Each surface can be read, approved and denied; a code-flow prompt can also be raised for the Owner.

This page holds what the two surfaces share: the three capabilities, the scopes they take, and the shapes the prompt pages read and send. The methods live with their flow, on OAuth Consents and Device Consents.

Approving a request takes its approval scopes: the power to decide it, and to create what approving it creates. Deciding takes wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.u. A code or device approval records a standing grant, so it also takes wildflower/Grant.c. A code approval for an app trusted on first use writes the app’s registration, so it also takes wildflower/Client.c and wildflower/Client.u. A code approval also takes the resource scopes the request asks for: its approver must be able to approve it as asked. Which of these a request takes depends on the request, so the decider checks them on each call, through the DelegatedScopes proof every approval obtains first. The proof also clamps what the Owner ticked to what the approver holds, so an approval is never recorded wider than its approver’s own authority.

Every decision is followed by a republish of the Owner prompt, once the decision has committed: the decided request is no longer waiting, so the host’s popup moves on.

decide_and_republish

Every decision on both surfaces runs through here.

Run decide in one write scope and, once it has committed a decision, republish the Owner prompt: the decided request is no longer pending.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn decide_and_republish<T>(
    &self,
    decide: impl FnOnce(&mut S::Tx<'_>) -> Result<T, AuthorizationServerError>,
) -> Result<T, AuthorizationServerError> {
    let decided = self.store.write(decide)?;
    self.owner_approval.republish_active();
    Ok(decided)
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/access/consents/mod.rs lines 184–195 · authorization-server in the code index

OAuth Consents

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/access/consents/oauth.rs

An app has sent a browser to /oauth/authorize, and its code request is parked, waiting for a decision. This page is that decision, as the consent card and the Owner’s popup drive it: read the prompt, ask the Owner about it, approve it, deny it. The capabilities are declared on Consents.

Every operation starts by loading the prompt, and then resolves it against the app’s registration as it stands now, through the same ResolvedCodeRequest /oauth/authorize used to park it, so the card can’t disagree with the endpoint. A prompt whose app has been disabled is never read and never approved: reading it is not found, and approving it denies it.

An approval writes through the writers, inside the decider’s one write scope: the request approver issues the code, bounded by the browser session the request was made in, and the grant recorder records the standing grant and, for an app trusted on first use, its registration. So the code, the grant and the registration land together or not at all.

The tests decide through a decider built over the consent fixtures.

domain::capabilities::access::consents::oauth

load_pending_code_request

The code-flow prompt id, pending at now: the Owner can’t read, approve, deny or be asked about a request still waiting on its browser’s limited page. Anything else is not found.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(super) fn load_pending_code_request(
    tx: &mut impl AuthorizationRequestsTx,
    id: &str,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<CodeRequest, AuthorizationServerError> {
    tx.code_request_by_id(id)?
        .filter(|request| request.is_pending_at(now))
        .ok_or_else(|| consent_not_found(id))
}
}

fn load_pending_code_request_accepts_a_live_request_and_refuses_the_rest() {

        .insert_code_request(&code_request(

        .unwrap();

        assert_eq!(

ConsentReader

oauth_consent

Load a pending authorization-code consent prompt for the launcher, with the client’s display name and its presented client change resolved against the current row, and the approval scopes the reader lacks.

Errors

AuthorizationServerError::OAuthConsentNotFound when id names no live code-flow prompt, or its client is disabled; a store failure.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) fn oauth_consent(
    &self,
    id: &str,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<OAuthConsentView, AuthorizationServerError> {
    self.store.read(|tx| {
        let pending_request = load_pending_code_request(tx, id, now)?;
        let resolved = resolve(tx, &pending_request)?;
        if resolved.is_client_disabled() {
            return Err(consent_not_found(id));
        }
        Ok(OAuthConsentView {
            missing_approval_scopes: resolved
                .approvable_scopes()
                .missing_approval_scopes(&self.reader_grant),
            client_name: resolved.client_name().to_owned(),
            presented_client_change: resolved.presented_client_change().clone(),
            pending_request,
        })
    })
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/access/consents/mod.rs lines 1466–1509 · authorization-server in the code index

ConsentRaiser

raise_for_owner

A browser that can read a prompt but not approve it hands it to the Owner. The request’s own raise_for_owner transition is written through the guarded replace, so a request decided meanwhile is not found.

Raise the pending authorization-code prompt id for the Owner and republish the Owner prompt, once may_raise_for_owner admits it: the authorization start limit, as for a request /oauth/authorize raises, so asking the Owner about request after request costs what starting them would have. A prompt not decidable in its requesting browser is already raised: nothing changes and the limit isn’t asked.

Errors

AuthorizationServerError::OAuthConsentNotFound when id names no live code-flow prompt, or its client is disabled (the rule on OwnerPrompt).

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) fn raise_for_owner(
    &self,
    id: &str,
    may_raise_for_owner: impl FnOnce() -> bool,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<OwnerRaising, AuthorizationServerError> {
    let raising = self.store.write(|tx| {
        let pending_request = load_pending_code_request(tx, id, now)?;
        if tx.is_client_disabled(&pending_request.client_id)? {
            return Err(consent_not_found(id));
        }
        if !pending_request.decidable_in_requesting_browser {
            return Ok(OwnerRaising::AlreadyRaised);
        }
        if !may_raise_for_owner() {
            return Ok(OwnerRaising::StartLimited);
        }
        let raised = pending_request
            .raise_for_owner(now)
            .map_err(|_| consent_not_found(id))?;
        if tx.replace_code_request(&pending_request, &raised)? {
            Ok(OwnerRaising::Raised)
        } else {
            Err(consent_not_found(id))
        }
    })?;
    if raising == OwnerRaising::Raised {
        self.owner_approval.republish_active();
    }
    Ok(raising)
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/access/consents/oauth.rs lines 77–107 · authorization-server in the code index

Raising a prompt for the Owner asks the start limit, and once admitted clears what made it decidable in the requesting browser and republishes; it decides nothing. Raising it again spends nothing, and a prompt no longer pending is not found.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn raising_a_prompt_for_the_owner_leaves_it_pending_and_republishes() {
    let store = FakeGrantStore::default();
    let request = CodeRequest::new(
        NewCodeRequestArgs {
            decidable_in_requesting_browser: true,
            ..fixture_code_args("req-1", "client", owned_scopes(&["read"]))
        },
        Utc::now(),
    );
    store.tx().insert_code_request(&request).unwrap();
    store
        .tx()
        .insert_code_request(&code_request(
            "req-2",
            RequestStatus::Denied,
            Utc::now() + Duration::minutes(5),
        ))
        .unwrap();
    let owner_approval = Arc::new(RecordingOwnerApproval::default());
    let raiser = ConsentRaiser::new(store, owner_approval.clone());

    assert_eq!(
        raiser.raise_for_owner("req-1", || false, Utc::now()),
        Ok(OwnerRaising::StartLimited),
    );
    assert!(
        raiser
            .store
            .tx()
            .code_request_by_id("req-1")
            .unwrap()
            .unwrap()
            .decidable_in_requesting_browser,
        "a refused raise leaves the prompt as it was"
    );
    assert_eq!(owner_approval.count(), 0);

    assert_eq!(
        raiser.raise_for_owner("req-1", || true, Utc::now()),
        Ok(OwnerRaising::Raised),
    );
    let raised = raiser
        .store
        .tx()
        .code_request_by_id("req-1")
        .unwrap()
        .unwrap();
    assert!(!raised.decidable_in_requesting_browser);
    assert_eq!(raised.state.status(), RequestStatus::Pending);
    assert_eq!(owner_approval.count(), 1);
    assert_eq!(
        raiser.raise_for_owner(
            "req-1",
            || panic!("an already-raised prompt spends nothing"),
            Utc::now()
        ),
        Ok(OwnerRaising::AlreadyRaised),
    );

    assert_eq!(
        raiser.raise_for_owner("req-2", || true, Utc::now()),
        Err(AuthorizationServerError::OAuthConsentNotFound {
            id: "req-2".to_owned()
        }),
    );
}
}

ConsentDecider

approve_oauth_consent

Approve the authorization-code consent prompt id: clamp the Owner’s ticks into a DelegatedScopes proof (which requires the approver’s approval scopes), issue the code, record the standing grant and, for a client trusted on first use, its registration, all in one write scope, so the code, the grant and the registration land together or not at all; once it commits, republish the Owner prompt and return the client callback URL. An approval that grants nothing is applied as a deny, and so is one for a request whose browser session has ended or whose client was disabled since it was made.

Errors

Each refusal writes nothing. InsufficientScope names the approval scopes the approver lacks (see ApprovableScopes::missing_approval_scopes); RegistrationNotAcknowledged when the presented client change finds the request new or changed and the Owner didn’t acknowledge it; LaunchPatientMismatch when the request’s SMART launch bound another patient; OAuthConsentNotFound when id names no live code-flow prompt.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) fn approve_oauth_consent(
    &self,
    id: &str,
    input: ApproveOAuthConsentInput,
    generate_code: impl FnOnce() -> String,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<ConsentOutcome, AuthorizationServerError> {
    self.decide_and_republish(|tx| self.approve_oauth_in(tx, id, input, generate_code, now))
}
}

The approval lands:

An approval of a registered client’s request issues its code, records the standing grant, returns the callback carrying the code and the client’s state, and republishes the Owner prompt.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn approve_oauth_consent_mints_a_code_and_returns_the_redirect() {
    let (store, owner_approval) = live_code_store();
    let outcome = approve_code(
        &store,
        &owner_approval,
        "req-1",
        approved(&["read"]),
        &owner_grant(),
        || "the-code".to_owned(),
    )
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        outcome,
        ConsentOutcome::Approved {
            redirect: Some("https://example.com/cb?code=the-code&state=state".to_owned()),
        },
    );
    assert!(store
        .tx()
        .authorization_code_by_request_id("req-1")
        .unwrap()
        .is_some());
    assert!(store
        .tx()
        .grant_by_client_and_redirect(
            "client",
            &url::Url::parse("https://example.com/cb").unwrap(),
        )
        .unwrap()
        .is_some());
    // The approval moved this request out of `pending`, so the Owner prompt
    // has to be recomputed: the prompt spans every flow, so a code-flow
    // approval may change it as much as a device one.
    assert_eq!(owner_approval.count(), 1);
}
}

        ] {
            let store = FakeGrantStore::default();
            let owner_approval = Arc::new(RecordingOwnerApproval::default());
            if let Some(registered_client) = maybe_registered_client {
                store.tx().upsert_client(registered_client).unwrap();
            }
            let request = code_request_for("req-1", "client", owned_scopes(requested_scopes));
            store.tx().insert_code_request(&request).unwrap();

            let result = approve_code(
                &store,
                &owner_approval,
                "req-1",
                approved(requested_scopes),
                &Grant::parse([
                    "wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.u",
                    "wildflower/Grant.c",
                    client_scope,
                ]),
                || panic!("must not mint a code without the power to write the client"),
            );
            assert_eq!(
                result,
                Err(AuthorizationServerError::InsufficientScope {
                    missing_scopes: vec![missing.to_owned()],
                }),
                "{maybe_registered_client:?} {requested_scopes:?} {client_scope}",
            );
            assert_eq!(
                store.tx().client_by_id("client").unwrap().as_ref(),
                maybe_registered_client,
            );
        }
    }
}
}
