authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/access/consents/mod.rs lines 900–916 · authorization-server in the code index

approve_oauth_in

approve_oauth_consent’s flow, inside its write scope tx. The checks run in order: a disabled client’s prompt is denied; the DelegatedScopes proof comes first after that, so an approver lacking an approval scope is refused before anything else; then the acknowledgement of a registration change; then the launch’s patient. Each refusal is an error that writes nothing, and only then does a clamp that left nothing become a deny.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn approve_oauth_in(
    &self,
    tx: &mut impl GrantTx,
    id: &str,
    input: ApproveOAuthConsentInput,
    generate_code: impl FnOnce() -> String,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<ConsentOutcome, AuthorizationServerError> {
    let pending_request = load_pending_code_request(tx, id, now)?;
    let requested_redirect_uri = &pending_request.redirect_uri;
    let resolved = resolve(tx, &pending_request)?;
    // The client was disabled since the request was made: it can't be
    // approved, so it ends here, and the app hears why.
    if resolved.is_client_disabled() {
        deny_pending_request(tx, &pending_request, now, id)?;
        return Ok(denial_outcome(
            &pending_request,
            AuthorizeRefusal::DisabledClient.description(),
        ));
    }
    // The proof every write below demands: the approver holds this prompt's
    // approval scopes, and the Owner's approval is clamped to what this
    // prompt may grant and covered by the approver's own grant. Taken
    // first, so an approver lacking an approval scope is refused before
    // anything else.
    let maybe_delegated_scopes = DelegatedScopes::clamp(
        &self.approver_grant,
        input.owner_approved_scopes,
        resolved.approvable_scopes(),
    )?;
    if resolved
        .presented_client_change()
        .would_change_registration()
        && !input.acknowledged_registration_change
    {
        return Err(AuthorizationServerError::RegistrationNotAcknowledged {
            id: id.to_owned(),
        });
    }
    if !pending_request.admits_patient(input.patient.as_deref()) {
        return Err(AuthorizationServerError::LaunchPatientMismatch { id: id.to_owned() });
    }
    let Some(delegated_scopes) = maybe_delegated_scopes else {
        deny_pending_request(tx, &pending_request, now, id)?;
        return Ok(denial_outcome(
            &pending_request,
            REQUEST_DECLINED_DESCRIPTION,
        ));
    };

    let issued_code = match RequestApprover::within(tx).approve_for_code(
        CodeAuthority::OwnerDelegated(&delegated_scopes),
        &pending_request,
        input.patient.as_deref(),
        generate_code(),
        &self.stale_session_cutoff,
        now,
    )? {
        CodeApproval::Issued(issued_code) => issued_code,
        CodeApproval::RequestNotPending => return Err(consent_not_found(id)),
        // The approver denied the request instead: tell the client so.
        CodeApproval::BrowserSessionEnded => {
            return Ok(denial_outcome(
                &pending_request,
                BROWSER_SIGNED_OUT_DESCRIPTION,
            ));
        }
    };
    GrantRecorder::within(tx).record_code_grant(
        &pending_request.client_id,
        requested_redirect_uri,
        &delegated_scopes,
        input.patient.as_deref(),
        now,
    )?;
    Ok(ConsentOutcome::Approved {
        redirect: Some(build_client_redirect_url(
            requested_redirect_uri,
            &issued_code.code,
            &pending_request.client_state,
        )),
    })
}
}

deny_pending_request

The deny is the request’s own deny transition, written through the guarded replace.

Deny the prompt id, pending_request as read, at now, in the caller’s write scope tx — the shared tail of every deny path (an explicit deny, an approval that grants nothing, and one for a client disabled since).

The deny lands only on a request still pending: when another surface decided it first (or it expired) since it was read, nothing changes and the prompt is not found, as an approval that loses the same race is.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn deny_pending_request(
    tx: &mut impl AuthorizationRequestsTx,
    pending_request: &CodeRequest,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
    id: &str,
) -> Result<(), AuthorizationServerError> {
    let denied = pending_request
        .deny(now)
        .map_err(|_| consent_not_found(id))?;
    if tx.replace_code_request(pending_request, &denied)? {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(consent_not_found(id))
    }
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/access/consents/oauth.rs lines 319–328 · authorization-server in the code index

Device Consents

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/access/consents/device.rs

The device page is where a code shown somewhere else gets decided. A device (a watch, a TV) shows a user code from the device flow; a browser that isn’t the Owner’s shows one from a browser pairing. Both are polled requests, keyed by their user_code. The approver opens /authorization/devices/{userCode}, sees what is asked, and approves or denies. The capabilities are declared on Consents.

Device consent is expandable: the approver may grant more than the device asked for, up to an envelope. For a device the envelope is the app’s registered scopes; for a browser pairing it is the Owner’s scopes, so no paired browser can hold more than a same-device session. Either way the DelegatedScopes clamp also bounds every resource scope by what the approver holds.

A device approval records a standing device grant, keyed by the app and the device’s name, through the grant recorder. A pairing records no grant: the pairing page’s poll starts the paired session once the request is approved. Neither approval has a callback to send a browser to; the device or the pairing page learns the decision by polling.

The tests decide through the consent fixtures.

domain::capabilities::access::consents::device

fn load_pending_request_by_user_code(

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/access/consents/device.rs lines 212–220 · authorization-server in the code index

ConsentReader

device_consent

Load a pending device-page consent prompt for the launcher, with the client’s name and expansion envelope resolved, and the approval scopes the reader lacks.

Errors

AuthorizationServerError::DeviceConsentNotFound when user_code names no live device-page prompt; a store failure.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) fn device_consent(
    &self,
    user_code: &str,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<DeviceConsentView, AuthorizationServerError> {
    let (request, maybe_existing_client) = self.store.read(|tx| {
        let request = load_pending_request_by_user_code(tx, user_code, now)?;
        let maybe_existing_client = tx.client_by_id(request.client_id())?;
        Ok::<_, AuthorizationServerError>((request, maybe_existing_client))
    })?;
    let (client_name, registered_client_scopes) = match maybe_existing_client {
        Some(existing_client) => (existing_client.name, existing_client.allowed_scopes),
        None => (request.client_id().to_owned(), Vec::new()),
    };
    let (approvable, starting_scopes, approvable_scopes) = match &request {
        PolledRequest::Pairing(_) => {
            let approvable = ApprovableScopes::for_browser_pairing();
            let starting_scopes = approvable.delegable_scopes(&self.reader_grant);
            (approvable, starting_scopes, crate::owner_scopes())
        }
        PolledRequest::Device(_) => (
            ApprovableScopes::for_device(&registered_client_scopes),
            request.requested_scopes().to_vec(),
            registered_client_scopes,
        ),
    };
    Ok(DeviceConsentView {
        request,
        client_name,
        starting_scopes,
        approvable_scopes,
        missing_approval_scopes: approvable.missing_approval_scopes(&self.reader_grant),
    })
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/access/consents/mod.rs lines 1365–1391 · authorization-server in the code index

ConsentDecider

approve_device_consent

Approve the device-page consent prompt user_code: apply the expandable scope decision (up to the client’s allowed_scopes for a device, up to OWNER_SCOPES for a browser pairing), transition the request, for a device mint (or refresh) the standing device grant, and republish the Owner prompt. An approval that grants nothing is applied as a deny.

Errors

InsufficientScope when the approver lacks the request’s approval scopes (see ApprovableScopes::missing_approval_scopes: wildflower/Grant.c for a device’s standing grant, which a browser pairing doesn’t record), and InsufficientApproverScope for a resource scope beyond the approver’s own authority, both writing nothing; DeviceConsentNotFound when user_code names no live prompt, names a device request whose client has no row (its envelope), or another surface decided it first.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) fn approve_device_consent(
    &self,
    user_code: &str,
    input: ApproveDeviceConsentInput,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<ConsentOutcome, AuthorizationServerError> {
    self.decide_and_republish(|tx| {
        match load_pending_request_by_user_code(tx, user_code, now)? {
            PolledRequest::Pairing(request) => {
                self.approve_browser_pairing_in(tx, user_code, &request, input, now)
            }
            PolledRequest::Device(request) => {
                self.approve_device_in(tx, user_code, &request, input, now)
            }
        }
    })
}
}

approve_device_in

The device’s own transition is DeviceRequest::approve, and the grant is named by device_grant_name.

Approve the pending device request request, inside the approval’s write scope tx.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn approve_device_in(
    &self,
    tx: &mut impl GrantTx,
    user_code: &str,
    request: &DeviceRequest,
    input: ApproveDeviceConsentInput,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<ConsentOutcome, AuthorizationServerError> {
    let client = tx
        .client_by_id(&request.client_id)?
        .ok_or_else(|| consent_not_found(user_code))?;
    // The proof every write below demands: the approver holds a device
    // prompt's approval scopes, and the Owner's approval is clamped to what
    // it may grant and covered by the approver's own grant.
    let Some(delegated_scopes) = DelegatedScopes::clamp(
        &self.approver_grant,
        input.owner_approved_scopes,
        &ApprovableScopes::for_device(&client.allowed_scopes),
    )?
    else {
        deny_device_request(tx, request, user_code, now)?;
        return Ok(ConsentOutcome::Denied { redirect: None });
    };
    if !RequestApprover::within(tx).approve_for_device(
        &delegated_scopes,
        request,
        input.patient.as_deref(),
        input.device_name.as_deref(),
        now,
    )? {
        return Err(consent_not_found(user_code));
    }
    let request_device_name = input
        .device_name
        .as_deref()
        .or(request.device_name.as_deref());
    let grant_name = device_grant_name(request_device_name, &client.name);
    GrantRecorder::within(tx).record_device_grant(
        &request.client_id,
        grant_name,
        &delegated_scopes,
        input.patient.as_deref(),
        now,
    )?;
    Ok(ConsentOutcome::Approved { redirect: None })
}
}

Deny the device request request, as read, at now, in the caller’s write scope tx — an explicit deny, or an approval that grants nothing. It lands only on a request still pending: when another surface decided it first (or it expired) since it was read, nothing changes and the prompt user_code is not found, as an approval that loses the same race is.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn deny_device_request(
    tx: &mut impl AuthorizationRequestsTx,
    request: &DeviceRequest,
    user_code: &str,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<(), AuthorizationServerError> {
    let denied = request
        .deny(now)
        .map_err(|_| consent_not_found(user_code))?;
    if tx.replace_device_request(request, &denied)? {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(consent_not_found(user_code))
    }
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/access/consents/device.rs lines 244–258 · authorization-server in the code index

Grants

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/access/grants.rs

The Owner’s list of trusted apps shows every standing grant: what each app, or each device, was allowed, and when it was last used. Revoking a grant ends what was issued under it: the app’s live access tokens and its refresh families die with the consent, so no app holding offline_access outlives its revoked consent.

The access tokens die through the host’s revocation store, which keeps a per-subject epoch outside the grant store: a token issued before its subject’s epoch no longer verifies. A token’s subject is its app’s client_id, so the epoch, and with it the revoke, is per app, not per grant. The revocation store is reached through the Revocation port.

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/access/grants.rs lines 82–84 · authorization-server in the code index

revoke

The tests record the subjects the revocation port is asked to bump, through a recording port.

Revoke the grant id: bump its client’s revocation epoch, killing its live access tokens, then delete the grant and expire the client’s refresh-token families in one write scope, so standing consent and standing credentials die together — the whole cascade, so no offline_access client outlives its revoked consent. Runs under this capability’s own Grant.d gate; the token-kill is part of revoking a grant, so it does not additionally require Token.d.

The one capability with two scopes: a read scope loads the grant for its client, the epoch is bumped, and a write scope deletes. The epoch lives on the revocation store, so its bump can’t sit inside this store’s write lock, and it goes first: a bump that over-revokes on a failed delete is recoverable (a retry finds the grant and finishes), while a delete that commits without its bump leaves live access tokens and a retry that answers 404.

The epoch and the families are per client, not per grant: revoking one of a client’s grants ends every access token and refresh-token family the client holds. Both concrete grant tables are hit (grant ids are UUIDs unique across them, so at most one deletes a row).

Errors

AuthorizationServerError::GrantNotFound when no grant has id, or it vanished between the read and the delete; a store or revocation-store failure.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) fn revoke(
    &self,
    id: &str,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<(), AuthorizationServerError> {
    let grant = self
        .store
        .read(|tx| tx.grant_by_id(id))?
        .ok_or_else(|| grant_not_found(id))?;
    self.revocation
        .revoke_subject_as_of_now(grant.client_id())
        .map_err(|e| {
            AuthorizationServerError::infrastructure("revoke_subject_as_of_now failed", e)
        })?;
    self.store.write(|tx| {
        let removed_code = tx.delete_authorization_code_grant(id)?;
        let removed_device = tx.delete_device_grant(id)?;
        if !(removed_code || removed_device) {
            return Err(grant_not_found(id));
        }
        tx.expire_refresh_token_families_for_client(grant.client_id(), now)
    })
}
}

Revoke kills the grant AND expires the client’s refresh-token families in one go: the family deadline is pulled back and its live token stamped consumed at the revoke instant, so standing consent and standing credentials die together.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn revoke_also_expires_the_clients_refresh_families() {
    use crate::domain::refresh_token::{RefreshToken, RefreshTokenFamily};

    let store = FakeGrantStore::default();
    store
        .tx()
        .create_authorization_code_grant(&code_grant("g1", "client-a"))
        .unwrap();
    store
        .tx()
        .insert_refresh_token_family_row(&RefreshTokenFamily {
            family_id: "fam-1".to_owned(),
            client_id: "client-a".to_owned(),
            scopes: vec!["read".to_owned()],
            patient: None,
            issued_at: Utc::now(),
            expires_at: Utc::now() + chrono::Duration::days(90),
            authorization_code_hash: None,
            grant_id: Some("g1".to_owned()),
            sid: None,
        })
        .unwrap();
    store
        .tx()
        .insert_refresh_token(&RefreshToken {
            token_hash: "live".to_owned(),
            family_id: "fam-1".to_owned(),
            issued_at: Utc::now(),
            consumed_at: None,
        })
        .unwrap();

    let revoked_at = Utc::now();
    let revoker = GrantsRevoker::new(store, Arc::new(SubjectsRevoked::default()));
    revoker.revoke("g1", revoked_at).unwrap();

    assert!(
        revoker.store.tx().grant_by_id("g1").unwrap().is_none(),
        "grant gone"
    );
    let (_token, family) = revoker
        .store
        .tx()
        .refresh_token_with_family_by_hash("live")
        .unwrap()
        .expect("row kept for auditability");
    assert_eq!(family.expires_at, revoked_at);
}
}

Clients

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/access/clients.rs

The Owner’s “Trusted apps” list is every registered client, with a switch to disable each. A disabled app gets nothing: /oauth/authorize and /oauth/token refuse it, and its waiting code requests are neither shown nor approved. Disabling writes one column, disabled_at, so re-enabling brings the app back exactly as it was registered. Disabling and re-enabling both edit the row in place, so both take wildflower/Client.u.

The two essential clients are how the Owner gets in, so an essential app can’t be disabled, and the list offers no switch for it. Re-enabling one is allowed, so an essential app disabled by hand in the database can still be recovered.

set_disabled_at

The tests disable and enable through the disabler fixtures, each disable stamped at a fixed second unless the test says otherwise. The property test runs any sequence of steps over two registered apps and one id never registered.

Set client_id’s disabled_at in one write scope and return the row as stored.

  • Some(stamp) disables the client, stamped stamp. The handler passes the server’s own now whatever time was sent, so a disable can’t be scheduled or backdated. A client that already carries a stamp keeps it, so a repeated disable doesn’t move the time, and a write that would change nothing is skipped.
  • None re-enables the client. Its registration (redirects, scopes, secret) is untouched by the round trip.
Errors

AuthorizationServerError::ClientNotFound when no such client exists. Disabling an essential client is AuthorizationServerError::EssentialClient (see is_essential_client), refused before anything is read. Re-enabling one stays allowed, so an essential client disabled out of band (direct SQL) can still be recovered.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) fn set_disabled_at(
    &self,
    client_id: &str,
    stamp: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
) -> Result<ClientView, AuthorizationServerError> {
    let essential = is_essential_client(client_id);
    if essential && stamp.is_some() {
        return Err(AuthorizationServerError::EssentialClient {
            client_id: client_id.to_owned(),
        });
    }
    let not_found = || AuthorizationServerError::ClientNotFound {
        client_id: client_id.to_owned(),
    };
    // One write scope, so two concurrent disables serialise at the read
    // and the second sees (and keeps) the first one's stamp.
    let client = self.store.write(|tx| {
        let client = tx.client_by_id(client_id)?.ok_or_else(not_found)?;
        let disabled_at = stamp.map(|stamp| client.disabled_at.unwrap_or(stamp));
        if disabled_at == client.disabled_at {
            return Ok(client);
        }
        if tx.set_client_disabled(client_id, disabled_at)? {
            Ok(Client {
                disabled_at,
                ..client
            })
        } else {
            Err(not_found())
        }
    })?;
    Ok(ClientView { client, essential })
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/access/clients.rs lines 299–325 · authorization-server in the code index

Any sequence of disables and enables — each step an index into IDS and the stamp to disable with (None enables) — leaves each client’s disabled_at equal to a simple model: the stamp of the first disable since the last enable, or None. No step touches any other field or creates a row. Each step returns the row as stored; every step naming the unregistered id is ClientNotFound.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn disable_and_enable_match_the_model(
    steps in prop::collection::vec(
        (0..IDS.len(), prop::option::of(0..10_000i64)),
        0..24,
    ),
) {
    let registered = [client(IDS[0], &["openid"]), client(IDS[1], &["patient/*.rs"])];
    let disabler = disabler_with(&registered);
    let mut model: [Option<DateTime<Utc>>; 2] = [None, None];

    for (index, stamp) in steps {
        if let Some(slot) = model.get_mut(index) {
            *slot = stamp.map(|stamp| slot.unwrap_or(at(stamp)));
        }
        let result = disabler.set_disabled_at(IDS[index], stamp.map(at));
        match (registered.get(index), model.get(index)) {
            (Some(row), Some(&disabled_at)) => {
                let expected = ClientView {
                    client: Client { disabled_at, ..row.clone() },
                    essential: false,
                };
                prop_assert_eq!(result, Ok(expected));
            }
            _ => {
                let not_found = AuthorizationServerError::ClientNotFound { client_id: IDS[index].to_owned() };
                prop_assert_eq!(result, Err(not_found));
            }
        }
    }

    for (row, disabled_at) in registered.iter().zip(model) {
        prop_assert_eq!(stored(&disabler, &row.client_id), Client { disabled_at, ..row.clone() });
    }
    prop_assert_eq!(disabler.store.tx().list_clients().unwrap().len(), registered.len());
}
}

The list holds only the live sessions, not a stale same-device session, and marks the caller’s.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn the_list_holds_the_live_sessions_and_marks_the_caller_s() {
    let store = FakeGrantStore::default();
    let now = Utc::now();
    let caller_s = BrowserSession::new_same_device_session(vec![], Duration::hours(8), now);
    let other = BrowserSession::new_same_device_session(
        vec![],
        Duration::hours(8),
        now - Duration::minutes(10),
    );
    let stale = BrowserSession::new_same_device_session(
        vec![],
        Duration::hours(8),
        now - Duration::hours(1),
    );
    let expired = BrowserSession::new_same_device_session(
        vec![],
        Duration::hours(8),
        now - Duration::hours(9),
    );
    let revoked = BrowserSession::new_same_device_session(vec![], Duration::hours(8), now);
    for session in [&caller_s, &other, &stale, &expired, &revoked] {
        store.tx().insert_browser_session(session).unwrap();
    }
    store
        .tx()
        .revoke_browser_session(&revoked.sid, now)
        .unwrap();
    let reader = BrowserSessionsReader::new(
        store,
        Arc::new(StaleSessionCutoff::new(
            now - Duration::minutes(30),
            HashSet::new(),
        )),
    );

    let listed: Vec<(String, bool)> = reader
        .list_live(Some(&caller_s.sid), now)
        .unwrap()
        .into_iter()
        .map(|view| (view.session.sid, view.held_by_caller))
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(
        listed,
        vec![(caller_s.sid.clone(), true), (other.sid.clone(), false)]
    );

    assert!(
        reader
            .list_live(None, now)
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .all(|view| !view.held_by_caller),
        "a caller under no session holds none"
    );
}
}

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/access/tokens.rs

The Owner can revoke an issued token directly: one token by its jti, or every token of a subject at once. Both go to the host’s revocation store, which the token verifier asks last about every access token, and which a refresh asks about its family’s subject too. The capability touches no grant store, only the Revocation port, so it isn’t generic over the store.

The route takes exactly one of the two modes per request. It refuses a body naming neither, both, or a jti without its expiresAt, and an expiresAt already past, since that token is expired anyway.

OAuth

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/oauth/mod.rs

The OAuth capabilities are the server’s front door: the /oauth/* surface an app, a browser or a device reaches before anyone holds a token. The Access capabilities open for a caller whose scopes cover them. Nobody arriving here has scopes yet, so these doors open on something else: the app’s own credentials, the browser session a request was made in, a secret only one page holds, or nothing at all.

Each capability does one job, and holding it lets a handler do nothing else with the store. The /oauth/authorize handler holds a starter that can start and continue a request. It can’t read a grant or mint a token. Inside, each operation opens one store scope and composes the authority proofs and writers beneath it, where the privileged writes live.

What opens the doorWho is at itCapabilities
The clientAn app’s back end or a device, authenticating as its OAuth clientClient Authenticator checks the credentials and yields the proof that Device Authorizer, Token Exchanger and Client Token Revoker take
NobodyA browser at /oauth/authorize, a wait page polling, anyone reading the JWKSCode Authorization Starter, Authorization Status Reader, Public Keys Reader
In-processThe host and the apps slice, launching an appLaunch Contexts mints the SMART launch value; the starter consumes it
A code minted in-processThe Owner’s browser, signing in on the same deviceSame-Device Sign-In redeems it; Same-Device Session Ender ends the session it started once its server’s launch views have closed
The browser sessionThe browser that made a request, on its limited pageSession Shortfall reads and cancels; the starter continues
A pairing codeA browser that isn’t the Owner’s, asking to be pairedBrowser Pairing

“Nobody” doesn’t mean unchecked. The starter answers any browser that holds a browser session, but it only parks a request: a code comes from the Owner’s decision or from a standing grant, never from the request alone. The status reader answers the browser session that made the request, or one holding the scopes to decide any request, so a leaked request id collects nothing.

In this part

  • Launch Contexts: minting SMART launch values, and consuming one once.
  • Code Authorization Starter: /oauth/authorize. Validates an app’s request, parks it, and sends the browser to its limited page, the consent card, the wait page, or straight back to the app with a code.
  • Authorization Status Reader: the wait page’s poll of a parked request.
  • Session Shortfall: the limited page’s read and Cancel, for a request asking more than its browser session holds.
  • Client Authenticator: checking a client’s credentials, yielding the proof the client-gated capabilities take.
  • Device Authorizer: /oauth/device_authorization, parking a device’s request for the Owner.
  • Browser Pairing: giving a browser that isn’t the Owner’s a paired session, once the Owner approves.
  • Same-Device Sign-In: redeeming the one-time code the base mints to sign the Owner’s browser in.
  • Same-Device Session Ender: ending the Owner sessions launches’ codes started, once the server’s last launch view closes.
  • Token Exchanger: /oauth/token, redeeming a code, a device code or a refresh token for tokens.
  • Client Token Revoker: /oauth/revoke, a client ending one of its own tokens.
  • Public Keys Reader: the JWKS, the public halves of the signing keys.

Launch Contexts

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/oauth/launch_contexts.rs

A SMART App Launch hands the app an opaque launch value, and the app echoes it back at /oauth/authorize. The launch context page says what one is: for one app or for a server’s launcher, five minutes to live, spent once. This page is the two ends of its life. Minting happens in-process, when an app is launched; consuming happens inside the /oauth/authorize request that presents it.

The authorization server owns the launch_contexts table, and nothing outside it writes there directly. The apps slice and the base reach it through the public LaunchContextMinter binding, which can only mint. Every mint clears out the launches already expired in the same write scope, so expired launches need no sweeper of their own.

The tests consume a launch as /oauth/authorize does, inside a write scope of the same store.

Persist a fresh launch context nonce for client_id, binding no patient and expiring LAUNCH_CONTEXT_TTL after now, and return it. Contexts already expired at now are pruned in the same scope. The caller generates nonce (a CSPRNG opaque token) so tests can inject a known value.

A minted context is unbound to any patient, expires after the TTL, and is consumed once by its own client.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn a_minted_context_is_consumed_once_by_its_client() {
    let store = FakeGrantStore::default();
    let launch_contexts = LaunchContexts::new(store);
    let now = Utc::now();
    let minted = launch_contexts
        .mint("app", "nonce-1".to_owned(), now)
        .expect("mint");
    assert_eq!(minted.client_id(), Some("app"));
    assert_eq!(minted.patient(), None);
    assert_eq!(minted.expires_at, now + LAUNCH_CONTEXT_TTL);

    assert_eq!(
        consume(&launch_contexts, "nonce-1", "other-app", now).unwrap(),
        Err(LaunchRefusal::ForAnotherApp),
        "another client can't consume it"
    );
    let consumed = consume(&launch_contexts, "nonce-1", "app", now)
        .unwrap()
        .expect("its own client consumes it");
    assert_eq!(consumed.consumed_at, Some(now));
    assert_eq!(
        consume(&launch_contexts, "nonce-1", "app", now).unwrap(),
        Err(LaunchRefusal::AlreadyUsed),
        "a replay is refused"
    );
}
}

fn insert_and_prune_expired(

) -> Result<LaunchContext, AuthorizationServerError> {
    self.store.write(|tx| {
        tx.delete_launch_contexts_expired_by(now)?;
        tx.insert_launch_context(&launch_context)
    })?;

}

Minting prunes the contexts already expired, and keeps live ones.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn minting_prunes_expired_contexts() {
    let store = FakeGrantStore::default();
    let launch_contexts = LaunchContexts::new(store);
    let now = Utc::now();
    launch_contexts
        .mint("app", "old".to_owned(), now - LAUNCH_CONTEXT_TTL)
        .expect("mint old");
    launch_contexts
        .mint("app", "recent".to_owned(), now - Duration::minutes(1))
        .expect("mint recent");
    launch_contexts
        .mint("app", "new".to_owned(), now)
        .expect("mint new");
    assert_eq!(
        launch_contexts
            .store
            .write(|tx| tx.delete_launch_contexts_expired_by(now))
            .unwrap(),
        0,
        "the last mint already pruned the expired context"
    );
    assert!(consume(&launch_contexts, "recent", "app", now)
        .unwrap()
        .is_ok());
    assert_eq!(
        consume(&launch_contexts, "old", "app", now).unwrap(),
        Err(LaunchRefusal::Unknown),
        "a pruned launch reads as unknown"
    );
}
}

consume_launch

Another app’s launch is reported as that before its state, so a wrong app never learns whether the launch was used or has expired. The starter goes further and tells the app another app’s launch as if it were forged.

Consume the launch nonce for client_id at now, in the caller’s write scope tx: the context, now stamped consumed, iff it was minted for client_id or for the server launcher and is unconsumed and unexpired. Otherwise nothing changes, and the LaunchRefusal says why. A context presented by the wrong client therefore stays consumable by its own. /oauth/authorize calls this inside its own write scope, so a request refused after the consume rolls back and leaves the launch unspent.

The consume is one conditional update, so of two racing consumes exactly one wins. Only when it finds nothing is the row read back to classify the refusal, checking in this order: no row is Unknown, another client’s launch is ForAnotherApp (so its state is never told), then AlreadyUsed, then Expired. A launch pruned after expiring is gone, so it reads as unknown.

The outer Result is the store’s; the inner one is the launch’s answer.

Errors

AuthorizationServerError::Infrastructure on a store failure, or when the conditional update refused a row that passes all four checks, which can’t happen.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) fn consume_launch(
    tx: &mut impl LaunchContextsTx,
    nonce: &str,
    client_id: &str,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<Result<LaunchContext, LaunchRefusal>, AuthorizationServerError> {
    if let Some(consumed) = tx.consume_launch_context(nonce, client_id, now)? {
        return Ok(Ok(consumed));
    }
    let refusal = match tx.launch_context_by_nonce(nonce)? {
        None => LaunchRefusal::Unknown,
        Some(stored) if !stored.admits_client(client_id) => LaunchRefusal::ForAnotherApp,
        Some(stored) if stored.consumed_at.is_some() => LaunchRefusal::AlreadyUsed,
        Some(stored) if stored.expires_at <= now => LaunchRefusal::Expired,
        Some(_) => {
            return Err(AuthorizationServerError::infrastructure(
                "consume_launch_context",
                "refused a launch that is admitted, unconsumed and unexpired",
            ))
        }
    };
    Ok(Err(refusal))
}
}

Each refusal is told apart, checking another client’s launch first: its state is never told, and it stays consumable by its own client.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn a_refused_consume_says_why() {
    let store = FakeGrantStore::default();
    let launch_contexts = LaunchContexts::new(store);
    let now = Utc::now();
    let expired_at = now + LAUNCH_CONTEXT_TTL;
    launch_contexts
        .mint("app", "live".to_owned(), now)
        .expect("mint live");
    launch_contexts
        .mint("app", "used".to_owned(), now)
        .expect("mint used");
    consume(&launch_contexts, "used", "app", now)
        .unwrap()
        .expect("consume used");

    for (nonce, client_id, at, refusal) in [
        ("forged", "app", now, LaunchRefusal::Unknown),
        ("live", "other-app", now, LaunchRefusal::ForAnotherApp),
        ("used", "other-app", now, LaunchRefusal::ForAnotherApp),
        (
            "live",
            "other-app",
            expired_at,
            LaunchRefusal::ForAnotherApp,
        ),
        ("used", "app", now, LaunchRefusal::AlreadyUsed),
        ("live", "app", expired_at, LaunchRefusal::Expired),
    ] {
        assert_eq!(
            consume(&launch_contexts, nonce, client_id, at).unwrap(),
            Err(refusal),
            "{nonce} by {client_id}"
        );
    }
    assert!(
        consume(&launch_contexts, "live", "app", now)
            .unwrap()
            .is_ok(),
        "the refusals left the live launch consumable by its own client"
    );
}
}

Code Authorization Starter

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/oauth/code_authorization_starter.rs

The code authorization starter is what /oauth/authorize does once a browser that holds a browser session arrives carrying an app’s request; a browser without one is sent to pair before it gets here. It validates the request, parks it as a code request, and decides where the browser goes next. It also goes on with a request the browser has confirmed on its limited page.

Three questions about the parked request pick the next step:

  1. Does the browser’s session hold everything the request asks for? If not, and the session hasn’t gone on past the limited page for this app before, the request waits on that browser’s limited page, and nothing else is decided until the browser says to go on.
  2. Does a standing grant cover it? When the request makes no change to the app’s registration, a standing grant covers every scope it asks for, and a launch’s patient is the grant’s, the code is issued at once under the grant: the fast path. The Grant page has the whole rule.
  3. Can the browser decide it itself? Otherwise the request waits for a person. A session that may decide consents and holds the request’s approval scopes is sent to the consent card; any other browser goes to the wait page while the request is raised for the Owner.

The starter is public: no scope opens it, because the caller is the browser of whoever opened the app. Its powers are exactly two operations, start and continue_past_session_shortfall, each in one write scope. A request that would bother the Owner, by being raised for the Owner or parked for its limited page, first asks the authorization start limit, which the route hands in.

The tests start requests from the starter fixtures: by default a request whose session holds all the Owner holds, so it falls short of nothing, from a browser that can’t decide consents, and always admitted by the start limit.

pub(crate) struct AuthorizeRequest<'a> {
    /// The OAuth `response_type`; only `code` is accepted.

    /// The PKCE challenge method; only `S256` is accepted.

    /// What the client asks for, space-separated.
    pub(crate) scope: &'a str,

    /// Where the client wants the answer. Until it is registered to the
    /// client, failures render locally rather than go there.
    pub(crate) redirect_uri: &'a str,
    /// The client's `state`, echoed back on every answer that reaches it.
    pub(crate) client_state: &'a str,
    /// The SMART App Launch `launch` value the app was launched with, or
    /// `None` for a plain OAuth request.
    pub(crate) launch: Option<&'a str>,
    /// The SMART App Launch `aud`: the FHIR server the app means to call with
    /// the token, or `None` when the app doesn't declare one.
    pub(crate) aud: Option<&'a str>,
    /// The grant the browser's session token (its cookie) carries: what the
    /// browser can do as a bearer on this server's pages, the consent card
    /// among them. What the session bounds a code to is read from its row

    pub(crate) session_token_grant: &'a Grant,
    /// Whether that browser session can decide consents. The request can be
    /// decided in that browser when it can and
    /// [`session_token_grant`](Self::session_token_grant) also holds the
    /// request's approval scopes (as the consent card and the approval check
    /// them with [`missing_approval_scopes`]); that is recorded on a parked
    /// request.
    ///
    /// [`missing_approval_scopes`]:
    /// crate::domain::authority::ApprovableScopes::missing_approval_scopes
    pub(crate) can_decide_consents: bool,
    /// Whether this start may raise a request for the Owner, asked once, only
    /// when the request is about to be (not decided in the requesting browser,
    /// and not issued on the standing-grant fast path) or about to park for
    /// its browser's limited page. The authorization start limit, deferred to
    /// here for a browser that can decide consents so that the requests it
    /// decides itself spend nothing; `true` for a start the limit already
    /// admitted. It is a closure, not a flag, because only the starter knows
    /// whether the request will bother the Owner.
    pub(crate) may_raise_for_owner: &'a dyn Fn() -> bool,
    /// The browser session the browser making the request holds, recorded on

fn main() {
pub(crate) enum AuthorizationStartError {
    /// No active signing key: the endpoint cannot issue codes, so it refuses up
    /// front rather than parking a request it can never complete.
    NoActiveSigningKey,
    /// A failure on a request whose `redirect_uri` is not trusted, shown as
    /// this server's own page: sending an error to an untrusted redirect
    /// would make the server an open redirector.
    LocalPage(AuthorizeRefusal),
    /// A spec'd error once `redirect_uri` is validated, with the sentence the
    /// redirect carries as its `error_description`. The URL is boxed to keep
    /// the error small enough for `clippy::result_large_err`.
    Redirectable {
        /// The client's trusted redirect, which the error goes back to.
        redirect_uri: Box<Url>,
        /// The OAuth `error` code.
        error: OAuthErrorCode,
        /// The sentence the redirect carries as its `error_description`.
        description: &'static str,
        /// The client's `state`, carried back on the callback.
        client_state: String,
    },
    /// The request this flow just parked was no longer pending when the fast
    /// path approved it — an unexpected concurrent transition. It rolls the
    /// scope back.
    RequestNotPending,
    /// The request would be raised for the Owner, or parked for its limited
    /// page, and
    /// [`may_raise_for_owner`](AuthorizeRequest::may_raise_for_owner) refused:
    /// the authorization start limit. Nothing is parked and the Owner isn't

    StartLimited,
    /// A store failure; or, from a Continue,
    /// [`AuthorizationServerError::AuthorizationRequestNotFound`] for a
    /// request no longer waiting on its limited page.
    Store(AuthorizationServerError),
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/oauth/code_authorization_starter.rs lines 223–235 · authorization-server in the code index

start

Validate authorize_query (client and redirect first, then the redirectable params), park it, and decide: a fully pre-approved request is issued a code under the standing grant’s authority and sent back to the client; anything else waits on the Owner as a pending consent. It all happens in one write scope, so a refusal from inside it rolls everything back, a spent launch included; the Owner prompt is republished once that has committed.

The request is resolved against its client’s registration (ResolvedCodeRequest). A disabled client is refused. A fixed (server-defined) registration holds the request to its redirects and scopes. Any other client is trusted on first use: a request outside the registration is parked with a warning rather than rejected, never takes the fast path, and — while its redirect is untrusted — renders every failure locally rather than risk an open redirect.

A declared aud must be this server’s origin (its FHIR base). A launch must name an unconsumed, unexpired launch context minted for this client or for the server launcher; it is consumed (so it never works twice) and carried onto the parked request. Either failure is invalid_request, and its description says why: a client sees its own launch’s state (not recognized, already used, expired), and another app’s launch looks unknown. A request with no launch is plain OAuth. When the launch binds a patient, the fast path applies only if the standing grant names the same one; otherwise the Owner decides.

A request whose browser session holds less than it asks for (see session_shortfall, against the session’s row) is parked, once validated, admitted by the start limit and its launch consumed, for its browser’s limited page (AuthorizeNextStep::ConfirmSessionShortfall); the fast path and the Owner wait for continue_past_session_shortfall. A session that has gone on past the page for this client before goes on as if it had again.

Errors

See AuthorizationStartError.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) fn start(
    &self,
    authorize_query: &AuthorizeRequest<'_>,
    ids: FreshIds,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<AuthorizeNextStep, AuthorizationStartError> {
    let decided = self
        .store
        .write(|tx| self.start_in(tx, authorize_query, ids, now))?;
    self.publish(decided)
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/oauth/code_authorization_starter.rs lines 1600–1642 · authorization-server in the code index

start_in

The order inside the scope is the point. Every check that can refuse the request runs first; the launch is consumed after them, so a refused request leaves its launch unspent; the request is parked last. The consume is consume_launch, which Launch Contexts explains with its refusals. The session’s shortfall is session_shortfall, against what the session’s row holds (browser_session_grant), and the standing grant’s coverage is GrantCoverage::resolve.

start’s flow, inside its write scope tx.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn start_in<T: GrantTx>(
    &self,
    tx: &mut T,
    authorize_query: &AuthorizeRequest<'_>,
    ids: FreshIds,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<Decided, AuthorizationStartError> {
    if !tx.has_active_signing_key()? {
        return Err(AuthorizationStartError::NoActiveSigningKey);
    }
    let maybe_existing_client = tx.client_by_id(authorize_query.client_id)?;
    let requested_redirect_uri = parse_redirect_uri(authorize_query.redirect_uri)?;
    let requested_scopes: Vec<String> = authorize_query
        .scope
        .split_whitespace()
        .map(str::to_string)
        .collect();
    let resolved = ResolvedCodeRequest::resolve(
        authorize_query.client_id,
        &requested_redirect_uri,
        &requested_scopes,
        maybe_existing_client.as_ref(),
    );
    if resolved.is_client_disabled() {
        return Err(AuthorizationStartError::LocalPage(
            AuthorizeRefusal::DisabledClient,
        ));
    }
    // A redirect is trustworthy only when a client we already know already
    // registered it.
    let redirect_trusted = resolved.is_redirect_registered();
    if resolved.is_registration_fixed() && !redirect_trusted {
        return Err(AuthorizationStartError::LocalPage(
            AuthorizeRefusal::RedirectUriNotAllowed,
        ));
    }
    validate_code_params(
        authorize_query,
        &requested_redirect_uri,
        redirect_trusted,
        &self.server_origin,
    )?;
    if resolved.is_registration_fixed() && !resolved.are_scopes_registered() {
        return Err(AuthorizationStartError::Redirectable {
            redirect_uri: Box::new(requested_redirect_uri),
            error: OAuthErrorCode::InvalidScope,
            description: SCOPES_NOT_REGISTERED_DESCRIPTION,
            client_state: authorize_query.client_state.to_owned(),
        });
    }
    let decidable_in_requesting_browser = authorize_query.can_decide_consents
        && resolved
            .approvable_scopes()
            .missing_approval_scopes(authorize_query.session_token_grant)
            .is_empty();
    let coverage = GrantCoverage::resolve(
        tx,
        resolved.presented_client_change(),
        authorize_query.client_id,
        &requested_redirect_uri,
        &requested_scopes,
    )?;
    // A session that ended since its cookie was checked parks nothing for
    // the limited page: the request goes on, and is denied once a code
    // would be issued under the session.
    let session_falls_short =
        browser_session_grant(tx, authorize_query.sid, &self.stale_session_cutoff, now)?
            .is_some_and(|session_grant| {
                !session_shortfall(&requested_scopes, &session_grant).is_empty()
            });
    let waits_on_limited_page = session_falls_short
        && !tx.is_session_shortfall_acknowledged_for_client(
            authorize_query.sid,
            authorize_query.client_id,
        )?;
    // Parking for the limited page writes a request and spends its launch,
    // so it asks the start limit as raising one for the Owner does. Continue
    // then raises it without asking again.
    if waits_on_limited_page && !(authorize_query.may_raise_for_owner)() {
        return Err(AuthorizationStartError::StartLimited);
    }

    // Consume the launch last, after every check that can refuse the
    // request; a refusal after it rolls the scope back, so a refused
    // request leaves its launch unspent.
    let launch_context = match authorize_query.launch {
        None => None,
        Some(launch) => match consume_launch(tx, launch, authorize_query.client_id, now)? {
            Ok(launch_context) => Some(launch_context),
            Err(launch_refusal) => {
                tracing::warn!(
                    client_id = authorize_query.client_id,
                    ?launch_refusal,
                    "refused a launch",
                );
                return Err(start_error(
                    authorize_query,
                    &requested_redirect_uri,
                    redirect_trusted,
                    OAuthErrorCode::InvalidRequest,
                    launch_refusal_kind(launch_refusal),
                ));
            }
        },
    };

    let (launch, launch_bound_patient) = launch_context.map_or((None, None), |context| {
        let launch_bound_patient = context.patient().map(str::to_owned);
        (Some(context.nonce), launch_bound_patient)
    });
    let parked_request = CodeRequest::new(
        NewCodeRequestArgs {
            id: ids.request_id.clone(),
            client_id: authorize_query.client_id.to_owned(),
            requested_scopes,
            ttl: AUTHORIZATION_REQUEST_TTL,
            redirect_uri: requested_redirect_uri,
            code_challenge: authorize_query.code_challenge.to_owned(),
            client_state: authorize_query.client_state.to_owned(),
            sid: authorize_query.sid.to_owned(),
            launch,
            launch_bound_patient,
            pre_approved_scopes: coverage.pre_approved_scopes().to_vec(),
            decidable_in_requesting_browser,
            awaits_limited_page: waits_on_limited_page,
        },
        now,
    );
    // The session falls short, and hasn't gone on for this client before:
    // park the request for its browser's limited page. The Owner isn't
    // told of it, so nothing is republished.
    if waits_on_limited_page {
        tx.insert_code_request(&parked_request)?;
        return Ok(Decided {
            next_step: Ok(AuthorizeNextStep::ConfirmSessionShortfall {
                request_id: ids.request_id,
            }),
            pending_consents_changed: false,
        });
    }
    let fast_path_coverage = fast_path_coverage(&parked_request, coverage);
    // A request about to be raised for the Owner asks the start limit
    // first.
    if fast_path_coverage.is_none()
        && !decidable_in_requesting_browser
        && !(authorize_query.may_raise_for_owner)()
    {
        return Err(AuthorizationStartError::StartLimited);
    }
    decide(
        tx,
        &parked_request,
        fast_path_coverage,
        ids.code,
        &self.stale_session_cutoff,
        now,
        // Park the request — every path from here on references it by id.
        |tx| {
            tx.insert_code_request(&parked_request)?;
            Ok(parked_request.clone())
        },
    )
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/oauth/code_authorization_starter.rs lines 337–499 · authorization-server in the code index

continue_past_session_shortfall

The request is loaded by load_code_request_awaiting_limited_page, and goes on through its own acknowledge_session_shortfall transition, written through the guarded replace, so a Cancel that landed first wins.

Go on with request id, which waits on the limited page of the browser holding the browser session sid: go on past the page (the request becomes pending, with a fresh AUTHORIZATION_REQUEST_TTL from now), remember that sid went on for the request’s client (so its later requests for that client skip the page), and take the branch start would have taken had the session held all it asks for. Its standing-grant coverage is read again (the Owner may have approved or revoked a grant meanwhile), so a covered request is issued code under it, and any other is raised for the Owner, and decided on the consent card or the wait page as recorded at its start. The start limit isn’t asked: the request spent from it when it parked.

Errors

AuthorizationStartError::Store with AuthorizationServerError::AuthorizationRequestNotFound for a request no longer waiting on that page (another session’s, already gone on, decided, or expired: the same as an expired request anywhere else); AuthorizationStartError::NoActiveSigningKey, as at the start, leaving the request waiting; AuthorizationStartError::Redirectable with access_denied for a client disabled since, the request denied (the limited page follows it as it follows Cancel’s); otherwise as start.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) fn continue_past_session_shortfall(
    &self,
    id: &str,
    sid: &str,
    code: String,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<AuthorizeNextStep, AuthorizationStartError> {
    let decided = self
        .store
        .write(|tx| self.continue_in(tx, id, sid, code, now))?;
    self.publish(decided)
}
}

fn main() {
fn a_session_gone_on_for_a_client_skips_the_limited_page_for_it() {

                Duration::hours(24),

            )
        })
        .unwrap();

            .start(
                &AuthorizeRequest {
                    sid,
                    ..request(client_id, scope)

        "req-1",

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/oauth/code_authorization_starter.rs lines 2136–2174 · authorization-server in the code index

continue_in

continue_past_session_shortfall’s flow, inside its write scope tx.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn continue_in<T: GrantTx>(
    &self,
    tx: &mut T,
    id: &str,
    sid: &str,
    code: String,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<Decided, AuthorizationStartError> {
    if !tx.has_active_signing_key()? {
        return Err(AuthorizationStartError::NoActiveSigningKey);
    }
    let parked_request = load_code_request_awaiting_limited_page(tx, id, sid, now)?;
    let maybe_existing_client = tx.client_by_id(&parked_request.client_id)?;
    let resolved = ResolvedCodeRequest::resolve(
        &parked_request.client_id,
        &parked_request.redirect_uri,
        &parked_request.requested_scopes,
        maybe_existing_client.as_ref(),
    );
    // The client was disabled since the request parked: the browser can't
    // go on with it, so it ends here, and the app hears why.
    if resolved.is_client_disabled() {
        return refuse_waiting_request(
            tx,
            &parked_request,
            AuthorizeRefusal::DisabledClient,
            now,
        );
    }
    let coverage = GrantCoverage::resolve(
        tx,
        resolved.presented_client_change(),
        &parked_request.client_id,
        &parked_request.redirect_uri,
        &parked_request.requested_scopes,
    )?;
    // The start limit isn't asked: the request spent from it when it
    // parked.
    decide(
        tx,
        &parked_request,
        fast_path_coverage(&parked_request, coverage),
        code,
        &self.stale_session_cutoff,
        now,
        |tx| {
            let not_found = || {
                AuthorizationStartError::Store(
                    AuthorizationServerError::AuthorizationRequestNotFound {
                        id: id.to_owned(),
                    },
                )
            };
            let continued = parked_request
                .acknowledge_session_shortfall(AUTHORIZATION_REQUEST_TTL, now)
                .map_err(|_| not_found())?;
            if !tx.replace_code_request(&parked_request, &continued)? {
                return Err(not_found());
            }
            tx.record_session_shortfall_acknowledgement(sid, &parked_request.client_id)?;
            Ok(continued)
        },
    )
}
}

fn main() {
fn publish(&self, decided: Decided) -> Result<AuthorizeNextStep, AuthorizationStartError> {

}

Decided

What a start’s or continue’s scope committed: the step the user-agent takes next, or the refusal it is sent away with, and whether the Owner prompt may have changed, to be republished once the scope has closed.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
struct Decided {
    /// The next step, or a refusal that keeps what the scope wrote: the fast
    /// path's denial for an ended browser session, and a Continue's denial
    /// for a client disabled since the request parked. A refusal that must
    /// roll the scope back is the scope's own `Err` instead.
    next_step: Result<AuthorizeNextStep, AuthorizationStartError>,
    /// Whether the Owner prompt may have changed, so it is republished.
    pending_consents_changed: bool,
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/oauth/code_authorization_starter.rs lines 572–580 · authorization-server in the code index

refuse_waiting_request

The denial is the request’s own deny_on_limited_page, the same transition as the limited page’s Cancel. The Owner never saw the request, so nothing is republished.

Deny parked_request, still waiting on its limited page, for refusal at now, in the scope tx, and send the app access_denied carrying refusal’s sentence. A request no longer waiting there (a Cancel won) is not found.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn refuse_waiting_request(
    tx: &mut impl GrantTx,
    parked_request: &CodeRequest,
    refusal: AuthorizeRefusal,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<Decided, AuthorizationStartError> {
    let not_found = || {
        AuthorizationStartError::Store(AuthorizationServerError::AuthorizationRequestNotFound {
            id: parked_request.id.clone(),
        })
    };
    let refused = parked_request
        .deny_on_limited_page(now)
        .map_err(|_| not_found())?;
    if !tx.replace_code_request(parked_request, &refused)? {
        return Err(not_found());
    }
    Ok(Decided {
        next_step: Err(AuthorizationStartError::Redirectable {
            redirect_uri: Box::new(parked_request.redirect_uri.clone()),
            error: OAuthErrorCode::AccessDenied,
            description: refusal.description(),
            client_state: parked_request.client_state.clone(),
        }),
        pending_consents_changed: false,
    })
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/oauth/code_authorization_starter.rs lines 1500–1550 · authorization-server in the code index

decide

The shared tail of CodeAuthorizationStarter::start and CodeAuthorizationStarter::continue_past_session_shortfall, in their scope tx, for request, whose session holds all it asks for or whose browser has said to go on, and which the start limit has admitted: park it (insert it, or go on past its limited page), which answers with the request as parked, then issue code under the standing grant when fast_path_coverage holds it, under stale_session_cutoff, or else raise it for the Owner.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn decide<T: GrantTx>(
    tx: &mut T,
    request: &CodeRequest,
    fast_path_coverage: Option<StandingGrantCoverage>,
    code: String,
    stale_session_cutoff: &StaleSessionCutoff,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
    park: impl FnOnce(&mut T) -> Result<CodeRequest, AuthorizationStartError>,
) -> Result<Decided, AuthorizationStartError> {
    let decidable_in_requesting_browser = request.decidable_in_requesting_browser;
    let parked_request = park(tx)?;

    let next_step = match fast_path_coverage {
        Some(standing_grant_coverage) => issue_under_standing_grant(
            tx,
            &standing_grant_coverage,
            &parked_request,
            code,
            stale_session_cutoff,
            now,
        )?,
        None => Ok(AuthorizeNextStep::AwaitOwner {
            request_id: parked_request.id.clone(),
            decidable_in_requesting_browser,
        }),
    };
    // A request raised for the Owner is newly pending; one the fast path
    // decided may have been the Owner prompt for the width of the approval,
    // so the prompt is recomputed either way.
    Ok(Decided {
        next_step,
        pending_consents_changed: true,
    })
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/oauth/code_authorization_starter.rs lines 638–671 · authorization-server in the code index

issue_under_standing_grant

The writer is the same one the Owner’s approval goes through, RequestApprover::approve_for_code, which bounds the code by the requesting browser’s session and stamps the grant used.

The fast path’s approval, in the scope tx: the one place a code is issued with no person deciding, its authority the standing grant. It goes through the same writer as the Owner’s approval, naming CodeAuthority::StandingGrant, so every code issued here can be found by that name. The two Results say which outcomes keep what the scope wrote:

  • issued: AuthorizeNextStep::RedirectToClient with the code; the scope commits the approved request, its code, and the standing grant’s last_used_at stamped with now;
  • the request’s browser session is no longer live under stale_session_cutoff: access_denied to the client, saying the browser signed out; the scope commits the request denied, since there is nothing to bound the code by and nothing to revoke later;
  • the request was no longer pending: AuthorizationStartError::RequestNotPending, which rolls the scope back.
#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn issue_under_standing_grant(
    tx: &mut impl GrantTx,
    standing_grant_coverage: &StandingGrantCoverage,
    parked_request: &CodeRequest,
    code: String,
    stale_session_cutoff: &StaleSessionCutoff,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<Result<AuthorizeNextStep, AuthorizationStartError>, AuthorizationStartError> {
    let requested_redirect_uri = parked_request.redirect_uri.clone();
    let client_state = &parked_request.client_state;
    match RequestApprover::within(tx).approve_for_code(
        CodeAuthority::StandingGrant(standing_grant_coverage),
        parked_request,
        standing_grant_coverage.patient(),
        code,
        stale_session_cutoff,
        now,
    )? {
        CodeApproval::Issued(issued_code) => Ok(Ok(AuthorizeNextStep::RedirectToClient {
            redirect_uri: requested_redirect_uri,
            code: issued_code.code,
            client_state: client_state.to_owned(),
        })),
        CodeApproval::RequestNotPending => Err(AuthorizationStartError::RequestNotPending),
        CodeApproval::BrowserSessionEnded => Ok(Err(AuthorizationStartError::Redirectable {
            redirect_uri: Box::new(requested_redirect_uri),
            error: OAuthErrorCode::AccessDenied,
            description: BROWSER_SIGNED_OUT_DESCRIPTION,
            client_state: client_state.to_owned(),
        })),
    }
}
}

            scopes: vec!["openid".to_owned()],
            ..code_grant("g1", "app")
        })
        .unwrap();
    let (code_authorization_starter, _) = starter(store);
    let outcome = code_authorization_starter
        .start(
            &request("app", "patient/Patient.r openid"),
            ids(),
            Utc::now(),
        )
        .expect("starts");
    assert!(matches!(outcome, AuthorizeNextStep::AwaitOwner { .. }));
    assert_eq!(grant_last_used_at(&code_authorization_starter), None);
}
}

parse_redirect_uri

The presented redirect_uri must be a well-formed http/https URL (RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1); either failure is an unconditional local page.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn parse_redirect_uri(redirect_uri: &str) -> Result<Url, AuthorizationStartError> {
    let parsed = Url::parse(redirect_uri)
        .map_err(|_| AuthorizationStartError::LocalPage(AuthorizeRefusal::InvalidRedirectUri))?;
    if parsed.scheme() != "http" && parsed.scheme() != "https" {
        return Err(AuthorizationStartError::LocalPage(
            AuthorizeRefusal::InvalidScheme,
        ));
    }
    Ok(parsed)
}
}

validate_code_params

The server’s origin is also its FHIR base and the iss every launch hands the app, so an aud names this server exactly when it equals the origin.

The response type, the PKCE challenge, and a declared aud — spec’d errors delivered back to the client only once the redirect is trusted, else as a local page.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn validate_code_params(
    authorize_query: &AuthorizeRequest<'_>,
    redirect_uri: &Url,
    redirect_trusted: bool,
    server_origin: &str,
) -> Result<(), AuthorizationStartError> {
    let fail = |error: OAuthErrorCode, local: AuthorizeRefusal| {
        start_error(
            authorize_query,
            redirect_uri,
            redirect_trusted,
            error,
            local,
        )
    };
    // Only the authorization-code grant is implemented (RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1).
    if authorize_query.response_type != "code" {
        return Err(fail(
            OAuthErrorCode::UnsupportedResponseType,
            AuthorizeRefusal::UnsupportedResponseType,
        ));
    }
    // Only S256 PKCE is supported; anything else is `invalid_request` (RFC
    // 7636 §4.4.1), as is a malformed challenge.
    if authorize_query.code_challenge_method != "S256" {
        return Err(fail(
            OAuthErrorCode::InvalidRequest,
            AuthorizeRefusal::UnsupportedCodeChallengeMethod,
        ));
    }
    if !is_valid_s256_code_challenge(authorize_query.code_challenge) {
        return Err(fail(
            OAuthErrorCode::InvalidRequest,
            AuthorizeRefusal::InvalidCodeChallenge,
        ));
    }
    // A declared SMART `aud` must name this server.
    if let Some(aud) = authorize_query.aud {
        // The server's origin is also its FHIR base, the `iss` every launch
        // hands the app, so a SMART `aud` names this server exactly when it is
        // that origin.
        if aud != server_origin {
            return Err(fail(
                OAuthErrorCode::InvalidRequest,
                AuthorizeRefusal::InvalidAudience,
            ));
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}
}

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn aud_must_name_this_server() {
    let code_authorization_starter = registered_app_starter();
    let authorize_query = AuthorizeRequest {
        aud: Some("https://ruth.relay.example"),
        ..request("app", "openid")
    };
    assert!(
        matches!(
            code_authorization_starter.start(&authorize_query, ids(), Utc::now()),
            Ok(AuthorizeNextStep::AwaitOwner { .. })
        ),
        "the origin is this server",
    );
    for refused in [
        "https://ruth.relay.example/",
        "https://ruth.relay.example/fhir-r4",
        "https://ruth.relay.example.evil",
        "http://ruth.relay.example",
        "https://other.relay.example",
        "",
    ] {
        let authorize_query = AuthorizeRequest {
            aud: Some(refused),
            ..request("app", "openid")
        };
        assert!(
            matches!(
                code_authorization_starter.start(&authorize_query, ids(), Utc::now()),
                Err(AuthorizationStartError::Redirectable {
                    error: OAuthErrorCode::InvalidRequest,
                    ..
                })
            ),
            "{refused:?} is not this server",
        );
        let untrusted_query = AuthorizeRequest {
            aud: Some(refused),
            ..request("newcomer", "openid")
        };
        assert!(matches!(
            code_authorization_starter.start(&untrusted_query, ids(), Utc::now()),
            Err(AuthorizationStartError::LocalPage(
                AuthorizeRefusal::InvalidAudience
            ))
        ));
    }
}
}

start_error

Whom a failure is told to depends on whether the redirect can be trusted: a redirect is trusted only when a client the server already knows registered it. Sending an error to an untrusted redirect would make the server an open redirector.

A refusal of authorize_query: back to the client as error, with the local kind’s sentence as its error_description, once its redirect is trusted; else the local page (RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1).

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn start_error(
    authorize_query: &AuthorizeRequest<'_>,
    redirect_uri: &Url,
    redirect_trusted: bool,
    error: OAuthErrorCode,
    local: AuthorizeRefusal,
) -> AuthorizationStartError {
    if redirect_trusted {
        AuthorizationStartError::Redirectable {
            redirect_uri: Box::new(redirect_uri.clone()),
            error,
            description: local.description(),
            client_state: authorize_query.client_state.to_owned(),
        }
    } else {
        AuthorizationStartError::LocalPage(local)
    }
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/oauth/code_authorization_starter.rs lines 1130–1163 · authorization-server in the code index

Authorization Status Reader

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/oauth/authorization_status_reader.rs

When an app’s code request can’t be decided in the browser that made it, the browser waits on the wait page. The page polls GET /oauth/authorize/{id} until the request is decided, then follows the answer back to the app: with a code, with access_denied, or nowhere if the request expired. The status reader is that poll, and its only power is this one read.

An approved request’s status carries its code, so the poll answers only a browser entitled to see it: the browser session the request was made in, or a session that could decide the request on the consent card anyway. Holding the request id is not enough. Reading the status gives a deciding session nothing new, since the code is bound by PKCE to the app that asked, and it lets the Owner’s wait page keep answering after the Owner signs in again in the same browser, under a new session.

The tests poll the fake store’s code and device requests as the requesting session or another.

domain::capabilities::oauth::authorization_status_reader

any_request_status_scopes

The scopes that let a browser session read the status of a code-flow request made in another browser session: the ones that load the request on the consent card and decide it there, wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.r and wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.u. A session holding them could approve the request itself, and the code its status carries is bound by PKCE to the client that asked, so the read gives it nothing new.

}

AuthorizationStatusView

Where a polled request stands.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) enum AuthorizationStatusView {
    /// Undecided and not yet expired: waiting for the Owner, or still on its
    /// browser's limited page. The wait page keeps polling.
    Pending,
    /// Denied: the route builds the client callback carrying
    /// `error=access_denied` from these.
    Denied {
        /// The registered redirect the client presented.
        redirect_uri: Url,
        /// The `state` the client sent, carried back on the callback.
        client_state: String,
    },
    /// Approved: the route builds the client callback carrying the code from
    /// these. An approved request answers with its code whatever the time;
    /// the code's own expiry is checked when the client redeems it.
    Approved {
        /// The registered redirect the client presented.
        redirect_uri: Url,
        /// The authorization code issued when the request was approved.
        code: String,
        /// The `state` the client sent, carried back on the callback.
        client_state: String,
    },
    /// The request passed its `expires_at` undecided. Expiry is never stored:
    /// the poll derives it from the time.
    Expired,
}
}

pub(crate) enum AuthorizationStatusError {
    /// No code request the poller may read has this id: the polling

    /// device request or pairing, or names a request the poller may not read.

    /// it `500 server_error`.
    ApprovedWithoutCode,

    Store(AuthorizationServerError),
}

status

The current status of the code request id, for the browser holding the browser session poller (None when it holds none):

  • pending, or still on its browser’s limited page (as undecided), and before expires_at: AuthorizationStatusView::Pending;
  • either of those past expires_at: AuthorizationStatusView::Expired;
  • denied: AuthorizationStatusView::Denied, with the callback details;
  • approved: AuthorizationStatusView::Approved, with the code issued for the request, whatever the time.

A request poller may not read (see PollingBrowserSession), a device request or a browser pairing (each has its own poll), and any request when there is no poller, is AuthorizationStatusError::NotFound, the same as an unknown id, so the read says nothing about whether id exists.

Errors

See AuthorizationStatusError.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub(crate) fn status(
    &self,
    id: &str,
    poller: Option<&PollingBrowserSession>,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<AuthorizationStatusView, AuthorizationStatusError> {
    self.store.read(|tx| {
        let request = tx
            .code_request_by_id(id)?
            .filter(|request| poller.is_some_and(|poller| poller.can_read(request)))
            .ok_or_else(|| AuthorizationStatusError::NotFound { id: id.to_owned() })?;
        Ok(match request.state {
            // A request still on its browser's limited page is as
            // undecided as one waiting for the Owner.
            CodeRequestState::AwaitingLimitedPage | CodeRequestState::Pending
                if request.is_expired_at(now) =>
            {
                AuthorizationStatusView::Expired
            }
            CodeRequestState::AwaitingLimitedPage | CodeRequestState::Pending => {
                AuthorizationStatusView::Pending
            }
            CodeRequestState::Denied => AuthorizationStatusView::Denied {
                redirect_uri: request.redirect_uri,
                client_state: request.client_state,
            },
            CodeRequestState::Approved(_) => {
                let code = tx
                    .authorization_code_by_request_id(id)?
                    .ok_or(AuthorizationStatusError::ApprovedWithoutCode)?;
                AuthorizationStatusView::Approved {
                    redirect_uri: request.redirect_uri,
                    code: code.code,
                    client_state: request.client_state,
                }
            }
        })
    })
}
}

fn main() {
fn status_reports_each_state_and_expires_stale_pending_requests() {
    let store = FakeGrantStore::default();
    let now = Utc::now();
    store
        .tx()
        .insert_code_request(&code_request(
            "pending",
            RequestStatus::Pending,
            now + Duration::minutes(5),
        ))
        .unwrap();
    store
        .tx()
        .insert_code_request(&code_request(
            "stale",
            RequestStatus::Pending,
            now - Duration::minutes(1),
        ))
        .unwrap();
    store
        .tx()
        .insert_code_request(&code_request(
            "denied",
            RequestStatus::Denied,
            now + Duration::minutes(5),
        ))
        .unwrap();
    store
        .tx()
        .insert_code_request(&code_request(
            "approved",
            RequestStatus::Approved,
            now + Duration::minutes(5),
        ))
        .unwrap();
    store
        .tx()
        .issue_authorization_code(&AuthorizationCode {
            code: "the-code".to_owned(),
            request_id: "approved".to_owned(),
            client_id: "client".to_owned(),
            redirect_uri: Url::parse("https://example.com/cb").unwrap(),
            code_challenge: "c".repeat(43),
            granted_scopes: vec!["read".to_owned()],
            patient: None,
            issued_at: now,
            expires_at: now + AUTHORIZATION_CODE_TTL,
            sid: FIXTURE_SID.to_owned(),
        })
        .unwrap();
    let reader = AuthorizationStatusReader::new(store);
    let requester = requester();

    assert_eq!(
        reader.status("pending", Some(&requester), now).unwrap(),
        AuthorizationStatusView::Pending
    );
    assert_eq!(
        reader.status("stale", Some(&requester), now).unwrap(),
        AuthorizationStatusView::Expired
    );
    assert!(matches!(
        reader.status("denied", Some(&requester), now).unwrap(),
        AuthorizationStatusView::Denied { .. }
    ));
    assert_eq!(
        reader.status("approved", Some(&requester), now).unwrap(),
        AuthorizationStatusView::Approved {
            redirect_uri: Url::parse("https://example.com/cb").unwrap(),
            code: "the-code".to_owned(),
            client_state: "state".to_owned(),
        }
    );
    assert!(matches!(
        reader.status("ghost", Some(&requester), now),
        Err(AuthorizationStatusError::NotFound { .. })
    ));
}
}

            now + Duration::minutes(5),
        ))
        .unwrap();
    store
        .tx()
        .insert_device_request(&device_request("device", "CODE", RequestStatus::Pending))
        .unwrap();
    let reader = AuthorizationStatusReader::new(store);
    let request_reader =
        Scope::wildflower(WildflowerResource::AuthorizationRequest, Permission::READ);
    let request_decider =
        Scope::wildflower(WildflowerResource::AuthorizationRequest, Permission::UPDATE);
    let decider = session("owner-sid", any_request_status_scopes());

    for poller in [&requester(), &decider] {
        assert_eq!(
            reader.status("parked", Some(poller), now).unwrap(),
            AuthorizationStatusView::Pending,
            "{poller:?}"
        );
    }
    for (id, poller) in [
        ("parked", Some(session("another-sid", Vec::new()))),
        ("parked", Some(session("reader-sid", vec![request_reader]))),
        (
            "parked",
            Some(session("decider-sid", vec![request_decider])),
        ),
        ("parked", None),
        ("device", Some(requester())),
        (
            "device",
            Some(session("owner-sid", any_request_status_scopes())),
        ),
        ("device", None),
    ] {
        assert!(
            matches!(
                reader.status(id, poller.as_ref(), now),
                Err(AuthorizationStatusError::NotFound { .. })
            ),
            "{id} polled from {poller:?}"
        );
    }
}
}

Session Shortfall

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/domain/capabilities/oauth/session_shortfall.rs

A browser paired with read-only access may run an app that asks for write. A code earned in that browser carries only what its session holds, so the person at the browser is told first, on the limited page, before the Owner is asked anything. The code authorization starter parks such a request awaiting the limited page and sends the browser there. The page reads what the session lacks, and the person goes on (the starter’s continue_past_session_shortfall) or cancels (here).

Every operation answers only the browser session the request was made in, so a leaked request id reads, continues and cancels nothing. No scope opens the capability: the caller is the browser that made the request, known by its browser session’s sid. What the session holds is read from its row, not from its token, as /oauth/authorize reads it, so the page and the starter judge the session alike.

The tests park code requests from the session shortfall fixtures.

load_code_request_awaiting_limited_page

The one load the page’s read, its Cancel and the starter’s Continue share.

Load request id for the browser session sid while it waits on that browser’s limited page: an unexpired code request made in sid, awaiting the page.
