Access Bindings

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/live_bindings/access.rs

The /authorization surface is the Owner’s: grants, apps, browsers, consent prompts and tokens. Every one of its capabilities is behind a scope, and these bindings say which. A handler names one in Scoped<…>; the extractor reads the verified claims the session gate left on the request, and builds the capability only if the token covers its required scopes. Otherwise the request gets a 403 naming what is missing, and the capability never exists. Each required scope comes from the capability’s own *_scopes() function, the same one the list of grantable admin scopes reads, so what is enforced and what can be granted can’t drift.

Most bindings are fixed-scope (FixedScopeCapability): one scope set gates the whole capability, and build never sees the caller’s grant. The consent reader and decider are data-dependent (Capability): they are gated by a scope too, but what approving a prompt takes depends on the prompt, so build keeps the caller’s grant for the methods to check per call.

The /authorization bindings: each scope-gated capability over the concrete SqliteGrantStore, built from the router state and the caller’s claims by its FixedScopeCapability (one required scope set) or Capability (a grant the capability checks per call) impl. Handlers acquire them through Scoped<…>, which checks the required scopes before the capability exists.

OAuth Bindings

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/live_bindings/oauth.rs

/oauth is the front door: apps, devices and browsers that hold no token for this server yet. No claims unlock its capabilities, so each is a FromState binding, built from the shared state alone and acquired through Live<…>. Where one has a gate, the gate is a proof its method takes, such as an authenticated client at /oauth/token, not the extractor.

Three handles here aren’t for handlers at all. setup_authorization_server gives them to the host, which calls them in-process: one mints launches, one mints sign-in codes, one waits on a consent.

live_bindings::oauth

The /oauth bindings: the pre-auth front door over the concrete SqliteGrantStore — the capabilities handlers acquire through Live<…> (FromState), whose gate, where they have one, is the proof their methods take — and the in-process minters and watcher crate::setup_authorization_server hands the host and the other slices.

mint

Only the code’s hash is kept, in memory, so a restart drops every outstanding code (Same-Device Sign-In Codes).

Mint a sign-in code and return it, for the code of /oauth/sign-in?code=…&next=…: the first browser to present it, within 60 seconds, is signed in as the Owner. Only its hash is kept, in memory, so a restart drops it.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub fn mint(&self) -> SameDeviceSignInCode {
    let code = generate_same_device_sign_in_code();
    self.codes.insert(&code, Utc::now());
    SameDeviceSignInCode::new(code, Arc::clone(&self.codes))
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/live_bindings/oauth.rs lines 246–250 · authorization-server in the code index

The Same-Device Sign-In tests hold a code to signing in once.

end_signed_in_sessions

The minter also ends the sessions codes signed in, through this run’s store, whichever of the server’s runs minted the codes: the host does once the server’s last launch view closes. Each code is a SameDeviceSignInCode, which holds the code and the set of the run that minted it, but nothing of that run’s store, so a view that outlives its run pins no run’s database. The flow is the same-device session ender.

Withdraw sign_in_codes, and end the sessions they signed browsers in with, by expiring them now in this run’s store, whichever run minted the codes: those browsers’ cookies stop working, and they are sent through sign-in again. Returns how many sessions were ended; a code that signed nobody in, or whose session was ended already, ends nothing. A failure leaves each code holding its session, so ending them can be tried again. It writes to the database, so call it on a blocking thread.

Errors

AuthorizationServerError::Infrastructure on a store failure.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub fn end_signed_in_sessions(
    &self,
    sign_in_codes: &[SameDeviceSignInCode],
) -> Result<usize, AuthorizationServerError> {

        .end_sessions_signed_in_with(sign_in_codes, Utc::now())

Wait until the request consent names no longer waits for the Owner: decided, expired, or gone. Answers at once for one that already doesn’t. Each read (is_awaiting_owner) runs on a blocking thread.

Errors

AuthorizationServerError::Infrastructure when reading the request fails, or when the authorization server stops before the request settles.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub async fn until_settled(&self, consent: ConsentKey) -> Result<(), AuthorizationServerError> {
    let mut pending_consents_recomputed_rx = self.pending_consents_recomputed_rx.clone();
    loop {
        pending_consents_recomputed_rx.borrow_and_update();
        let store = self.store.clone();
        let read_consent = consent.clone();
        let pending = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || {
            store.read(|tx| tx.is_awaiting_owner(&read_consent, Utc::now()))
        })
        .await
        .map_err(|error| {
            AuthorizationServerError::infrastructure("reading a pending consent", error)
        })??;
        if !pending {
            return Ok(());
        }
        if pending_consents_recomputed_rx.changed().await.is_err() {
            return Err(AuthorizationServerError::infrastructure(
                "watching a pending consent",
                "the authorization server stopped",
            ));
        }
    }
}
}

Ports and Adapters

A few things the domain must do reach outside the store: telling the host a request now waits for the Owner, revoking and checking tokens in the revocation store the FHIR server shares, and asking the host whether a visitor may start another request. The domain doesn’t learn what does these. It calls out through a port, a small trait it owns; an adapter implements the port on the concrete runtime type. The capabilities hold the ports as trait objects lifted from the state, and their unit tests wire in fakes that record the calls or fail on purpose.

The ports live in ports/, bare contracts. Two of the adapters live in adapters/; the start gate’s real adapter is the host’s, since the host is who decides.

ports

Host/HTTP-seam dependency-inversion traits the authorization server’s domain capabilities call out through — so domain::capabilities can trigger the runtime side-effects a consent or logout flow needs without the domain learning axum, the Owner prompt’s watch channel, or the revocation store’s concrete type. The real implementations live in crate::adapters, on AuthorizationServerState; tests wire in-memory fakes. Mirrors apps-rust’s ports/.

  • OwnerApproval — ask the Owner: republish the OwnerPrompt to the host after any transition that may change it (see the trait);
  • Revocation / RevocationCheck — denylist a token jti or bulk-revoke a subject, and answer whether a token is revoked; the seams the revoking capabilities, logout, and the token verifier go through;
  • AuthorizationStartGate — the host’s say over whether a request may start an authorization request, which the limit on /oauth/authorize and /oauth/device_authorization asks. Public: the host implements it.

adapters

The composition layer: the crate::ports seams implemented onto the concrete runtime types. Each adapter lives here rather than beside its trait so ports/ stays a set of bare contracts the domain can name without learning what implements them.

Tell the host which request now waits for the Owner. Any transition that may change the Owner prompt calls this after its write: a new /oauth/authorize, /oauth/device_authorization or pairing request, a request raised for the Owner, an approval or a denial. So the host notifies about a new request, and its server page shows the one waiting.

Republish the OwnerPrompt, the newest request awaiting the Owner, to the host.

The adapter

The Owner prompt’s republish seam (crate::ports) adapted onto the bare AuthorizationServerState. See the module docs for the composition layer.

The adapter is the shared state itself, so an Arc<AuthorizationServerState> is the port handle the capabilities hold.

Recompute the OwnerPrompt from the store and publish it on its watch sender. Call after every transition that may change it (see OwnerApproval).

The DB read happens inside send_if_modified, so the watch sender’s internal lock serialises the read+publish pair across concurrent callers: whichever caller commits last to SQLite is also whichever publishes last to the watch (and the published value matches what is in the DB at that moment). Without this, a thread that read the newest request before a concurrent thread’s commit could overwrite the watch with a stale one after the concurrent publish — the host would advertise a request whose row was already handled.

Uses send_if_modified so a transition that leaves the newest request unchanged (e.g. denying an older one) does not produce a spurious change of the server’s status.

On a DB-read failure the watch keeps what it holds: None there says nothing is pending, which the host takes to mean every request it notified for is settled, so a transient failure publishing it would re-notify each one still waiting. A request handled meanwhile drops off on the next mutation or reaper tick that reads.

Either way it then pings pending_consents_recomputed_tx, so a PendingConsentWatcher rereads its request: one decided or expired while a newer one stays newest changes nothing on the watch above.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn republish_active(&self) {
    self.owner_approval_tx.send_if_modified(|current| {
        let next = match self.store.read(|tx| tx.owner_prompt(Utc::now())) {
            Ok(next) => next,
            Err(error) => {
                tracing::warn!("owner_prompt query failed; keeping the last: {error}");
                return false;
            }
        };
        if *current == next {
            false
        } else {
            *current = next;
            true
        }
    });
    self.pending_consents_recomputed_tx.send_replace(());
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/adapters/owner_approval.rs lines 45–62 · authorization-server in the code index

  • The read happens inside send_if_modified, under the channel’s lock, so whichever caller commits last to SQLite also publishes last, and the channel never goes back to a request already handled.
  • A publish that changes nothing is suppressed, so denying an older request leaves the server’s status alone.
  • A failed read keeps what the channel holds. Publishing nothing would tell the host every request it notified is settled, and a passing failure would then re-notify each one still waiting. A request handled meanwhile drops off at the next write or reaper tick.
  • Either way it pings the recompute channel, so a PendingConsentWatcher rereads its request: one decided under a newer request changes nothing on the published channel.

The OAuth Endpoints tests hold it to clearing the prompt once a consent is decided.

Revocation

Revoke issued tokens: denylist one token’s jti until its expiry, tagged with why, or move a subject’s revocation epoch to now, which kills every access and refresh token issued to it before. A grant’s revoke, /authorization/revocations, logout and an app revoking its own token at /oauth/revoke go through it. Errors are strings, so the port doesn’t carry the store’s error type.

Revoke issued tokens. Both operations are implemented over the shared RevocationStore; a test fake records the calls (or fails, to prove a caller swallows or surfaces the error). Errors are stringified so the port stays free of the store’s concrete error type.

RevocationCheck

Ask whether a token is revoked: by its jti on the denylist, or by being issued to its subject before the subject’s epoch. A missing jti skips the first check, a missing issue time the second. The token verifier asks it behind every gate, and so, in-process, the FHIR server’s; refresh redemption asks whether a family began before its app’s epoch. Every caller fails closed on an error.

Answer whether an issued token has been revoked — the read side of the same store, kept as its own object-safe seam so the token verifier can be tested against a stub. Errors are stringified for the same reason as Revocation’s.

The token verifier runs the full check here (the per-jti denylist and the per-subject epoch), behind the authorization server’s gates and, through InProcessTokenVerifier, HFS’s bearer auth. Refresh redemption asks it whether a family began before its client’s epoch. Both fail closed on a store error.

fn main() {
pub(crate) trait RevocationCheck: Send + Sync + 'static {
    /// Whether the token identified by `jti` (denylisted individually) or

    ///

    ///
    /// Returns the store failure (stringified) when the read fails; the caller

        jti: Option<&str>,
        issued_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,

ports::authorization_start_gate

AuthorizationStartGate — the host’s say over how fast authorization requests are started, asked by the limit on the two routes that start one (http::middleware::authorization_start_limit).

AuthorizationStartGate

The host’s say over how fast authorization requests start. /oauth/authorize and /oauth/device_authorization park requests the Owner is asked about, and a stranger shouldn’t be able to raise them without end. The server knows nothing of who is asking beyond the request; the host’s listener puts what it knows of the connection in the request’s extensions, and the host decides from those. A request it admits has spent from whatever allowance it keeps; one it refuses is answered 429 Too Many Requests.

Whether a request may start an authorization request (GET /oauth/authorize, POST /oauth/device_authorization), handed to crate::setup_authorization_server.

The authorization server knows nothing of who is asking beyond the request; the host, whose listener put what it knows of the connection in the request’s extensions (its connect info), decides. Asked at most once per request: before the request is parsed, or, for a request carrying a browser session that can decide consents or an /oauth/authorize request carrying no browser session, only once the request is to be raised for the Owner. POST /authorization/oauth-consents/{id}/ask-owner, which raises a parked request for the Owner, asks it too, only when it raises one. A request it admits has spent from whatever allowance it keeps, and one it refuses is answered 429 Too Many Requests.

Seeding

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/seeding.rs

Some rows must exist before anyone can ask for anything: a key to sign tokens with, and the server’s own clients. Seeding writes them at every boot, and is safe to run again. The signing key is inserted only when no key is active, and never rotated. The server’s own clients are upserted: rewritten to match the code every boot, so their registrations follow the host’s configuration and a store written by another build is corrected. An upsert keeps a row’s registration time and any disable the Owner set.

The bundled SMART sample apps’ clients are static, so a migration seeds them instead (0003_seed_sample_clients). Seeding in code is kept for what depends on the running host: the configured scopes and origin, and a freshly generated key.

A debug build also seeds a client for each first-party app’s local dev server. Release builds contain no code that could write them.

seeding

First-boot seeding for the grant store: the signing key and the essential clients (the host app’s client and the browser-session client). Safe to call on every boot — the signing key is inserted only when none exists (never rotated), and the two clients are ensured (re-applied as an upsert) so their definitions always match the host’s granted scopes, correcting any drift in the stored rows.

The bundled SMART sample-app clients (growth-chart, medication-viewer → my_web_app, PRECISE-HBR) are seeded in SQL instead — migration 0003_seed_sample_clients — since they’re static definitions a migration can express. Only the runtime-derived seeds (the essential clients’ scopes, the generated signing key) stay here.

open_and_seed_store

setup_authorization_server calls it first, and the server doesn’t start if it fails. A key is generated before the write scope opens, because generating an RSA key is slow.

Wrap the host-owned connection pool in a grant store (applying migrations, which includes the SQL seed of the SMART sample-app clients) and run the runtime-derived first-boot seeding steps — the signing key, the essential clients, and the FHIR server UI’s client. Safe to call on every boot.

Errors

Returns an error if the store cannot be created (migrations) or if any seeding step fails.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub fn open_and_seed_store(
    pool: DieselPool,
    host_app_client_scopes: &[String],
    fhir_ui_client_id: &str,
    server_origin: &url::Url,
) -> anyhow::Result<SqliteGrantStore> {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::new(pool).context("failed to open grant store")?;
    // RSA key generation is slow, so it runs before the write lock is taken,
    // and only on a boot that finds no active key.
    let candidate_signing_key = if store
        .read(|tx| tx.active_signing_key())
        .context("failed to read signing keys")?
        .is_none()
    {
        Some(SigningKey::generate().context("failed to generate signing key")?)
    } else {
        None
    };
    store.write(|tx| -> anyhow::Result<()> {
        ensure_some_active_signing_key(tx, candidate_signing_key)
            .context("failed to seed signing key")?;
        ensure_essential_clients(tx, host_app_client_scopes)
            .context("failed to seed the essential clients")?;
        ensure_fhir_ui_client(tx, fhir_ui_client_id, server_origin)

Insert candidate, generated before the scope opened, as the active signing key if none is active; otherwise leave the existing keys alone. Idempotent — safe to call on every boot.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn ensure_some_active_signing_key(
    tx: &mut impl SigningKeysTx,
    candidate: Option<SigningKey>,
) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let existing = tx.active_signing_key().context("read signing keys")?;
    if existing.is_some() {
        return Ok(());
    }
    let mut key = candidate.context("the active signing key vanished during seeding")?;
    key.is_active = true;
    tx.insert_signing_key(&key).context("insert signing key")?;
    Ok(())
}
}

ensure_essential_clients

The two essential clients are server-defined, public, and have no redirect URIs. The browser-session client has no grant type: its tokens are minted only at /oauth/sign-in and by the pairing page’s poll, and neither is an OAuth flow.

Ensure the essential clients — the host app’s client (crate::WILDFLOWER_HOST_APP_CLIENT_ID) and the browser-session client (crate::BROWSER_SESSION_CLIENT_ID) — match the code’s definitions. Upserted on every boot so their policy always matches: the host app’s client is allowed host_app_client_scopes (the live app sources them from tauri-shared-config.json; see crate::default_host_app_client_scopes), and the browser-session client the Owner’s scopes (crate::OWNER_SCOPES), the most any browser session may hold. This corrects stored rows that have drifted (registration time and any admin disable are preserved).

Both are public with no redirect URIs. The host app’s client is allowed every grant type; the browser-session client none, since its tokens are minted only at /oauth/sign-in (a same-device session) and by the pairing page’s poll (a paired session), neither of them OAuth, so no OAuth flow can be run as it and /oauth/token never mints its token.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn ensure_essential_clients(
    tx: &mut impl ClientsTx,
    host_app_client_scopes: &[String],
) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let wildflower_host_app_client = Client {
        client_id: crate::WILDFLOWER_HOST_APP_CLIENT_ID.to_string(),
        name: "Wildflower Host".to_string(),
        kind: ClientKind::Public,
        redirect_uris: vec![],
        allowed_scopes: host_app_client_scopes.to_vec(),
        allowed_grant_types: AllowedGrantType::ALL.to_vec(),
        secret_hash: None,
        registered_at: Utc::now(),
        disabled_at: None,
        registration_source: RegistrationSource::ServerDefined,
    };
    tx.upsert_client(&wildflower_host_app_client)
        .context("seed the host app's client")?;
    let browser_session_client = Client {
        client_id: crate::BROWSER_SESSION_CLIENT_ID.to_string(),
        name: "Wildflower Browsers".to_string(),
        kind: ClientKind::Public,
        redirect_uris: vec![],
        allowed_scopes: crate::owner_scopes(),
        allowed_grant_types: vec![],
        secret_hash: None,
        registered_at: Utc::now(),
        disabled_at: None,
        registration_source: RegistrationSource::ServerDefined,
    };
    tx.upsert_client(&browser_session_client)
        .context("seed the browser-session client")?;
    Ok(())
}
}

ensure_fhir_ui_client

The FHIR server’s web UI signs its users in here with the authorization-code flow, so its client follows the server’s origin.

The FHIR server UI’s client: a public client (PKCE, no secret) whose one redirect URI is {server_origin}/ui/callback, where helios-ui completes its sign-in, allowed user/*.cruds — the UI acts as the signed-in user across every resource type. Upserted on every boot, like ensure_essential_clients, so it follows the server’s origin.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn ensure_fhir_ui_client(
    tx: &mut impl ClientsTx,
    fhir_ui_client_id: &str,
    server_origin: &url::Url,
) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let client = Client {
        client_id: fhir_ui_client_id.to_string(),
        name: "FHIR server UI".to_string(),
        kind: ClientKind::Public,
        redirect_uris: vec![server_origin
            .join("/ui/callback")
            .context("build the UI's redirect URI")?],
        allowed_scopes: vec![Scope::fhir_user_all(Permission::ALL).to_string()],
        allowed_grant_types: vec![
            AllowedGrantType::AuthorizationCode,
            AllowedGrantType::RefreshToken,
        ],
        secret_hash: None,
        registered_at: Utc::now(),
        disabled_at: None,
        registration_source: RegistrationSource::ServerDefined,
    };
    tx.upsert_client(&client)
        .context("seed the FHIR server UI client")?;
    Ok(())
}
}

seed_dev_app_clients

Debug builds only: a client for each first-party app’s local dev server. The first-party apps ship from the published site, and their clients register its redirect. A debug build also gets a dev tile per app, whose launch URL points at the app’s vite dev server on localhost, and that launch needs a client whose redirect is that exact loopback address. Each dev client is a separate client under its own id, because adding a plaintext loopback redirect to the production client would register it on a client a public website uses.

  • Ports come from the shared dev-app-ports.json, embedded at compile time. The apps’ dev seed and each app’s vite.config.ts read the same file, so a redirect can’t drift off the port its dev server listens on.
  • The redirect is the origin root, except the OHIF viewer’s, whose launch lands on /fhir-viewer, since redirect matching is exact.
  • Scopes mirror each app’s production client, which is what a dev build of the app asks for.
  • It is code, not a migration, because migrations run in release databases too. The function, and its one call in the Tauri host, are compiled only into debug builds.
  • It upserts, so a change to a definition lands on the next boot. They are trusted on first use, like any app the Owner approved.

The debug-only OAuth clients for the first-party apps’ vite dev servers — the authorization server half of wildflowerhealthio_apps::seed_dev_apps.

The first-party SMART apps (Medications, Importer, the OHIF imaging viewer, Strength) ship as rows served from https://wildflowerhealth.io (apps migrations 0005_first_party_apps_to_cloud onward), whose clients register the published-site redirect URI. A debug build also gets an <app>-dev row (wildflowerhealthio_apps::dev_seed) whose launch URL points at the app’s local vite dev server on the port dev-app-ports.json pins, and that row needs its own client, under a random id, whose absolute http://localhost:{port} redirect is what the authorize flow matches (FHIR Sync for Pebble has no row, but its dev server gets a client the same way). They are separate clients rather than extra redirect entries on the production ones because adding a plaintext loopback redirect there would register it on a client that a public website uses.

The redirect path is the origin root for every app but the OHIF viewer, whose launch lands on /fhir-viewer — redirect matching is exact-URL.

Scopes mirror each app’s production client exactly — a dev build of the app requests the same set (apps/*/src/config.ts).

Runtime rather than a migration for the same reason as the app rows: migrations run unconditionally, so a migration-seeded dev client would exist in release databases too. The whole function is #[cfg(debug_assertions)], as is its single call site in the Tauri host.

Upserted (not insert-if-missing) so a definition change lands on the next boot — the same treatment ensure_essential_clients gets, and safe here because nothing but this code owns these rows.

Errors

Returns an error if the store cannot be opened/migrated or an upsert fails.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub fn seed_dev_app_clients(pool: DieselPool) -> anyhow::Result<()> {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::new(pool).context("failed to open grant store")?;
    // Ports come from the shared dev-port file, not literals — see
    // [`DEV_APP_PORTS_JSON`].
    let ports: DevAppPorts = serde_json::from_str(DEV_APP_PORTS_JSON)
        .expect("the embedded dev-app-ports.json must declare a port per dev app id");
    let dev_clients = [
        (
            MEDICATIONS_DEV_CLIENT_ID,
            "Medications (Dev)",
            // `apps/medications/medications-web/src/config.ts`'s `MEDICATIONS_SCOPE` — see
            // [`MEDICATIONS_DEV_SCOPES`].
            MEDICATIONS_DEV_SCOPES,
            ports.medications_dev,
            DEV_ROOT_REDIRECT_PATH,
        ),
        (
            IMPORTER_DEV_CLIENT_ID,
            "Importer (Dev)",
            // Mirrors the production Importer client's write-carrying set
            // (`apps/importer-web/src/config.ts`, as widened by the authorization server
            // migration `0009_widen_importer_client_write_scopes`, re-applied by
            // `0015` on an install that skipped it) — a dev build
            // requests the same scopes, and unlike the medications viewer above the
            // Importer writes. Full `.cruds` (create + read + update + delete +
            // search) on each handled type.
            [
                "launch",
                "openid",
                "fhirUser",
                "system/DocumentReference.cruds",
                "system/Patient.cruds",
                "system/Observation.cruds",
                "system/Practitioner.cruds",
                "system/DiagnosticReport.cruds",
                "system/Medication.cruds",
                "system/MedicationRequest.cruds",
                "system/MedicationDispense.cruds",
                "system/ServiceRequest.cruds",
                "system/ImagingStudy.cruds",
            ]
            .as_slice(),
            ports.importer_dev,
            DEV_ROOT_REDIRECT_PATH,
        ),
        (
            OHIF_VIEWER_DEV_CLIENT_ID,
            "Imaging (Dev)",
            // Mirrors the production OHIF viewer client's read-only set (the
            // `smartScope` in `apps/ohif-viewer-web/config/app-config.js`, seeded
            // by migration `0009`): the launch Patient plus the ImagingStudy and
            // DocumentReference searches the OHIF FHIR data source issues.
            [
                "launch",
                "openid",
                "fhirUser",
                "system/Patient.rs",
                "system/ImagingStudy.rs",
                "system/DocumentReference.rs",
            ]
            .as_slice(),
            ports.ohif_viewer_dev,
            // NOT the root: redirect matching is exact-URL, so the entry must be
            // the exact route the launch targets — the FHIR
            // Viewer mode, as on the production client (seeded by migration
            // `0009_seed_ohif_viewer_client` and repointed by `0010`), which is
            // where OHIF's data source sends the browser back to and what it
            // passes as `redirect_uri`.
            "/fhir-viewer",
        ),
        (
            FHIR_SYNC_PEBBLE_DEV_CLIENT_ID,
            "FHIR Sync for Pebble (Dev)",
            // Mirrors the production FHIR Sync for Pebble client (migration
            // `0017_seed_fhir_sync_pebble_client`, widened by `0018`, re-keyed by
            // `0030`, the `scope` in
            // `apps/fhir-sync-pebble/fhir-sync-pebble-web/src/config.ts`). Standalone-only, so
            // there is no `wildflowerhealthio_apps::dev_seed` row; the loopback root carries
            // the `ConnectMenu`'s redirect.
            [
                "openid",
                "fhirUser",
                "system/Patient.rs",
                "system/Observation.cu",
            ]
            .as_slice(),
            ports.fhir_sync_pebble_dev,
            DEV_ROOT_REDIRECT_PATH,
        ),
        (
            PLOTS_DEV_CLIENT_ID,
            "Plots (Dev)",
            // `apps/plots/plots-web/src/config.ts`'s scope string — see
            // [`PLOTS_DEV_SCOPES`].
            PLOTS_DEV_SCOPES,
            ports.plots_dev,
            DEV_ROOT_REDIRECT_PATH,
        ),
        (
            SYNTHETIC_DATA_DEV_CLIENT_ID,
            "Synthetic Data (Dev)",
            // `apps/synthetic-data/synthetic-data-web/src/config.ts`'s scope string — see
            // [`SYNTHETIC_DATA_DEV_SCOPES`].
            SYNTHETIC_DATA_DEV_SCOPES,
            ports.synthetic_data_dev,
            DEV_ROOT_REDIRECT_PATH,
        ),
        (
            STRENGTH_DEV_CLIENT_ID,
            "Wildflower Strength (Dev)",
            // `apps/strength/strength-web/src/config.ts`'s `STRENGTH_SCOPE` — see
            // [`STRENGTH_DEV_SCOPES`].
            STRENGTH_DEV_SCOPES,
            ports.strength_dev,
            DEV_ROOT_REDIRECT_PATH,
        ),
    ];
    for (client_id, name, scopes, port, redirect_path) in dev_clients {
        use url::Url;

        let client = Client {
            client_id: client_id.to_string(),
            name: name.to_string(),
            kind: ClientKind::Public,
            // The port comes from the shared `dev-app-ports.json` (above), the
            // same file the apps dev seed and each `vite.config.ts` read — so it
            // is never a literal duplicated here, and the path is the route that
            // client's launch actually lands on (redirect matching is exact-URL).
            redirect_uris: vec![
                Url::parse(&format!("http://localhost:{port}{redirect_path}")).unwrap(),
            ],
            allowed_scopes: scopes.iter().map(|s| (*s).to_string()).collect(),
            allowed_grant_types: vec![
                AllowedGrantType::AuthorizationCode,
                AllowedGrantType::RefreshToken,
            ],
            secret_hash: None,
            registered_at: Utc::now(),
            disabled_at: None,
            registration_source: RegistrationSource::TrustedOnFirstUse,
        };
        store
            .write(|tx| tx.upsert_client(&client))
            .with_context(|| format!("seed dev client {client_id}"))?;
    }
    Ok(())
}
}

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn seeds_the_plots_dev_client_with_the_apps_own_scopes() {
    const PLOTS_CONFIG_TS: &str = include_str!(concat!(
        env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
        "/../../../../apps/plots/plots-web/src/config.ts"
    ));
    const PLOTS_CLIENT_ID: &str = "474e103de61f9141c4b640d59bfa130e";
    let scope_string = format!("'{}'", PLOTS_DEV_SCOPES.join(" "));
    assert!(
        PLOTS_CONFIG_TS.contains(&scope_string),
        "apps/plots/plots-web/src/config.ts must request exactly {scope_string}",
    );
    for client_id in [PLOTS_DEV_CLIENT_ID, PLOTS_CLIENT_ID] {
        assert!(
            PLOTS_CONFIG_TS.contains(&format!("'{client_id}'")),
            "apps/plots/plots-web/src/config.ts must launch as {client_id}",
        );
    }

    let pool =
        wildflowerhealthio_persistence::open_in_memory_pool().expect("open in-memory pool");
    seed_dev_app_clients(pool.clone()).expect("seed dev clients");
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::new(pool).expect("open grant store");
    let client = store
        .read(|tx| tx.client_by_id(PLOTS_DEV_CLIENT_ID))
        .expect("query client")
        .expect("plots dev client seeded");
    let ports: DevAppPorts = serde_json::from_str(DEV_APP_PORTS_JSON).expect("dev ports");
    assert_eq!(client.kind, ClientKind::Public);
    assert_eq!(client.allowed_scopes, PLOTS_DEV_SCOPES);

        client.redirect_uris,
        vec![
            url::Url::parse(&format!("http://localhost:{}/", ports.plots_dev))
                .expect("a valid absolute redirect")
        ],
    );

    let production = store
        .read(|tx| tx.client_by_id(PLOTS_CLIENT_ID))
        .expect("query client")
        .expect("migration 0028 re-keys the Plots client");
    assert_eq!(production.allowed_scopes, PLOTS_DEV_SCOPES);
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/seeding.rs lines 668–711 · authorization-server in the code index

Persistence

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/db/mod.rs

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/db/shared.rs

This part is the SQLite adapter behind the Grant Store port. The domain asks the port for two kinds of scope, a read and a write (GrantStore), and for primitives inside them, one trait per table. This part answers each of those with SQL against the host’s shared database file.

The adapter decides nothing. A primitive reports absence and conflict through its return type, an Option or a bool, and fails only with the opaque infrastructure error. What a missing row or a lost race means is decided in the capabilities. What the adapter does own is the guard that keeps a primitive safe when two callers race: a conditional UPDATE … RETURNING only one of them can win, a primary key, a partial unique index, a CHECK. Each page in this part names the guard behind each primitive, and its tests hold the guard against a real database.

The domain’s row types are the diesel rows. Client, SigningKey, LaunchContext and the rest derive diesel’s Queryable, Selectable and Insertable where they are defined, and name their table there. The adapter holds the table! declarations those derives point at, the column mappings a domain field needs to reach a TEXT column, and the trait implementations. The two kinds of row whose shape differs from the domain’s, a grant read off the cross-kind view and an authorization request of either table, have row types of their own here, converted on the way in and out.

Where things live

SqliteGrantStore holds the connection pool, applies the migrations and opens the two scopes. Each concern’s file holds its table!, its column mappings and its port trait, implemented on SqliteGrantTx, the handle a scope lends its closure:

  • Clients, db/clients.rs: the clients table, the registered apps.
  • Browser Sessions, db/browser_sessions.rs: browser_sessions, and session_shortfall_acknowledgements beside it.
  • Authorization Requests, db/authorization_requests/: code_authorization_requests for code requests, and user_code_requests for device requests and browser pairings.
  • Launch Contexts, db/launch_contexts.rs: launch_contexts, each consumed once.
  • Grants, db/grants/: authorization_code_grants, device_grants, and the grants view across them.
  • Authorization Codes, db/authorization_codes.rs: authorization_codes, the one-minute codes.
  • Refresh Tokens, db/refresh_tokens.rs: refresh_token_families and the refresh_tokens rotated within them.
  • Signing Keys, db/signing_keys.rs: signing_keys, the RSA keys tokens are signed with.
  • Test Fixtures: the generators and helpers the adapter’s tests share.

The schema lives in the crate’s migrations/ directory, one <version>_<name>/ folder per migration holding an up.sql and a down.sql, compiled into the binary and applied when the store is opened (migrations).

db::shared

SQLite stores lists, URLs and enums as TEXT. A domain row keeps its field as the domain type (Vec<String>, Url, FlowType) and plugs a mapping in with #[diesel(serialize_as = …, deserialize_as = …)]. A read parses the stored text, so a corrupt or out-of-domain value is a typed read error, never a panic and never a silently wrong value. Each table’s page has a test that tampers with a stored row to show it.

A mapping only one concern binds lives in that concern’s file; the ones here are bound by two or more. The two macros generate every mapping in the adapter, shared and per-concern alike.

json_text_column

It makes JsonStrings here, a list of strings (scopes, mostly) bound by clients, browser sessions, both request tables, codes, grants and refresh families, and one newtype per other shape beside its table.

Define a newtype that binds/reads its inner value as compact JSON in a TEXT column — one concrete type per inner shape (a generic would run into diesel’s derive limitations). Reads parse the stored TEXT; corrupt JSON surfaces as a diesel deserialization error, never a panic.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
macro_rules! json_text_column {
    ($(#[$doc:meta])* $name:ident, $inner:ty) => {
        $(#[$doc])*
        #[derive(
            Debug,
            ::diesel::expression::AsExpression,
            ::diesel::deserialize::FromSqlRow,
        )]
        #[diesel(sql_type = ::diesel::sql_types::Text)]
        pub struct $name(pub $inner);

        impl ::core::convert::From<$inner> for $name {
            fn from(value: $inner) -> Self {
                Self(value)
            }
        }

        impl ::core::convert::From<$name> for $inner {
            fn from(wrapper: $name) -> Self {
                wrapper.0
            }
        }

        impl ::diesel::deserialize::FromSql<::diesel::sql_types::Text, ::diesel::sqlite::Sqlite>
            for $name
        {
            fn from_sql(
                value: ::diesel::sqlite::SqliteValue<'_, '_, '_>,
            ) -> ::diesel::deserialize::Result<Self> {
                let text = <String as ::diesel::deserialize::FromSql<
                    ::diesel::sql_types::Text,
                    ::diesel::sqlite::Sqlite,
                >>::from_sql(value)?;
                Ok(Self(::serde_json::from_str(&text)?))
            }
        }

        impl ::diesel::serialize::ToSql<::diesel::sql_types::Text, ::diesel::sqlite::Sqlite>
            for $name
        {
            fn to_sql<'b>(
                &'b self,
                out: &mut ::diesel::serialize::Output<'b, '_, ::diesel::sqlite::Sqlite>,
            ) -> ::diesel::serialize::Result {
                out.set_value(::serde_json::to_string(&self.0)?);
                Ok(::diesel::serialize::IsNull::No)
            }
        }
    };
}
}

fn main() {
macro_rules! text_enum_column {
    ($name:ty) => {
        impl ::diesel::deserialize::FromSql<::diesel::sql_types::Text, ::diesel::sqlite::Sqlite>
            for $name
        {
            fn from_sql(
                value: ::diesel::sqlite::SqliteValue<'_, '_, '_>,
            ) -> ::diesel::deserialize::Result<Self> {
                let text = <String as ::diesel::deserialize::FromSql<
                    ::diesel::sql_types::Text,
                    ::diesel::sqlite::Sqlite,
                >>::from_sql(value)?;
                Ok(text.parse::<$name>()?)
            }
        }

        impl ::diesel::serialize::ToSql<::diesel::sql_types::Text, ::diesel::sqlite::Sqlite>
            for $name
        {
            fn to_sql<'b>(
                &'b self,
                out: &mut ::diesel::serialize::Output<'b, '_, ::diesel::sqlite::Sqlite>,
            ) -> ::diesel::serialize::Result {
                out.set_value(self.as_ref().to_owned());
                Ok(::diesel::serialize::IsNull::No)
            }
        }
    };
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/db/shared.rs line 129 · authorization-server in the code index

SQLite Grant Store

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/db/grant_store.rs

SqliteGrantStore is the Grant Store port’s SQLite adapter. It holds a pool of connections onto the host’s shared database file, applies this crate’s migrations when it is opened, and opens the port’s two scopes on a connection it checks out of the pool: a read scope in autocommit, where each statement sees a committed state and no lock is held between statements, and a write scope inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, which takes the write lock before its first read.

SQLite admits one writer at a time across every connection to the file. A second write scope’s BEGIN IMMEDIATE waits for the first to commit, for up to the connection’s busy timeout, and then fails. That is what lets a capability read a row, decide, and write it back in one write scope without another writer landing in between.

The revocation store and lock order

The host’s token revocation store, which holds the per-token denylist and each app’s revocation epoch, is not in this adapter. It reads and writes through the host’s shared rusqlite connection: another connection onto the same file, behind a lock of its own. No write scope touches the revocation store. Taking that connection’s lock while holding the file’s write lock risks a lock-order stall: the other connection, mid-write, can be waiting for the write lock this scope holds, and the two wait on each other until the busy timeout. So a capability reads or writes the revocation store before or after its write scope, never inside it, which is why two operations open two scopes.

db::grant_store

SqliteGrantStore

The SQLite adapter for the GrantStore port. Cheap to clone (the pool is an Arc inside), so it drops straight into the axum state.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub struct SqliteGrantStore {
    /// The app-wide r2d2 pool onto the shared database file, built and owned
    /// by the host (`wildflowerhealthio_persistence::open_pool`): the same pool
    /// the other diesel-backed slices' stores ride. Diesel's connection API is
    /// `&mut`, so each scope checks a connection out of the pool rather than
    /// sharing one behind a mutex; the pool (an `Arc` inside) makes the store
    /// cheap to clone into the axum state. Its connections are additional
    /// openers onto the same file the host's rusqlite
    /// `persistence-rust::Connection` serves the remaining rusqlite slices
    /// from: `SQLite` permits several connections per file, and the pool's
    /// `busy_timeout` pragma rides out the brief write locks any connection
    /// takes.
    pool: DieselPool,
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/db/grant_store.rs lines 131–137 · authorization-server in the code index

write

The closure’s own error comes back unchanged, so a capability sees its flow’s refusal, not a store error. Only a failure of BEGIN, COMMIT or ROLLBACK itself becomes the infrastructure error grant store transaction failed.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn write<T, E: From<AuthorizationServerError>>(
    &self,
    f: impl FnOnce(&mut Self::Tx<'_>) -> Result<T, E>,
) -> Result<T, E> {
    let mut conn = self.connection()?;
    let sqlite: &mut SqliteConnection = &mut conn;
    sqlite
        .immediate_transaction(|conn| {
            f(&mut SqliteGrantTx { conn }).map_err(ScopeError::Closure)
        })
        .map_err(|error| match error {
            ScopeError::Closure(error) => error,
            ScopeError::Transaction(error) => {
                E::from(AuthorizationServerError::infrastructure(
                    "grant store transaction failed",
                    error,
                ))
            }
        })
}
}

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
enum ScopeError<E> {
    /// The scope's closure failed with its own error; the transaction rolls
    /// back, and the caller gets that error as it was.
    Closure(E),
    /// Diesel's `BEGIN`, `COMMIT` or `ROLLBACK` failed; the caller gets it as an
    /// infrastructure error.
    Transaction(diesel::result::Error),
}
}

MIGRATIONS

A migration runs once per database, so a shipped migration is never edited. An install that already ran it never reads it again; a change lands as a new migration, which reaches fresh and upgraded installs alike. The tests hold each migration to that: each drives a database to the version just before it with MigrationsThrough, plants the rows an install could hold, upgrades, and checks the result, often reverting the migration too, to show its down.sql restores what was there.

The authorization server migrations, embedded from the crate’s migrations/ tree at compile time (diesel layout: <version>_<name>/up.sql + down.sql). Applied once per database in SqliteGrantStore::new via wildflowerhealthio_persistence::run_diesel_migrations under MIGRATION_NAMESPACE (see that runner for why the stock diesel harness can’t be shared across slices). Each migration’s header says what it changes and why (see migrations/); because each runs only once per database, an upgrade neither re-drops nor re-seeds.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
const MIGRATIONS: EmbeddedMigrations = embed_migrations!();
}

authorization-server-rust/src/db/grant_store.rs line 36 · authorization-server in the code index

Running the migrations twice is a no-op the second time (the namespaced runner skips already-applied versions) and every expected table — plus the grants view — exists afterwards, so opening an existing database never re-drops or errors.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn migrations_are_idempotent_and_create_the_schema() {
    let mut conn = SqliteConnection::establish(":memory:").expect("open in-memory");
    wildflowerhealthio_persistence::run_diesel_migrations(
        &mut conn,
        MIGRATION_NAMESPACE,
        MIGRATIONS,
    )
    .expect("first run");
    wildflowerhealthio_persistence::run_diesel_migrations(
        &mut conn,
        MIGRATION_NAMESPACE,
        MIGRATIONS,
    )
    .expect("second run");
    let names: Vec<String> = diesel::sql_query(
        "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type IN ('table', 'view') ORDER BY name",
    )
    .load::<Name>(&mut conn)
    .expect("list tables")
    .into_iter()
    .map(|n| n.name)
    .collect();
    for expected in [
        "authorization_code_grants",
        "authorization_codes",
        "clients",
        "code_authorization_requests",
        "device_grants",
        "grants",
        "browser_sessions",
        "launch_contexts",
        "refresh_token_families",
        "refresh_tokens",
        "session_shortfall_acknowledgements",
        "signing_keys",
        "user_code_requests",
    ] {
        assert!(names.iter().any(|n| n == expected), "missing {expected}");
    }
}
}

Migration 0001 is a destructive rebaseline: applied over a database carrying the retired rusqlite-migrated tables (simulated here by pre-creating an old-shape grants parent + child with a row in it), it drops them and recreates the final shape — no copy, no error.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn migration_rebaselines_over_the_old_rusqlite_tables() {
    use diesel::connection::SimpleConnection;

    let mut conn = SqliteConnection::establish(":memory:").expect("open in-memory");
    conn.batch_execute(
        "PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON;
         CREATE TABLE grants (
             id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL,
             client_id TEXT NOT NULL,
             scopes TEXT NOT NULL,
             granted_at TEXT NOT NULL,
             last_used_at TEXT,
             patient TEXT,
             grant_type TEXT NOT NULL
         );
         CREATE TABLE authorization_code_grants (
             id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL REFERENCES grants(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
             client_id TEXT NOT NULL,
             redirect_uri TEXT NOT NULL
         );
         INSERT INTO grants VALUES
             ('g1', 'c1', '[]', '2024-01-01 00:00:00+00:00', NULL, NULL,
              'authorization_code');
         INSERT INTO authorization_code_grants VALUES
             ('g1', 'c1', 'https://example.com/cb');",
    )
    .expect("simulate the old schema");

    wildflowerhealthio_persistence::run_diesel_migrations(
        &mut conn,
        MIGRATION_NAMESPACE,
        MIGRATIONS,
    )
    .expect("rebaseline");

    // The old parent's row is gone (destructive) and `grants` is now the
    // UNION ALL view over the two rebuilt concrete tables.
    let grants: Vec<Name> = diesel::sql_query("SELECT id AS name FROM grants")
        .load(&mut conn)
        .expect("grants view is queryable");
    assert!(grants.is_empty(), "the rebaseline copies no data");
    let kind: Vec<Name> =
        diesel::sql_query("SELECT type AS name FROM sqlite_master WHERE name = 'grants'")
            .load(&mut conn)
            .expect("sqlite_master");
    assert_eq!(kind.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(kind[0].name, "view");
}
}

Every migration has a version of its own, apart from the historical 0009 pair (left as it shipped; 0015 / 0016 repair it). The runner records applied migrations by version alone, so a second directory under a version an install has already applied is silently skipped there — while a fresh database runs it, so no other test notices.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn migration_versions_are_unique_apart_from_the_historical_0009_pair() {
    let mut names_by_version = std::collections::BTreeMap::<String, Vec<String>>::new();
    for migration in
        MigrationSource::<Sqlite>::migrations(&MIGRATIONS).expect("load migrations")
    {
        names_by_version
            .entry(migration.name().version().to_string())
            .or_default()
            .push(migration.name().to_string());
    }
    let mut shared: Vec<(String, Vec<String>)> = names_by_version
        .into_iter()
        .filter(|(_, names)| names.len() > 1)
        .collect();
    for (_, names) in &mut shared {
        names.sort();
    }
    assert_eq!(
        shared,
        vec![(
            "0009".to_owned(),
            vec![
                "0009_seed_ohif_viewer_client".to_owned(),
                "0009_widen_importer_client_write_scopes".to_owned(),
            ],
        )],
        "give each new migration a version no other migration uses",
    );
}
}

The 0009 pair and its repairs

Two folders share version 0009, and the runner records versions alone, so an install that opened while only one of them existed recorded 0009 and never ran the other. Later migrations repair each half.

The regression 0010_ohif_viewer_client_fhir_viewer_redirect exists for: migrations are run-once, so an install that already applied 0009 never re-reads it. Editing 0009’s redirect_uris in place would have left every upgraded install on the published directory URL, and /authorize matches redirect_uri by exact URL equality — so the /fhir-viewer launch would fail there. A fresh open applies both migrations and cannot tell the two apart; driving a database to 0009 first is the only way to observe it.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn an_install_already_at_0009_is_upgraded_onto_the_fhir_viewer_redirect() {
    let mut conn = SqliteConnection::establish(":memory:").expect("open in-memory");
    wildflowerhealthio_persistence::run_diesel_migrations(
        &mut conn,
        MIGRATION_NAMESPACE,
        MigrationsThrough("0009"),
    )
    .expect("migrate to 0009");

    let seeded: Vec<Name> =
        diesel::sql_query("SELECT redirect_uris AS name FROM clients WHERE client_id = ?")
            .bind::<diesel::sql_types::Text, _>("ohif-viewer")
            .load(&mut conn)
            .expect("0009 must have seeded the ohif-viewer client");
    assert_eq!(
        seeded[0].name, r#"["/","https://wildflowerhealth.io/ohif-viewer/"]"#,
        "0009 must stay exactly as it shipped — an install that ran it sees no edit",
    );

    wildflowerhealthio_persistence::run_diesel_migrations(
        &mut conn,
        MIGRATION_NAMESPACE,
        MigrationsThrough("0010"),
    )
    .expect("upgrade through 0010");

    let upgraded: Vec<Name> =
        diesel::sql_query("SELECT redirect_uris AS name FROM clients WHERE client_id = ?")
            .bind::<diesel::sql_types::Text, _>("ohif-viewer")
            .load(&mut conn)
            .expect("the client row must survive the upgrade");
    assert_eq!(
        upgraded[0].name,
        r#"["/","https://wildflowerhealth.io/ohif-viewer/fhir-viewer"]"#,
    );
}
}

Seeding, reshaping and re-keying clients

The first-party apps’ clients are written by SQL migrations, and every later change to one, a new redirect, narrower scopes, a random id, a new name, is a migration of its own. A re-key carries what was issued to the old id with it, and a rename or a reshape leaves alone a row the Owner has changed.

A new seed reaches an install that already ran every earlier migration: driving a database through 0018 and then opening it with the full set must add the lifting-app client (0019) with its exact redirect URIs and scope set — the upgrade path a fresh open cannot distinguish from a first run.

An install already at 0026 loses both Web Trace clients when it upgrades, with every grant and refresh token they hold, under the foreign key refresh_tokens keeps on its family.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn an_install_already_at_0026_loses_the_web_trace_clients() {
    let mut conn = SqliteConnection::establish(":memory:").expect("open in-memory");
    diesel::sql_query("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON")
        .execute(&mut conn)
        .expect("enforce foreign keys, as the pool does");
    wildflowerhealthio_persistence::run_diesel_migrations(
        &mut conn,
        MIGRATION_NAMESPACE,
        MigrationsThrough("0026"),
    )
    .expect("migrate to 0026");
    for statement in [
        "INSERT INTO clients \
         (client_id, name, kind, redirect_uris, allowed_scopes, allowed_grant_types, \
          secret_hash, registered_at, disabled_at) \
         VALUES ('web-trace-app-dev', 'Web Trace (Dev)', 'public', \
                 '[\"http://localhost:5191/\"]', '[\"launch\"]', \
                 '[\"authorization_code\"]', NULL, '2024-01-01 00:00:00+00:00', NULL)",
        "INSERT INTO refresh_token_families \
         (family_id, client_id, scopes, issued_at, expires_at) \
         VALUES ('web-trace-family', 'web-trace-app', '[]', '2024-01-01', '2099-01-01')",
        "INSERT INTO refresh_token_families \
         (family_id, client_id, scopes, issued_at, expires_at) \
         VALUES ('importer-family', 'importer-app', '[]', '2024-01-01', '2099-01-01')",
        "INSERT INTO refresh_tokens (token_hash, family_id, issued_at) \
         VALUES ('web-trace-token', 'web-trace-family', '2024-01-01')",
        "INSERT INTO refresh_tokens (token_hash, family_id, issued_at) \
         VALUES ('importer-token', 'importer-family', '2024-01-01')",
    ] {
        diesel::sql_query(statement)
            .execute(&mut conn)
            .expect("plant a 0026 row");
    }

    wildflowerhealthio_persistence::run_diesel_migrations(
        &mut conn,
        MIGRATION_NAMESPACE,
        MigrationsThrough("0027"),
    )
    .expect("upgrade through 0027");

    for client_id in ["web-trace-app", "web-trace-app-dev"] {
        assert!(column_for_client(&mut conn, "client_id", client_id).is_empty());
    }
    assert_eq!(
        column_for_client(&mut conn, "client_id", "importer-app").len(),
        1
    );
    let token_hashes: Vec<Name> =
        diesel::sql_query("SELECT token_hash AS name FROM refresh_tokens ORDER BY token_hash")
            .load(&mut conn)
            .expect("query refresh_tokens");
    let token_hashes: Vec<&str> = token_hashes.iter().map(|row| row.name.as_str()).collect();
    assert_eq!(
        token_hashes,
        ["importer-token"],
        "another client's tokens stay"
    );
}
}

An install already at 0027 re-keys the site’s clients when 0028 runs: each production client takes its random id and its redirect moves to the product’s path, each dev client takes its random id, what was issued to them (here a launch) follows, and the Synthetic Data Loader gains a production client. Reverting 0028 restores the old ids and paths and removes that client.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn an_install_already_at_0027_rekeys_the_site_app_clients() {
    use diesel::connection::SimpleConnection as _;
    const SYNTHETIC_DATA: &str = "225ba6af034a3acec6be7ff8010df67f";
    // (old id, new id, the redirect it holds after `0028`).
    let production = [
        (
            "medications-app",
            "9769f8b274370708d0d3ebb2e3e59b7c",
            r#"["https://wildflowerhealth.io/medications/"]"#,
        ),
        (
            "importer-app",
            "165cd26573e5ac72378e6ad2d2198330",
            r#"["https://wildflowerhealth.io/importer/"]"#,
        ),
        (
            "health-viewer-app",
            "474e103de61f9141c4b640d59bfa130e",
            r#"["https://wildflowerhealth.io/health-viewer/"]"#,
        ),
        (
            "wildflower-server-docs",
            "664a01e8614050cd82ffe90350b81413",
            r#"["https://wildflowerhealth.io/server-docs/"]"#,
        ),
    ];
    let dev = [
        ("medications-app-dev", "4be2ee91360733fdcb99b43a3822de5f"),
        ("importer-app-dev", "57268ff88aea38d6a22de56ae53e2c28"),
        ("health-viewer-app-dev", "e7efc7c805f5f8f640bb3b3d48a2d7aa"),
        ("synthetic-data-app-dev", "07a31e58db3367afda5c6480e03ed993"),
    ];

    let mut conn = SqliteConnection::establish(":memory:").expect("open in-memory");
    wildflowerhealthio_persistence::run_diesel_migrations(
        &mut conn,
        MIGRATION_NAMESPACE,
        MigrationsThrough("0027"),
    )
    .expect("migrate to 0027");
    let redirects_at_0027: Vec<String> = production
        .iter()
        .map(|(old, _, _)| {
            column_for_client(&mut conn, "redirect_uris", old)[0]
                .name
                .clone()
        })
        .collect();
    for (old, _) in dev {
        conn.batch_execute(&format!(
            "INSERT INTO clients \
             (client_id, name, kind, redirect_uris, allowed_scopes, allowed_grant_types, \
              secret_hash, registered_at, disabled_at) \
             VALUES ('{old}', 'A (Dev)', 'public', '[\"http://localhost:5190/\"]', \
                     '[\"launch\"]', '[\"authorization_code\"]', NULL, \
                     '2024-01-01 00:00:00+00:00', NULL)"
        ))
        .expect("a dev client at 0027");
    }
    conn.batch_execute(
        "INSERT INTO launch_contexts (nonce, client_id, patient, created_at, expires_at) \
         VALUES ('issued', 'importer-app', 'pat-1', \
                 '2026-01-01T00:00:00Z', '2026-01-01T00:05:00Z')",
    )
    .expect("a launch at 0027");

    wildflowerhealthio_persistence::run_diesel_migrations(
        &mut conn,
        MIGRATION_NAMESPACE,
        MigrationsThrough("0028"),
    )
    .expect("upgrade through 0028");

    for (old, new, redirects) in production {
        assert!(column_for_client(&mut conn, "client_id", old).is_empty());
        assert_eq!(
            column_for_client(&mut conn, "redirect_uris", new)[0].name,
            redirects,
        );
    }
    for (old, new) in dev {
        assert!(column_for_client(&mut conn, "client_id", old).is_empty());
        assert_eq!(
            column_for_client(&mut conn, "redirect_uris", new)[0].name,
            r#"["http://localhost:5190/"]"#,
        );
    }
    let launch: Vec<Name> = diesel::sql_query(
        "SELECT client_id AS name FROM launch_contexts WHERE nonce = 'issued'",
    )
    .load(&mut conn)
    .expect("read the launch");
    assert_eq!(launch[0].name, "165cd26573e5ac72378e6ad2d2198330");
    assert_eq!(
        column_for_client(&mut conn, "redirect_uris", SYNTHETIC_DATA)[0].name,
        r#"["https://wildflowerhealth.io/synthetic-data/"]"#,
    );

    let migration_0028 = MIGRATIONS
        .migrations()
        .expect("embedded migrations")
        .into_iter()
        .find(|migration| migration.name().version() == MigrationVersion::from("0028"))
        .expect("0028 is embedded");
    migration_0028.revert(&mut conn).expect("revert 0028");
    for ((old, _, _), at_0027) in production.iter().zip(&redirects_at_0027) {
        assert_eq!(
            &column_for_client(&mut conn, "redirect_uris", old)[0].name,
            at_0027,
        );
    }
    for (old, _) in dev {
        assert_eq!(column_for_client(&mut conn, "client_id", old).len(), 1);
    }
    assert!(column_for_client(&mut conn, "client_id", SYNTHETIC_DATA).is_empty());
}
}

fn main() {
fn an_install_already_at_0037_rekeys_the_browser_session_client_and_ends_owner_sessions() {
    use diesel::connection::SimpleConnection as _;
    const BROWSERS: &str = "cb9bbe139845cae9654b7909d60d274f";
    const OLD_ID: &str = "wildflower-owner-browser";
    const REVOKED_AT: &str = "2026-10-01 00:00:00+00:00";
    const CLIENT_TABLES: [(&str, &str); 6] = [
        ("authorization_requests", "id"),
        ("authorization_codes", "code"),
        ("authorization_code_grants", "id"),
        ("device_grants", "id"),
        ("refresh_token_families", "family_id"),
        ("launch_contexts", "nonce"),
    ];

    let mut conn = SqliteConnection::establish(":memory:").expect("open in-memory");
    wildflowerhealthio_persistence::run_diesel_migrations(
        &mut conn,
        MIGRATION_NAMESPACE,
        MigrationsThrough("0037"),
    )
    .expect("migrate to 0037");
    conn.batch_execute(&format!(
        "INSERT INTO clients \
         (client_id, name, kind, redirect_uris, allowed_scopes, allowed_grant_types, \
          secret_hash, registered_at, disabled_at) \
         VALUES ('{OLD_ID}', 'Wildflower (Owner browsers)', 'public', \
                 '[]', '[\"system/*.cruds\"]', '[]', NULL, \
                 '2024-01-01 00:00:00+00:00', NULL); \
         INSERT INTO authorization_requests \
         (id, grant_type, client_id, requested_scopes, requested_at, expires_at, status) \
         VALUES ('browser-row', 'authorization_code', '{OLD_ID}', '[]', \
                 '2026-10-16 00:00:00+00:00', '2026-10-16 00:10:00+00:00', 'pending'); \
         INSERT INTO authorization_codes \
         (code, request_id, client_id, redirect_uri, code_challenge, granted_scopes, \
          issued_at, expires_at, sid) \
         VALUES ('browser-row', 'browser-row', '{OLD_ID}', 'https://example/', \
                 'challenge', '[]', '2026-10-16 00:00:00+00:00', \
                 '2026-10-16 00:01:00+00:00', 'standing'); \
         INSERT INTO authorization_code_grants \
         (id, client_id, scopes, granted_at, redirect_uri) \
         VALUES ('browser-row', '{OLD_ID}', '[]', '2026-10-16T00:00:00Z', \
                 'https://example/'); \
         INSERT INTO device_grants \
         (id, client_id, scopes, granted_at, device_name) \
         VALUES ('browser-row', '{OLD_ID}', '[]', '2026-10-16T00:00:00Z', 'A laptop'); \
         INSERT INTO refresh_token_families \
         (family_id, client_id, scopes, issued_at, expires_at) \
         VALUES ('browser-row', '{OLD_ID}', '[]', '2026-10-16 00:00:00+00:00', \
                 '2026-10-17 00:00:00+00:00'); \
         INSERT INTO launch_contexts (nonce, client_id, created_at, expires_at) \
         VALUES ('browser-row', '{OLD_ID}', '2026-10-16 00:00:00+00:00', \
                 '2026-10-16 00:10:00+00:00'); \
         INSERT INTO browser_sessions \
         (sid, kind, name, scopes, created_at, expires_at, revoked_at) \
         VALUES ('standing', 'owner', NULL, '[]', '2026-10-16 00:00:00+00:00', \
                 '2026-10-16 08:00:00+00:00', NULL), \
                ('revoked', 'owner', NULL, '[]', '2026-10-01 00:00:00+00:00', \
                 '2026-10-01 08:00:00+00:00', '{REVOKED_AT}'), \
                ('approved', 'approved', 'A tablet', '[]', '2026-10-16 00:00:00+00:00', \
                 '2026-11-16 00:00:00+00:00', NULL)"
    ))
    .expect("the browser-session client, a row naming it per table and three sessions at 0037");
    let client_ids_of_seeded_rows = |conn: &mut SqliteConnection| {
        CLIENT_TABLES.map(|(table, key)| {
            diesel::sql_query(format!(
                "SELECT client_id AS name FROM {table} WHERE {key} = 'browser-row'"
            ))
            .load::<Name>(conn)
            .expect("read the seeded row")
            .remove(0)
            .name
        })
    };

    wildflowerhealthio_persistence::run_diesel_migrations(
        &mut conn,
        MIGRATION_NAMESPACE,
        MigrationsThrough("0038"),

    .expect("upgrade through 0038");

    assert!(column_for_client(&mut conn, "client_id", OLD_ID).is_empty());
    assert_eq!(
        column_for_client(&mut conn, "name", BROWSERS)[0].name,
        "Wildflower Browsers"
    );
    assert_eq!(client_ids_of_seeded_rows(&mut conn), [BROWSERS; 6]);
    let revoked_at_of = |conn: &mut SqliteConnection, sid: &str| {

            .bind::<diesel::sql_types::Text, _>(sid)

            .expect("read the session")
            .remove(0)
            .name
    };
    let ended_at = revoked_at_of(&mut conn, "standing").expect("the same-device session ended");
    assert!(
        chrono::DateTime::parse_from_str(&ended_at, "%F %T%.f%:z").is_ok(),
        "{ended_at} is in the diesel chrono text encoding"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        revoked_at_of(&mut conn, "revoked").as_deref(),
        Some(REVOKED_AT)
    );
    assert_eq!(revoked_at_of(&mut conn, "approved"), None);
    diesel::sql_query("SELECT decidable_in_requesting_browser FROM authorization_requests")
        .execute(&mut conn)
        .expect("the column has its new name");

    let migration_0038 = MIGRATIONS
        .migrations()
        .expect("embedded migrations")
        .into_iter()
        .find(|migration| migration.name().version() == MigrationVersion::from("0038"))
        .expect("0038 is embedded");
    migration_0038.revert(&mut conn).expect("revert 0038");
    assert_eq!(column_for_client(&mut conn, "client_id", OLD_ID).len(), 1);
    assert!(column_for_client(&mut conn, "client_id", BROWSERS).is_empty());
    assert_eq!(client_ids_of_seeded_rows(&mut conn), [OLD_ID; 6]);
    diesel::sql_query("SELECT requested_by_owner_browser FROM authorization_requests")
        .execute(&mut conn)
        .expect("the column has its old name");
}
}

            .into_iter()

            .collect::<Vec<_>>()

    let family_expiry = |conn: &mut SqliteConnection, family_id: &str| {

        .remove(0)

    assert_eq!(consumed_at(&mut conn, "live"), Some(ended_at));
    assert_eq!(consumed_at(&mut conn, "spent").as_deref(), Some(EARLIER));

    assert_eq!(consumed_at(&mut conn, "dead"), None);
    for (family_id, token_hash) in [("code-in-session", "in-session"), ("device", "device")] {
        assert_eq!(family_expiry(&mut conn, family_id), FUTURE, "{family_id}");
        assert_eq!(consumed_at(&mut conn, token_hash), None, "{token_hash}");
    }
    assert_eq!(
        read(&mut conn, "SELECT code AS name FROM authorization_codes"),
        [Some("in-session".to_owned())]
    );
    assert_eq!(
        read(

        ),

            Some("in-session:pending".to_owned()),
            Some("sessionless:expired".to_owned()),
        ]
    );

            "INSERT INTO authorization_codes \
             (code, request_id, client_id, redirect_uri, code_challenge, granted_scopes, \
              issued_at, expires_at, sid) \

                     '{EARLIER}', '{FUTURE}', NULL)"
        ))
    };
    assert!(
        insert_sessionless_code(&mut conn).is_err(),
        "a code names its session"
    );

    let migration_0042 = MIGRATIONS

        .expect("embedded migrations")
        .into_iter()
        .find(|migration| migration.name().version() == MigrationVersion::from("0042"))
        .expect("0042 is embedded");
    migration_0042.revert(&mut conn).expect("revert 0042");
    insert_sessionless_code(&mut conn).expect("a code's sid is nullable again");

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn an_install_already_at_0045_renames_the_browser_session_kinds() {
    use diesel::connection::SimpleConnection as _;

    const REVOKED_AT: &str = "2026-10-16 03:00:00+00:00";

    let mut conn = SqliteConnection::establish(":memory:").expect("open in-memory");
    wildflowerhealthio_persistence::run_diesel_migrations(
        &mut conn,
        MIGRATION_NAMESPACE,
        MigrationsThrough("0045"),
    )
    .expect("migrate to 0045");
    conn.batch_execute(&format!(
        "INSERT INTO browser_sessions \
         (sid, kind, name, scopes, created_at, expires_at, revoked_at, last_seen_at) \
         VALUES ('same-device', 'owner', NULL, '[\"system/*.cruds\"]', '{CREATED_AT}', \
                 '2026-10-16 08:00:00+00:00', NULL, '{LAST_SEEN_AT}'), \
                ('paired', 'approved', 'A tablet', '[\"wildflower/launch\"]', \
                 '{CREATED_AT}', '2026-10-17 00:00:00+00:00', NULL, '{LAST_SEEN_AT}'), \
                ('revoked', 'approved', 'A phone', '[]', '{CREATED_AT}', \
                 '2026-10-17 00:00:00+00:00', '{REVOKED_AT}', '{CREATED_AT}')"
    ))
    .expect("three sessions at 0045");

    wildflowerhealthio_persistence::run_diesel_migrations(
        &mut conn,
        MIGRATION_NAMESPACE,
        MigrationsThrough("0046"),
    )
    .expect("upgrade through 0046");

    let column_of = |conn: &mut SqliteConnection, column: &str, sid: &str| {
        diesel::sql_query(format!(
            "SELECT {column} AS name FROM browser_sessions WHERE sid = ?"
        ))
        .bind::<diesel::sql_types::Text, _>(sid)
        .load::<OptionalName>(conn)
        .expect("read the session")
        .remove(0)
        .name
    };
    assert_eq!(
        column_of(&mut conn, "kind", "same-device").as_deref(),
        Some("same_device")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        column_of(&mut conn, "kind", "paired").as_deref(),
        Some("paired")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        column_of(&mut conn, "kind", "revoked").as_deref(),
        Some("paired")
    );
    assert_eq!(column_of(&mut conn, "name", "same-device"), None);
    assert_eq!(
        column_of(&mut conn, "scopes", "same-device").as_deref(),
        Some("[\"system/*.cruds\"]")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        column_of(&mut conn, "name", "paired").as_deref(),
        Some("A tablet")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        column_of(&mut conn, "expires_at", "paired").as_deref(),
        Some("2026-10-17 00:00:00+00:00")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        column_of(&mut conn, "last_seen_at", "paired").as_deref(),
        Some(LAST_SEEN_AT)
    );
    assert_eq!(column_of(&mut conn, "revoked_at", "paired"), None);
    assert_eq!(
        column_of(&mut conn, "revoked_at", "revoked").as_deref(),
        Some(REVOKED_AT)
    );
    assert_eq!(
        column_of(&mut conn, "created_at", "revoked").as_deref(),
        Some(CREATED_AT)
    );
    assert!(
        conn.batch_execute(&format!(
            "INSERT INTO browser_sessions \
             (sid, kind, name, scopes, created_at, expires_at, last_seen_at) \
             VALUES ('old', 'owner', NULL, '[]', '{CREATED_AT}', '{CREATED_AT}', \
                     '{CREATED_AT}')"
        ))
        .is_err(),
        "the rebuilt CHECK refuses the old kinds"
    );
    assert!(
        conn.batch_execute(&format!(
            "INSERT INTO browser_sessions \
             (sid, kind, name, scopes, created_at, expires_at, last_seen_at) \
             VALUES ('same-device', 'same_device', NULL, '[]', '{CREATED_AT}', \
                     '{CREATED_AT}', '{CREATED_AT}')"
        ))
        .is_err(),
        "sid stays the primary key"
    );

    let migration_0046 = MIGRATIONS
        .migrations()
        .expect("embedded migrations")
        .into_iter()
        .find(|migration| migration.name().version() == MigrationVersion::from("0046"))
        .expect("0046 is embedded");
    migration_0046.revert(&mut conn).expect("revert 0046");
    assert_eq!(
        column_of(&mut conn, "kind", "same-device").as_deref(),
        Some("owner")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        column_of(&mut conn, "kind", "paired").as_deref(),
        Some("approved")
    );
    assert_eq!(
        column_of(&mut conn, "revoked_at", "revoked").as_deref(),
        Some(REVOKED_AT)
    );
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/db/grant_store.rs lines 2268–2549 · authorization-server in the code index

Clients

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/db/clients.rs

The clients table holds every app’s registration: one row per client_id, read back as a Client, which maps onto the row one field to one column of the same name. The row is the registration. Every check at /oauth/authorize and /oauth/token reads it, the Owner’s approvals of an app trusted on first use write it, and boot-time seeding rewrites the server’s own clients on every boot. The primary key is client_id, so an app has at most one registration, and every lookup goes through that key.

The three list columns hold compact JSON text: allowed_scopes through the shared JsonStrings, and redirect_uris and allowed_grant_types through two mappings only the client binds, JsonUrls and JsonAllowedGrantTypes. kind and registration_source are stored as their wire strings. The tests draw clients from arb_client.

Each of the client row’s custom column mappings rejects an out-of-domain stored value on read as a typed diesel error, never a panic: the JSON TEXT newtypes (JsonUrls / JsonStrings / JsonAllowedGrantTypes) on malformed JSON or an unknown enum member, and the ClientKind text-enum mapping on an unknown discriminant. A row tampered via raw SQL surfaces at the client_by_id read boundary as Err, so a corrupt row can never silently decode to a wrong-but-valid client.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn stored_columns_reject_corrupt_values() {
    // `column = bad_value` tampered onto the migration-seeded `growth_chart`
    // row, each asserted to fail the read.
    for (column, bad_value) in [
        ("redirect_uris", "not json"),        // JsonUrls: malformed JSON
        ("redirect_uris", "[\"not a url\"]"), // JsonUrls: valid JSON, not a URL
        // JsonUrls: a path entry is not an absolute URL (why migration 0021
        // strips them)
        ("redirect_uris", "[\"/\"]"),
        ("allowed_scopes", "not json"), // JsonStrings: malformed JSON
        ("allowed_grant_types", "[\"totally_unknown\"]"), // JsonAllowedGrantTypes: unknown member
        ("kind", "bogus_kind"),                           // ClientKind: unknown discriminant
    ] {
        let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
        let mut conn = store.pool().get().expect("check out a connection");
        diesel::sql_query(format!(
            "UPDATE clients SET {column} = '{bad_value}' WHERE client_id = 'growth_chart'"
        ))
        .execute(&mut conn)
        .expect("tamper the stored row");
        drop(conn);
        assert!(
            store.read(|tx| tx.client_by_id("growth_chart")).is_err(),
            "a corrupt `{column}` must surface as a typed read error",
        );
    }
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/db/clients.rs lines 65–76 · authorization-server in the code index

upsert_client

An app keeps the time it was first registered, and a disabled app stays disabled, whoever writes its registration again: an approval that widens a disabled app’s registration doesn’t re-enable it.

Insert a client, or update its policy fields if one with the same client_id already exists. Used by the seeding every boot runs, so a seeded client’s definition always matches the code, and by the grant recorder’s trust-on-first-use registration. Uses ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE, so it never deletes the row and preserves registered_at and disabled_at — the original registration time and any admin disable survive rather than the client being resurrected.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn upsert_client(&mut self, client: &Client) -> Result<(), AuthorizationServerError> {
    let conn = &mut *self.conn;
    use diesel::upsert::excluded;
    diesel::insert_into(clients::table)
        .values(client.clone())
        .on_conflict(clients::client_id)
        .do_update()
        .set((
            clients::name.eq(excluded(clients::name)),
            clients::kind.eq(excluded(clients::kind)),
            clients::redirect_uris.eq(excluded(clients::redirect_uris)),
            clients::allowed_scopes.eq(excluded(clients::allowed_scopes)),
            clients::allowed_grant_types.eq(excluded(clients::allowed_grant_types)),
            clients::secret_hash.eq(excluded(clients::secret_hash)),
            clients::registration_source.eq(excluded(clients::registration_source)),
        ))
        .execute(conn)
        .map_err(|e| AuthorizationServerError::infrastructure("upsert_client failed", e))?;
    Ok(())
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/db/clients.rs lines 113–132 · authorization-server in the code index

Upserting an existing client updates its name and policy in place but keeps its first registered_at and the Owner’s disable.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn upsert_updates_policy_but_preserves_registration_and_disable() {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    let registered_at = chrono::DateTime::from_timestamp(1_000, 0).unwrap();
    let disabled_at = chrono::DateTime::from_timestamp(1_500, 0).unwrap();
    let mut client = Client {
        client_id: "c1".to_string(),
        name: "First".to_string(),
        kind: ClientKind::Public,
        redirect_uris: vec![],
        allowed_scopes: vec!["openid".to_string()],
        allowed_grant_types: AllowedGrantType::ALL.to_vec(),
        secret_hash: None,
        registered_at,
        disabled_at: Some(disabled_at),
        registration_source: RegistrationSource::TrustedOnFirstUse,
    };
    store.write(|tx| tx.upsert_client(&client)).expect("insert");

    // Re-seed with drifted policy, a newer registered_at, and disabled_at
    // cleared: the policy fields update, but registration time and the admin
    // disable are preserved (the row is updated in place, never resurrected).
    client.name = "Renamed".to_string();
    client.allowed_scopes = vec!["system/*.cruds".to_string()];
    client.registered_at = chrono::DateTime::from_timestamp(2_000, 0).unwrap();
    client.disabled_at = None;
    client.registration_source = RegistrationSource::ServerDefined;
    store.write(|tx| tx.upsert_client(&client)).expect("update");

    let fetched = store
        .read(|tx| tx.client_by_id("c1"))
        .expect("query")
        .expect("row present");
    assert_eq!(fetched.name, "Renamed");
    assert_eq!(fetched.allowed_scopes, vec!["system/*.cruds".to_string()]);
    assert_eq!(fetched.registered_at, registered_at);
    assert_eq!(fetched.disabled_at, Some(disabled_at));
    assert_eq!(
        fetched.registration_source,
        RegistrationSource::ServerDefined,
        "seeding marks the rows it owns server-defined"
    );
}
}
