authorization-server-rust/src/db/clients.rs lines 79–86 · authorization-server in the code index

list_clients returns every stored row — the migration seeds plus whatever was upserted — exactly once each, sorted by client_id, with each upserted row decoding back unchanged.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn list_clients_returns_every_row_sorted_by_id(
    upserted in prop::collection::vec(arb_client(), 0..6),
) {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    let mut expected: std::collections::BTreeMap<String, Client> = store
        .read(|tx| tx.list_clients())
        .expect("list seeds")
        .into_iter()
        .map(|c| (c.client_id.clone(), c))
        .collect();
    for client in &upserted {
        // Fresh ids only: a repeat upsert keeps the first row's
        // `registered_at` / `disabled_at` by design, which is
        // `upsert_client`'s property, not this one's.
        if !expected.contains_key(&client.client_id) {
            store.write(|tx| tx.upsert_client(client)).expect("upsert");
            expected.insert(client.client_id.clone(), client.clone());
        }
    }

    let listed = store.read(|tx| tx.list_clients()).expect("list");
    prop_assert_eq!(listed, expected.into_values().collect::<Vec<_>>());
}
}

fn main() {
fn set_client_disabled(
    &mut self,
    client_id: &str,
    disabled_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
) -> Result<bool, AuthorizationServerError> {
    let conn = &mut *self.conn;
    let updated = diesel::update(clients::table.find(client_id))
        .set(clients::disabled_at.eq(disabled_at))
        .execute(conn)
        .map_err(|e| {
            AuthorizationServerError::infrastructure("set_client_disabled failed", e)
        })?;
    Ok(updated > 0)
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/db/clients.rs lines 91–104 · authorization-server in the code index

Setting then clearing disabled_at touches only that column: every other field of the row reads back exactly as registered, and the stamp itself reads back as written at each step.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn set_client_disabled_round_trips_only_the_stamp(
    client in arb_client(),
    stamp in arb_timestamp(),
) {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    // A seeded id would keep the seed's policy on upsert; use a fresh one.
    prop_assume!(!seeded_client_ids(&store).contains(&client.client_id));
    store.write(|tx| tx.upsert_client(&client)).expect("upsert");

    prop_assert!(store.write(|tx| tx.set_client_disabled(&client.client_id, Some(stamp))).expect("disable"));
    let disabled = store.read(|tx| tx.client_by_id(&client.client_id)).expect("query").expect("row");
    prop_assert_eq!(&disabled, &Client { disabled_at: Some(stamp), ..client.clone() });

    prop_assert!(store.write(|tx| tx.set_client_disabled(&client.client_id, None)).expect("enable"));
    let enabled = store.read(|tx| tx.client_by_id(&client.client_id)).expect("query").expect("row");
    prop_assert_eq!(enabled, Client { disabled_at: None, ..client });
}
}

fn main() {
fn set_client_disabled_on_an_unknown_id_is_a_miss(
    client_id in "[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,32}",
    stamp in arb_opt_timestamp(),
) {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    let before = seeded_client_ids(&store);
    prop_assume!(!before.contains(&client_id));
    prop_assert!(!store.write(|tx| tx.set_client_disabled(&client_id, stamp)).expect("update"));
    prop_assert_eq!(seeded_client_ids(&store), before);
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/db/clients.rs lines 270–279 · authorization-server in the code index

The seeded clients

The SMART apps’ clients aren’t written by Rust: SQL migrations insert their rows. These tests are the guard that the hand-written SQL decodes as a Client. Several also pin a row to the app it registers, read from that app’s own source, so the row and the scopes the app asks for can’t drift apart unnoticed.

Every SMART client is seeded by a migration (not Rust) — the sample apps by 0003, Medications by 0004 (renamed and given its published-site redirect by 0006), the server-docs API console by 0007, the Importer by 0008, the OHIF imaging viewer by 0009 (re-seeded by 0016 on an install that skipped it), FHIR Sync for Pebble by 0017 (its Observation scope widened by 0018), Strength by 0019, Plots by 0022 (both renamed by 0035), and the Synthetic Data Loader by 0028 (which re-keys Medications, the console, the Importer and Plots to random ids, as 0025 / 0026 did Strength and the launcher, 0029 does the OHIF viewer and 0030 FHIR Sync for Pebble), and Wildflower Authorization by 0031 (the launcher’s scopes are narrowed by 0032), and 0037 puts each hosted app’s own origin in front of the redirect on wildflowerhealth.io it held — so a freshly-migrated store has them all, and every hand-written row decodes back to a valid Client. This is the guard that the SQL seeds’ JSON columns and registered_at text stay in the exact shape the store’s read path parses (a malformed value would fail client_by_id’s row mapping, not silently).

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn migrations_seed_the_smart_app_clients() {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    for client_id in [
        "growth_chart",
        "my_web_app",
        "cc344727-6f90-496c-94fd-c7829aa9a51d",
        "9769f8b274370708d0d3ebb2e3e59b7c",
        "664a01e8614050cd82ffe90350b81413",
        "03a513940b52f8c2649a5366d1a26d19",
        "165cd26573e5ac72378e6ad2d2198330",
        "941de68e6b59eb9dcc32df8ede89e636",
        "6847df97d54c31936d54ca1b36b3bb09",
        "bdf9fc5cb5a28c6683b49896b0ef8a75",
        "474e103de61f9141c4b640d59bfa130e",
        "225ba6af034a3acec6be7ff8010df67f",
        "7277e898bee8ac81ea44788236e619a5",
    ] {
        let client = store
            .read(|tx| tx.client_by_id(client_id))
            .expect("query (a decode failure surfaces here)")
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{client_id} is seeded by a clients migration"));
        assert_eq!(client.client_id, client_id);
        assert_eq!(client.kind, ClientKind::Public);
        assert!(
            client.secret_hash.is_none(),
            "{client_id} is a public client"
        );
        assert!(!client.allowed_scopes.is_empty());
        assert!(!client.redirect_uris.is_empty());
        assert!(!client.allowed_grant_types.is_empty());
    }

    // `my_web_app` (the Medication Viewer registration) carries the exact
    // scope + redirect from the review comment.
    let mwa = store
        .read(|tx| tx.client_by_id("my_web_app"))
        .unwrap()
        .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(
        mwa.allowed_scopes,
        vec![
            "launch".to_string(),
            "openid".to_string(),
            "fhirUser".to_string(),
            "patient/*.read".to_string(),
        ],
    );
    assert_eq!(
        mwa.redirect_uris[0].as_str(),

    assert_eq!(

            AllowedGrantType::RefreshToken
        ],

    // the pre-rename first-party ids are gone with `0006`, the Web Trace
    // clients with `0027`, and the ids `0028` re-keyed with it.
    for retired in [
        "medication_viewer",
        "wildflower-medication",
        "wildflower-web-trace",
        "web-trace-app",
        "web-trace-app-dev",
        "medications-app",
        "wildflower-server-docs",
        "importer-app",
        "health-viewer-app",

            "{retired} must no longer be registered",

    }

        .unwrap()

Wildflower Authorization’s client (0031) is a public PKCE client returning to the app’s published root (its own origin, added by 0037, and its path on wildflowerhealth.io), allowed exactly the scopes the app asks for (widened by 0041). Its id and scope string are read out of the app’s src/config.ts, the one place the app writes them, so the row can’t drift from it unnoticed: a scope the app asks for that the row doesn’t allow fails /oauth/authorize.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn migrations_seed_the_authorization_web_client_with_the_apps_own_scopes() {
    const AUTHORIZATION_WEB_CONFIG_TS: &str = include_str!(concat!(
        env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
        "/../../../../apps/authorization/authorization-web/src/config.ts"
    ));
    const AUTHORIZATION_WEB_CLIENT_ID: &str = "7277e898bee8ac81ea44788236e619a5";
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    let client = store
        .read(|tx| tx.client_by_id(AUTHORIZATION_WEB_CLIENT_ID))
        .expect("query (a decode failure surfaces here)")
        .expect("0031 seeds the Wildflower Authorization client");

    assert!(
        AUTHORIZATION_WEB_CONFIG_TS.contains(&format!("'{AUTHORIZATION_WEB_CLIENT_ID}'")),
        "apps/authorization/authorization-web/src/config.ts must sign in as {AUTHORIZATION_WEB_CLIENT_ID}",
    );
    let scope_string = format!("'{}'", client.allowed_scopes.join(" "));
    assert!(
        AUTHORIZATION_WEB_CONFIG_TS.contains(&scope_string),
        "apps/authorization/authorization-web/src/config.ts must request exactly {scope_string}",
    );
    assert_eq!(client.name, "Wildflower Authorization");
    assert_eq!(client.kind, ClientKind::Public);
    assert!(client.secret_hash.is_none());
    assert_eq!(client.disabled_at, None);
    assert_eq!(
        client.redirect_uris,

                .expect("a valid absolute redirect"),

                .expect("a valid absolute redirect"),
        ],
    );
    assert_eq!(
        client.allowed_scopes,
        vec![
            "openid".to_string(),
            "wildflower/Grant.rd".to_string(),

        client.allowed_grant_types,

            AllowedGrantType::RefreshToken,

authorization-server-rust/src/db/clients.rs lines 906–940 · authorization-server in the code index

The App Catalog publishes each Wildflower Health app’s OAuth client registration as its HALO preassignedCredentials, for a server that registers the app itself. Every Wildflower Health entry carrying the object must match its seeded client: a public client with no secret, the same scopes and grant types, every redirect it lists registered, and a smart-app’s launchUrl among them, since its launch page is where it returns to. The seeded row is the source of truth, so a migration that changes one fails here until the catalog follows.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn app_catalog_preassigns_wildflower_health_clients_as_seeded() {
    const APP_CATALOG_JSON: &str = include_str!(concat!(
        env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
        "/../../../../apps/app-catalog/app-catalog-web/public/apps.json"
    ));
    // The catalog's id for Wildflower Health, the publisher of every app
    // whose client the migrations seed. Another publisher's credentials are
    // that publisher's to keep, so they are not checked here.
    const WILDFLOWER_HEALTH_PUBLISHER_ID: &str = "5a3385ad-9a2b-4dc6-85a0-5b874da0b019";
    let catalog: Vec<AppCatalogEntry> =
        serde_json::from_str(APP_CATALOG_JSON).expect("apps.json decodes as catalog entries");
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    let mut checked = 0;
    for entry in catalog {
        if entry.publisher.id != WILDFLOWER_HEALTH_PUBLISHER_ID {
            continue;
        }
        let Some(credentials) = entry.preassigned_credentials else {
            continue;
        };
        let name = entry.name;
        let client_id = credentials.client_id;
        let client = store
            .read(|tx| tx.client_by_id(&client_id))
            .expect("query (a decode failure surfaces here)")
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{name}: {client_id} is seeded by a clients migration"));

        assert_eq!(client.kind, ClientKind::Public, "{name}");
        assert!(client.secret_hash.is_none(), "{name}");
        assert_eq!(credentials.token_endpoint_auth_method, "none", "{name}");
        assert_eq!(entry.scopes, client.allowed_scopes, "{name}: scopes");
        assert_eq!(
            credentials.grant_types, client.allowed_grant_types,
            "{name}: grantTypes"
        );
        for redirect in &credentials.redirect_uris {
            assert!(
                client.redirect_uris.contains(redirect),
                "{name}: {redirect} is not registered for {client_id}",
            );
        }
        if let Some(launch_url) = &entry.launch_url {
            assert!(
                client.redirect_uris.contains(launch_url),
                "{name}: its launchUrl {launch_url} is not registered for {client_id}",
            );
        }
        checked += 1;
    }
    assert!(
        checked > 0,
        "apps.json preassigns none of Wildflower Health's seeded clients"
    );
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/db/clients.rs lines 845–898 · authorization-server in the code index

Browser Sessions

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/db/browser_sessions.rs

Two tables hold what the server knows about the browsers it has let in. browser_sessions holds one row per browser session, keyed by its sid, read back as a BrowserSession, one field to one column of the same name. scopes is compact JSON text through the shared JsonStrings; kind is its wire string, same_device or paired, which a CHECK on the column also enforces.

A session’s row outlives the session. Revoking it stamps revoked_at and keeps the row, because the token verifier and a refresh look the sid up to refuse what the session minted. The row goes only in the retention sweep, purge_expired, with the cutoff now less BROWSER_SESSION_RETENTION.

session_shortfall_acknowledgements records, per session, the apps it has gone on past its limited page for. Its primary key is the pair (sid, client_id), so a pair is recorded at most once and a lookup by the pair is a key lookup. Neither table carries a foreign key: sid here, and on the requests, codes and refresh families that record it, is a soft reference the retention sweep keeps tidy.

The tests open a store with store.

authorization-server-rust/src/db/browser_sessions.rs lines 113–130 · authorization-server in the code index

A started session round-trips through the table, and revoking it stamps it once: a second revoke keeps the first instant and reports false. It reads as revoked once revoked, and so does a sid with no row.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn a_session_round_trips_and_is_revoked_once() {
    let store = store();
    let now = chrono::Utc::now();
    let session = BrowserSession::new_same_device_session(
        vec!["system/*.cruds".to_owned(), "wildflower/*.cruds".to_owned()],
        Duration::hours(8),
        now,
    );
    store
        .write(|tx| tx.insert_browser_session(&session))
        .expect("insert");
    assert_eq!(
        store
            .read(|tx| tx.browser_session_by_sid(&session.sid))
            .expect("read"),
        Some(session.clone())
    );
    assert!(store
        .read(|tx| tx.browser_session_by_sid("no-such-sid"))
        .expect("read")
        .is_none());
    assert!(!store
        .read(|tx| tx.is_browser_session_revoked(&session.sid))
        .expect("read"));
    assert!(store
        .read(|tx| tx.is_browser_session_revoked("no-such-sid"))
        .expect("read"));

    let revoked_at = now + Duration::minutes(1);
    assert!(store
        .write(|tx| tx.revoke_browser_session(&session.sid, revoked_at))
        .expect("revoke"));
    assert!(!store
        .write(|tx| tx.revoke_browser_session(&session.sid, revoked_at + Duration::minutes(1)))
        .expect("second revoke"));
    let stored = store
        .read(|tx| tx.browser_session_by_sid(&session.sid))
        .expect("read")
        .expect("still there");
    assert_eq!(stored.revoked_at, Some(revoked_at));
    assert!(store
        .read(|tx| tx.is_browser_session_revoked(&session.sid))
        .expect("read"));
    assert!(!store
        .write(|tx| tx.revoke_browser_session("no-such-sid", now))
        .expect("revoke"));
}
}

fn main() {
fn live_sessions_are_the_unrevoked_unexpired_ones_newest_first() {
    let store = store();
    let now = chrono::Utc::now();
    let older = BrowserSession::new_same_device_session(

        vec![],

        store
            .write(|tx| tx.insert_browser_session(session))
            .expect("insert");
    }
    store
        .write(|tx| tx.revoke_browser_session(&revoked.sid, now))
        .expect("revoke");

    let live: Vec<String> = store
        .read(|tx| tx.live_browser_sessions(now))
        .expect("read")
        .into_iter()
        .map(|session| session.sid)
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(live, vec![newer.sid, older.sid]);

fn main() {
fn expiring_a_session_moves_its_expiry_back_to_now() {
    let store = store();
    let now = chrono::Utc::now();
    let live = BrowserSession::new_same_device_session(vec![], Duration::hours(8), now);
    let expired = BrowserSession::new_same_device_session(

            .write(|tx| tx.insert_browser_session(session))

        .write(|tx| tx.expire_browser_session(&live.sid, expired_at))
        .expect("expire"));

        .write(|tx| tx.expire_browser_session(&expired.sid, expired_at))

        .write(|tx| tx.expire_browser_session("no-such-sid", expired_at))
        .expect("expire a missing one"));

                .expect("read"),
            Some(BrowserSession {

When the server accepts a session’s cookie it passes seen_before as seen_at less LAST_SEEN_RESOLUTION, so the column moves at most once per window, and never backwards. A refresh family rotating passes seen_at as seen_before, so it moves the column unless the column is already later.

A touch moves last_seen_at only when it was last seen before the guard, so a second touch inside the window and a touch from the past leave it; a sid with no row moves nothing.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn a_touch_moves_last_seen_only_past_the_guard() {
    let store = store();
    let signed_in_at = chrono::Utc::now();
    let session =
        BrowserSession::new_same_device_session(vec![], Duration::hours(8), signed_in_at);
    store
        .write(|tx| tx.insert_browser_session(&session))
        .expect("insert");
    let last_seen = |store: &SqliteGrantStore| {
        store
            .read(|tx| tx.browser_session_by_sid(&session.sid))
            .expect("read")
            .expect("stored")
            .last_seen_at
    };

    let seen_at = signed_in_at + Duration::minutes(6);
    assert!(store
        .write(|tx| tx.touch_browser_session_last_seen(
            &session.sid,
            seen_at,
            seen_at - Duration::minutes(5)
        ))
        .expect("touch"));
    assert_eq!(last_seen(&store), seen_at);

    let soon_after = seen_at + Duration::minutes(1);
    assert!(!store
        .write(|tx| tx.touch_browser_session_last_seen(
            &session.sid,
            soon_after,
            soon_after - Duration::minutes(5)
        ))
        .expect("touch inside the window"));
    assert!(!store
        .write(|tx| tx.touch_browser_session_last_seen(
            &session.sid,
            signed_in_at,
            signed_in_at
        ))
        .expect("touch from the past"));
    assert_eq!(last_seen(&store), seen_at);
    assert!(!store
        .write(|tx| tx.touch_browser_session_last_seen("no-such-sid", soon_after, soon_after))
        .expect("touch"));
}
}

delete_browser_sessions_ended_before

The prune test keeps sessions alive with refresh families built by family.

Delete every browser session that expired or was revoked before cutoff and that no refresh-token family alive at cutoff names, returning how many went, and with them every limited-page acknowledgement whose session is gone. A family that outlives its session’s expiry keeps the row, so its refresh still finds the session it was minted under. The family probe is correlated on sid, so refresh_token_families_sid_idx answers it.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn delete_browser_sessions_ended_before(
    &mut self,
    cutoff: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<usize, AuthorizationServerError> {
    let conn = &mut *self.conn;
    let named_by_a_family_alive_at_cutoff = exists(
        refresh_token_families::table
            .filter(refresh_token_families::sid.eq(browser_sessions::sid.nullable()))
            .filter(refresh_token_families::expires_at.ge(cutoff)),
    );
    let pruned = diesel::delete(
        browser_sessions::table
            .filter(
                browser_sessions::expires_at
                    .lt(cutoff)
                    .or(browser_sessions::revoked_at.lt(cutoff)),
            )
            .filter(not(named_by_a_family_alive_at_cutoff)),
    )
    .execute(conn)
    .map_err(|e| {
        AuthorizationServerError::infrastructure(
            "delete_browser_sessions_ended_before failed",
            e,
        )
    })?;
    diesel::delete(session_shortfall_acknowledgements::table.filter(
        not(exists(browser_sessions::table.filter(
            browser_sessions::sid.eq(session_shortfall_acknowledgements::sid),
        ))),
    ))
    .execute(conn)
    .map_err(|e| {
        AuthorizationServerError::infrastructure(
            "delete session_shortfall_acknowledgements without a session failed",
            e,
        )
    })?;
    Ok(pruned)
}
}

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn the_prune_takes_only_sessions_ended_before_the_cutoff_that_no_live_family_names() {
    let store = store();
    let now = chrono::Utc::now();
    let cutoff = now - Duration::hours(24);
    let session = |created_at| {
        BrowserSession::new_same_device_session(vec![], Duration::hours(8), created_at)
    };
    let expired_long_ago = session(now - Duration::days(3));
    // Still unexpired, but revoked a day and more ago.
    let revoked_long_ago = BrowserSession::new_same_device_session(
        vec![],
        Duration::hours(48),
        now - Duration::hours(30),
    );
    let expired_recently = session(now - Duration::hours(10));
    let named_by_a_live_family = session(now - Duration::days(3));
    let named_by_a_dead_family = session(now - Duration::days(3));
    for session in [
        &expired_long_ago,
        &revoked_long_ago,
        &expired_recently,
        &named_by_a_live_family,
        &named_by_a_dead_family,
    ] {
        store
            .write(|tx| tx.insert_browser_session(session))
            .expect("insert");
    }
    store
        .write(|tx| tx.revoke_browser_session(&revoked_long_ago.sid, now - Duration::hours(29)))
        .expect("revoke");
    store
        .write(|tx| {
            tx.insert_refresh_token_family_row(&family(
                "live",
                &named_by_a_live_family.sid,
                now + Duration::days(30),
            ))?;
            tx.insert_refresh_token_family_row(&family(
                "dead",
                &named_by_a_dead_family.sid,
                now - Duration::days(2),
            ))
        })
        .expect("families");
    store
        .write(|tx| {
            tx.record_session_shortfall_acknowledgement(&expired_long_ago.sid, "app")?;
            tx.record_session_shortfall_acknowledgement(&expired_recently.sid, "app")
        })
        .expect("acknowledgements");

    let pruned = store
        .write(|tx| tx.delete_browser_sessions_ended_before(cutoff))
        .expect("prune");

    assert_eq!(pruned, 3);
    for (session, kept) in [
        (&expired_long_ago, false),
        (&revoked_long_ago, false),
        (&expired_recently, true),
        (&named_by_a_live_family, true),
        (&named_by_a_dead_family, false),
    ] {
        assert_eq!(
            store
                .read(|tx| tx.browser_session_by_sid(&session.sid))
                .expect("read")
                .is_some(),
            kept,
            "session created {}",
            session.created_at
        );
    }
    for (session, kept) in [(&expired_long_ago, false), (&expired_recently, true)] {
        assert_eq!(
            store
                .read(|tx| tx.is_session_shortfall_acknowledged_for_client(&session.sid, "app"))
                .expect("read"),
            kept,
            "acknowledgement of the session created {}",
            session.created_at
        );
    }
}

Authorization Requests

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/db/authorization_requests/mod.rs

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/db/authorization_requests/code_request_row.rs

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/db/authorization_requests/user_code_request_row.rs

The authorization requests live in two tables, by how a request is keyed. code_authorization_requests holds the code requests, keyed by id. user_code_requests holds the device requests and browser pairings, keyed by the poller’s secret, found by the user_code the Owner enters, and told apart by a flow column. Only this module knows those two flows share a table.

A decision lands once. Every write of a transition is the flow’s guarded replace: one UPDATE of the whole row, guarded on the key and the status the request was read with, so of two transitions read from one row the first to land wins and the other matches nothing (the guarded replace). At most one pending request holds a user_code: a partial unique index holds it, and a request decided or claimed is outside the index.

A row is checked against its flow and status on the way in. Each table’s row type reads into the flow’s struct through one conversion, the one place the columns are held against the flow and status; the table’s CHECKs refuse the same rows on write. A row whose approval disagrees with its status, or that lacks a column its flow requires, fails the read as malformed rather than reading as absent.

The tests’ requests are built by the helpers on the Test Fixtures page.

db::authorization_requests::code_request_row

CodeAuthorizationRequestRow

One code_authorization_requests row, one field per column of the same name. Every column a CodeRequest always has is NOT NULL. The approval is granted_scopes and patient, set only while the request is approved; the table’s CHECKs hold it to that, and to a status the code flow has. No foreign key ties client_id to clients or sid to browser_sessions: an app trusted on first use has no clients row yet, and a session is pruned on its own schedule.

fn main() {
pub(super) struct CodeAuthorizationRequestRow {
    /// The primary key: the request's UUID, so every read and write by id is
    /// a key lookup. An authorization code names its request by it.
    pub(super) id: String,
    /// The client that made the request.
    client_id: String,
    /// The scopes the client asked for, as a JSON array.
    requested_scopes: JsonStrings,
    /// When the request started; the Owner prompt orders by it.
    requested_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    /// When the request stops waiting for a decision. The retention sweep
    /// deletes a row by it, whatever its status.
    expires_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    /// Where the request stands, as its wire string: `awaiting_limited_page`,
    /// `pending`, `approved` or `denied`. A replace lands only on a row still
    /// at the status it was read with. Expiry is read from `expires_at`, never
    /// stored here.
    status: RequestStatus,
    /// The approved scopes, as a JSON array: set exactly while `status` is
    /// `approved`.
    granted_scopes: Option<JsonStrings>,
    /// The patient the approval binds, if any; only ever set beside
    /// `granted_scopes`.
    patient: Option<String>,
    /// The redirect the client presented, which its code or error goes back to.
    redirect_uri: UrlText,
    /// The PKCE S256 challenge the code's redemption is checked against.
    code_challenge: String,
    /// The `state` the client sent, which its callback carries back.

    /// The browser session the request was made in, which its code is issued

    sid: String,

    /// plain OAuth request.
    launch: Option<String>,
    /// The patient the consumed launch binds, if any, which an approval must
    /// name.
    launch_bound_patient: Option<String>,
    /// The requested scopes a standing grant already covered when the request

    pre_approved_scopes: JsonStrings,
    /// Whether the browser that made the request can decide it itself; raising
    /// the request for the Owner clears it.
    decidable_in_requesting_browser: bool,
}
}

fn main() {
fn try_from(mut row: CodeAuthorizationRequestRow) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
    let approval = approval_from_columns(
        row.status,
        row.granted_scopes.take(),
        row.patient.take(),
        |problem| row.malformed(problem),
    )?;
    let state = match (row.status, approval) {
        (RequestStatus::AwaitingLimitedPage, None) => CodeRequestState::AwaitingLimitedPage,
        (RequestStatus::Pending, None) => CodeRequestState::Pending,
        (RequestStatus::Approved, Some(approval)) => CodeRequestState::Approved(approval),
        (RequestStatus::Denied, None) => CodeRequestState::Denied,
        (status, _) => {
            return Err(row.malformed(&format!("is {status}, which its flow never is")));
        }
    };
    Ok(CodeRequest {
        id: row.id,
        client_id: row.client_id,
        requested_scopes: row.requested_scopes.0,
        requested_at: row.requested_at,
        expires_at: row.expires_at,
        state,
        redirect_uri: row.redirect_uri.0,
        code_challenge: row.code_challenge,
        client_state: row.client_state,
        sid: row.sid,
        launch: row.launch,
        launch_bound_patient: row.launch_bound_patient,
        pre_approved_scopes: row.pre_approved_scopes.0,
        decidable_in_requesting_browser: row.decidable_in_requesting_browser,
    })
}
}

UserCodeRequestRow

One user_code_requests row, one field per column of the same name. A browser pairing keeps its browser’s name in device_name, the column the device page reads a requester’s name from. The approval is granted_scopes and patient, set only while the request is approved or claimed; the table’s CHECKs hold it to that, to a status these flows have, and a pairing to a name and no patient.

Two indexes on user_code serve the device page: a plain one for its lookups by the code the Owner types or confirms, and user_code_requests_pending_user_code_uidx, unique where status is pending, so at most one pending request holds a user code. Decided and claimed rows are outside it, so they may share a code with each other and with one pending request.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn take_state<A>(
    &mut self,
    into_flow_approval: impl FnOnce(&Self, Approval) -> Result<A, AuthorizationServerError>,
) -> Result<PolledState<A>, AuthorizationServerError> {
    let approval = approval_from_columns(
        self.status,
        self.granted_scopes.take(),
        self.patient.take(),
        |problem| self.malformed(problem),
    )?;
    match (self.status, approval) {
        (RequestStatus::Pending, None) => Ok(PolledState::Pending),
        (RequestStatus::Denied, None) => Ok(PolledState::Denied),
        (RequestStatus::Approved, Some(approval)) => {
            Ok(PolledState::Approved(into_flow_approval(self, approval)?))
        }
        (RequestStatus::Claimed, Some(approval)) => {
            Ok(PolledState::Claimed(into_flow_approval(self, approval)?))
        }
        (status, _) => Err(self.malformed(&format!("is {status}, which its flow never is"))),
    }
}
}

db::authorization_requests

approval_from_columns

Both conversions read the approval through it.

The approval a row’s granted_scopes and patient columns hold: present exactly when status is approved or claimed, and a patient only beside granted scopes. Any other combination is malformed.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn approval_from_columns(
    status: RequestStatus,
    granted_scopes: Option<JsonStrings>,
    patient: Option<String>,
    malformed: impl FnOnce(&str) -> AuthorizationServerError,
) -> Result<Option<Approval>, AuthorizationServerError> {
    let carries_approval = matches!(status, RequestStatus::Approved | RequestStatus::Claimed);
    match (granted_scopes, patient) {
        (Some(granted_scopes), patient) if carries_approval => Ok(Some(Approval {
            granted_scopes: granted_scopes.0,
            patient,
        })),
        (None, None) if !carries_approval => Ok(None),
        _ => Err(malformed(&format!(
            "is {status} but its approval columns disagree"
        ))),
    }
}
}

A row whose approval columns disagree with its status, in a status its flow never has, or with a column its flow requires missing, is refused by the schema’s CHECKs; and if one were there anyway, it fails the read as malformed rather than reading as absent.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn a_malformed_row_fails_the_read() {
    for (id, tamper) in [
        (
            "req-1",
            "UPDATE code_authorization_requests SET status = 'approved' WHERE id = 'req-1'",
        ),
        (
            "req-1",
            "UPDATE code_authorization_requests SET granted_scopes = '[]' WHERE id = 'req-1'",
        ),
        (
            "req-1",
            "UPDATE code_authorization_requests SET patient = 'Patient/1' WHERE id = 'req-1'",
        ),
        (
            "req-1",
            "UPDATE code_authorization_requests SET status = 'claimed', granted_scopes = '[]' \
             WHERE id = 'req-1'",
        ),
        (
            "dev-1",
            "UPDATE user_code_requests SET status = 'awaiting_limited_page' WHERE id = 'dev-1'",
        ),
        (
            "dev-1",
            "UPDATE user_code_requests SET flow = 'authorization_code' WHERE id = 'dev-1'",
        ),
        (
            "dev-1",
            "UPDATE user_code_requests SET flow = 'browser_pairing' WHERE id = 'dev-1'",
        ),
        (
            "dev-1",
            "UPDATE user_code_requests SET flow = 'browser_pairing', \
             status = 'approved', granted_scopes = '[]', patient = 'Patient/1', \
             device_name = 'Laptop' WHERE id = 'dev-1'",
        ),
        (
            "dev-1",
            "UPDATE user_code_requests SET status = 'approved' WHERE id = 'dev-1'",
        ),
    ] {
        let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
        insert_code(&store, &code_request("req-1", false));
        insert_device(&store, &device_request("dev-1"));
        let mut conn = store.pool().get().expect("check out a connection");
        assert!(
            diesel::sql_query(tamper).execute(&mut conn).is_err(),
            "the schema refuses {tamper}"
        );
        drop(conn);
        execute_unchecked(&store, tamper);
        assert!(
            store.read(|tx| tx.authorization_request_by_id(id)).is_err(),
            "{tamper}"
        );
    }
}
}

Inserting a request

Bulk reclamation of expired rows is the retention sweep’s, so an insert leaves an unrelated expired row alone. The one row it clears is an expired pending one holding the new request’s user_code, which would otherwise hold the slot in the partial unique index.

Insert a user-code request’s row, first clearing an already-expired pending row holding its user_code (as of the request’s start): that row occupies the partial unique index the insert would otherwise collide with. Bulk reclamation is the retention sweep’s; see authorization-server-rust/docs/Book/Domain/Retention Explanation.md.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn insert_user_code_row(
    &mut self,
    row: &UserCodeRequestRow,
) -> Result<(), AuthorizationServerError> {
    diesel::delete(
        user_code_requests::table
            .filter(user_code_requests::user_code.eq(&row.user_code))
            .filter(user_code_requests::status.eq(RequestStatus::Pending))
            .filter(user_code_requests::expires_at.lt(row.requested_at)),
    )
    .execute(self.conn)
    .map_err(failed("insert_user_code_row failed"))?;
    diesel::insert_into(user_code_requests::table)
        .values(row)
        .execute(self.conn)
        .map_err(failed("insert_user_code_row failed"))?;
    Ok(())
}
}

) -> Result<bool, AuthorizationServerError> {
    if changed.id != read.id {
        return Err(replaced_by_another(&read.id, &changed.id));
    }
    let affected = diesel::update(
        code_authorization_requests::table
            .find(&read.id)
            .filter(code_authorization_requests::status.eq(read.state.status())),
    )
    .set(CodeAuthorizationRequestRow::from(changed))
    .execute(self.conn)
    .map_err(failed("replace_authorization_request failed"))?;
    Ok(affected == 1)
}
}

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn a_replace_lands_only_while_the_row_has_the_status_it_was_read_with() {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    let now = Utc::now();
    let read = device_request("dev-1");

        .approve(approval, Some("Kitchen iPad".to_owned()), now)
        .expect("approves");

        .write(|tx| tx.replace_device_request(&read, &approved))
        .expect("replace"));

    );

    assert!(
        !store
            .write(|tx| tx.replace_device_request(&read, &denied))
            .expect("replace"),

    );
    assert_eq!(
        stored(&store, "dev-1"),

authorization-server-rust/src/db/authorization_requests/mod.rs lines 923–947 · authorization-server in the code index

owner_prompt

The one request the host notifies about and opens: the Owner prompt.

Two reads, the newest candidate from each table, keeping the later by requested_at (on a tie, the code request; within a table, the greater id). The client’s name comes from its registration through a left join: a client trusted on first use has none until the Owner approves it. A disabled client’s request is skipped, a client with no row’s kept (the rule on OwnerPrompt). Only pending rows are candidates, so a code request still on its browser’s limited page is none.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn owner_prompt(
    &mut self,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<Option<OwnerPrompt>, AuthorizationServerError> {
    let code = self.newest_pending_code_request(now)?;
    let polled = self.newest_pending_user_code_request(now)?;
    Ok(
        later_of(code, polled).map(|(request, registered_client_name)| {
            OwnerPrompt::for_request(&request, registered_client_name)
        }),
    )
}
}

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn newest_pending_code_request(
    &mut self,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<Option<PromptCandidate>, AuthorizationServerError> {
    code_authorization_requests::table
        .left_join(
            clients::table.on(clients::client_id.eq(code_authorization_requests::client_id)),
        )
        .filter(code_authorization_requests::status.eq(RequestStatus::Pending))
        .filter(code_authorization_requests::expires_at.gt(now))
        .filter(clients::disabled_at.is_null())
        .order((
            code_authorization_requests::requested_at.desc(),
            code_authorization_requests::id.desc(),
        ))
        .select((
            CodeAuthorizationRequestRow::as_select(),
            clients::name.nullable(),
        ))
        .first::<(CodeAuthorizationRequestRow, Option<String>)>(self.conn)
        .optional()
        .map_err(failed("owner_prompt failed"))?
        .map(|(row, registered_client_name)| {
            Ok((
                AuthorizationRequest::Code(CodeRequest::try_from(row)?),
                registered_client_name,
            ))
        })
        .transpose()
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/db/authorization_requests/mod.rs lines 202–226 · authorization-server in the code index

Of the newest pending code request and the newest pending user-code request, the later by requested_at; on a tie, the code request.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn later_of(
    code: Option<PromptCandidate>,
    polled: Option<PromptCandidate>,
) -> Option<PromptCandidate> {
    match (code, polled) {
        (Some(code), Some(polled)) if polled.0.requested_at() > code.0.requested_at() => {
            Some(polled)
        }
        (Some(code), _) => Some(code),
        (None, polled) => polled,
    }
}
}

is_awaiting_owner

Whether the consent the host holds open is still undecided.

The request by the key consent_key carries, then its client’s disabled_at, both within the caller’s scope.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn is_awaiting_owner(
    &mut self,
    consent_key: &ConsentKey,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<bool, AuthorizationServerError> {
    let request = match consent_key {
        ConsentKey::DeviceCode { user_code } | ConsentKey::BrowserPairing { user_code } => self
            .pending_polled_request_by_user_code(user_code)?
            .map(AuthorizationRequest::from),
        ConsentKey::AuthorizationCode { id } => {
            self.code_request_by_id(id)?.map(AuthorizationRequest::Code)
        }
    };
    match request {
        Some(request) if request.is_undecided_at(now) => {
            Ok(!self.is_client_disabled(request.client_id())?)
        }
        _ => Ok(false),
    }
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/db/authorization_requests/mod.rs lines 336–355 · authorization-server in the code index

A request awaits the Owner until it is decided or expires, and a code request still on its browser’s limited page counts as undecided, as it waits there.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn a_request_awaits_the_owner_until_it_is_decided_or_expires() {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    let now = Utc::now();
    for (id, status, expires_at) in [
        (
            "waiting",
            RequestStatus::Pending,
            now + Duration::minutes(5),
        ),
        (
            "on-limited-page",
            RequestStatus::AwaitingLimitedPage,
            now + Duration::minutes(5),
        ),
        ("stale", RequestStatus::Pending, now - Duration::minutes(1)),
        (
            "approved",
            RequestStatus::Approved,
            now + Duration::minutes(5),
        ),
        ("denied", RequestStatus::Denied, now + Duration::minutes(5)),
    ] {
        store
            .write(|tx| tx.insert_code_request(&code_request(id, status, expires_at)))
            .unwrap();
    }
    store
        .write(|tx| {
            tx.insert_device_request(&device_request(
                "device-waiting",
                "ABCD-EFGH",
                RequestStatus::Pending,
            ))
        })
        .unwrap();
    store
        .write(|tx| {
            tx.insert_device_request(&device_request(
                "device-denied",
                "WXYZ-WXYZ",
                RequestStatus::Denied,
            ))
        })
        .unwrap();

    let pending = |key: ConsentKey| awaiting(&store, &key, now);
    assert!(pending(oauth("waiting")));
    assert!(pending(oauth("on-limited-page")));
    assert!(pending(device("ABCD-EFGH")));
    assert!(!pending(oauth("stale")));
    assert!(!pending(oauth("approved")));
    assert!(!pending(oauth("denied")));
    assert!(!pending(device("WXYZ-WXYZ")));
    assert!(!pending(oauth("ghost")));
    assert!(!pending(device("GHST-GHST")));
    assert!(!pending(oauth("device-waiting")));
}
}

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn delete_expired_requests_respects_the_cutoff() {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    let now = Utc::now();
    let old = now - Duration::days(10);
    insert_device(
        &store,
        &device_request_at("old", "UC-OLD", old, Duration::minutes(5)),
    );
    insert_device(
        &store,
        &device_with_status(
            device_request_at("old-claimed", "UC-CLAIMED", old, Duration::minutes(5)),
            RequestStatus::Claimed,
        ),
    );
    insert_device(&store, &device_request("recent"));
    insert_code(
        &store,
        &CodeRequest::new(
            NewCodeRequestArgs {
                ttl: Duration::minutes(5),
                ..fixture_code_args("old-code", "app", vec!["read".to_owned()])
            },
            old,
        ),
    );
    insert_code(&store, &code_request("recent-code", false));
    let cutoff = now - Duration::days(7);
    let deleted_polled = store
        .write(|tx| tx.delete_polled_requests_expired_before(cutoff))
        .expect("delete");
    assert_eq!(deleted_polled, 2);
    assert!(stored(&store, "old").is_none());
    assert!(stored(&store, "old-claimed").is_none());
    assert!(stored(&store, "recent").is_some());
    assert!(stored(&store, "old-code").is_some(), "another table's");
    let deleted_code = store
        .write(|tx| tx.delete_code_requests_expired_before(cutoff))
        .expect("delete");
    assert_eq!(deleted_code, 1);
    assert!(stored(&store, "old-code").is_none());
    assert!(stored(&store, "recent-code").is_some());
}
}

Launch Contexts

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/db/launch_contexts.rs

The launch_contexts table holds one row per SMART launch value the server hands out: a launch context, keyed by the value itself, the nonce, kept in plain text since it lives five minutes and is good for one use. The LaunchContext domain type is the row. A NULL client_id is a launch any app may consume, and the table’s CHECK (patient IS NULL OR client_id IS NOT NULL) refuses a patient on such a launch. A launch is minted in-process, and /oauth/authorize consumes it once. No other slice of the host reads or writes the table.

Every test opens its own store with store.

db::launch_contexts

impl LaunchContextsTx for SqliteGrantTx

The port is LaunchContextsTx.

fn main() {
fn insert_launch_context(
    &mut self,
    context: &LaunchContext,
) -> Result<(), AuthorizationServerError> {
    let conn = &mut *self.conn;
    diesel::insert_into(launch_contexts::table)
        .values(context.clone())
        .execute(conn)
        .map_err(|e| {
            AuthorizationServerError::infrastructure("insert_launch_context failed", e)
        })?;
    Ok(())
}

authorization-server-rust/src/db/launch_contexts.rs lines 32–44 · authorization-server in the code index

consume_launch_context

A consume that matches nothing changes nothing, so a launch presented by the wrong app stays consumable by its own.

Stamp the launch nonce consumed at now and return it, iff it was minted for client_id or for any client, is unconsumed, and is unexpired at now; otherwise None and nothing changes. One conditional UPDATE … RETURNING, so the check and the stamp are a single statement under SQLite’s write lock: of two racing authorizes presenting the same nonce, exactly one gets the row.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn consume_launch_context(
    &mut self,
    nonce: &str,
    client_id: &str,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<Option<LaunchContext>, AuthorizationServerError> {
    let conn = &mut *self.conn;
    diesel::update(
        launch_contexts::table
            .find(nonce)
            .filter(
                launch_contexts::client_id
                    .eq(client_id)
                    .or(launch_contexts::client_id.is_null()),
            )
            .filter(launch_contexts::consumed_at.is_null())
            .filter(launch_contexts::expires_at.gt(now)),
    )
    .set(launch_contexts::consumed_at.eq(now))
    .returning(LaunchContext::as_returning())
    .get_result(conn)
    .optional()
    .map_err(|e| AuthorizationServerError::infrastructure("consume_launch_context failed", e))
}
}

A minted context round-trips through the table: the consume returns the row exactly as inserted, now stamped consumed.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn a_minted_context_round_trips_through_its_consume() {
    let store = store();
    let now = chrono::Utc::now();
    let context =
        LaunchContext::for_client("nonce-1".to_owned(), "app", Some("pat-1".to_owned()), now);
    store
        .write(|tx| tx.insert_launch_context(&context))
        .expect("insert");

    let consumed_at = now + Duration::seconds(1);
    let consumed = store
        .write(|tx| tx.consume_launch_context("nonce-1", "app", consumed_at))
        .expect("consume")
        .expect("live context");
    let mut expected = context;
    expected.consumed_at = Some(consumed_at);
    assert_eq!(consumed, expected);
}
}

Single use: the second consume of the same nonce finds nothing.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn a_context_is_consumed_once() {
    let store = store();
    let now = chrono::Utc::now();
    store
        .write(|tx| {
            tx.insert_launch_context(&LaunchContext::for_client(
                "nonce-1".to_owned(),
                "app",
                None,
                now,
            ))
        })
        .expect("insert");
    let consume = || {
        store
            .write(|tx| tx.consume_launch_context("nonce-1", "app", now))
            .expect("consume")
    };
    assert!(consume().is_some(), "the first consume wins");
    assert!(consume().is_none(), "a replay finds nothing");
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/db/launch_contexts.rs lines 223–238 · authorization-server in the code index

Against the table, a refused consume says why: unknown, another client’s (checked first, so its state is never told), already used, or expired. Another client’s attempt leaves the launch consumable by its own.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn a_refused_consume_says_why() {
    let store = store();
    let launch_contexts = LaunchContexts::new(store.clone());
    let consume = |nonce: &str, client_id: &str, at| {
        store.write(|tx| consume_launch(tx, nonce, client_id, at))
    };
    let now = chrono::Utc::now();
    let expired_at = now + LAUNCH_CONTEXT_TTL;
    launch_contexts
        .mint("app", "live".to_owned(), now)
        .expect("mint live");
    launch_contexts
        .mint("app", "used".to_owned(), now)
        .expect("mint used");
    consume("used", "app", now)
        .expect("consume")
        .expect("its own client consumes it");

    for (nonce, client_id, at, refusal) in [
        ("forged", "app", now, LaunchRefusal::Unknown),
        ("live", "other-app", now, LaunchRefusal::ForAnotherApp),
        ("used", "other-app", now, LaunchRefusal::ForAnotherApp),
        (
            "live",
            "other-app",
            expired_at,
            LaunchRefusal::ForAnotherApp,
        ),
        ("used", "app", now, LaunchRefusal::AlreadyUsed),
        ("live", "app", expired_at, LaunchRefusal::Expired),
    ] {
        assert_eq!(
            consume(nonce, client_id, at).expect("consume"),
            Err(refusal),
            "{nonce} by {client_id}"
        );
    }
    assert!(
        consume("live", "app", now).expect("consume").is_ok(),
        "the refusals left the live launch consumable by its own client"
    );
}
}

The prune deletes contexts expired at or before now, consumed or not, and keeps live ones.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn the_prune_deletes_only_expired_contexts() {
    let store = store();
    let now = chrono::Utc::now();
    let expired_at = now - LAUNCH_CONTEXT_TTL;
    store
        .write(|tx| {
            tx.insert_launch_context(&LaunchContext::for_client(
                "expired".to_owned(),
                "app",
                None,
                expired_at,
            ))?;
            let mut expired_consumed = LaunchContext::for_client(
                "expired-consumed".to_owned(),
                "app",
                None,
                expired_at,
            );
            expired_consumed.consumed_at = Some(expired_at);
            tx.insert_launch_context(&expired_consumed)?;
            tx.insert_launch_context(&LaunchContext::for_client(
                "live".to_owned(),
                "app",
                None,
                now,
            ))
        })
        .expect("insert");
    let pruned = store
        .write(|tx| tx.delete_launch_contexts_expired_by(now))
        .expect("prune");
    assert_eq!(pruned, 2);
    assert!(store
        .write(|tx| tx.consume_launch_context("live", "app", now))
        .expect("consume")
        .is_some());
}
}

Grants

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/db/grants/mod.rs

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/db/grants/general.rs

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/db/grants/authorization_code.rs

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/db/grants/device.rs

A grant is the Owner’s standing yes, and it comes in two kinds. The store keeps one table per kind, authorization_code_grants and device_grants, each carrying every column its kind needs. A write or a keyed lookup of one kind is one statement on one table, and the store never has to keep a parent row and a child row in step.

Each table’s identity is a unique key declared in the schema. (client_id, redirect_uri) holds code grants to one standing consent per app per redirect URI, so two approvals racing to insert can’t both succeed; (client_id, device_name) holds device grants to one pairing per app per device name.

The Owner’s list and the lookup by id span both kinds. Those read a grants view, a UNION ALL of the two tables that tags each row with its kind and leaves the other kind’s own column NULL. Grant ids are UUIDs minted when the grant is first recorded, so an id names at most one row across both tables.

db::grants

Each GrantsTx method on SqliteGrantTx is one line handing its connection to a statement below, in its kind’s file or, when it spans both kinds, in general.

db::grants::general

GrantViewRow

A row off the grants VIEW: the shared columns, the kind tag, and each kind’s payload column (NULL for the other kind). TryFrom repacks it into the Grant enum, dispatching on the tag.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
struct GrantViewRow {
    /// The grant's id, a UUID unique across both tables.
    id: String,
    /// The client the grant is for.
    client_id: String,
    /// Everything the Owner has approved under the grant, as a JSON array.
    scopes: JsonStrings,
    /// The latest approval.
    granted_at: DateTime<Utc>,
    /// When the grant was last used; `NULL` until it first is.
    last_used_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
    /// The patient the latest approval named, if any.
    patient: Option<String>,
    /// The kind tag, which says which payload column is the row's own.
    grant_type: FlowType,
    /// An authorization-code grant's redirect URI; `NULL` on a device grant.
    redirect_uri: Option<UrlText>,
    /// A device grant's device name; `NULL` on an authorization-code grant.
    device_name: Option<String>,
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/db/grants/general.rs lines 42–61 · authorization-server in the code index

Into a Grant

The view selects each kind’s own column from that kind’s table, where it is NOT NULL, so a row missing its own column can’t arise; the check is there anyway, and is a logged 500, never a panic. The round trip draws grants of either kind from arb_grant.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn try_from(row: GrantViewRow) -> Result<Self, Self::Error> {
    // The UNION ALL projects each kind's payload column NOT NULL from its
    // own table, so a NULL payload for the row's own kind is structurally
    // impossible — guarded anyway so a future view edit degrades to a
    // logged 500, never a panic.
    let make_missing_payload_error = || {
        AuthorizationServerError::infrastructure(
            "grants view row missing its kind's payload column",
            &row.id,
        )
    };
    match row.grant_type {
        FlowType::AuthorizationCode => {
            let redirect_uri = row.redirect_uri.ok_or_else(make_missing_payload_error)?.0;
            Ok(Grant::AuthorizationCode(AuthorizationCodeGrant {
                id: row.id,
                client_id: row.client_id,
                scopes: row.scopes.0,
                granted_at: row.granted_at,
                last_used_at: row.last_used_at,
                patient: row.patient,
                redirect_uri,
            }))
        }
        FlowType::DeviceCode => {
            let device_name = row.device_name.ok_or_else(make_missing_payload_error)?;
            Ok(Grant::DeviceCode(DeviceGrant {
                id: row.id,
                client_id: row.client_id,
                scopes: row.scopes.0,
                granted_at: row.granted_at,
                last_used_at: row.last_used_at,
                patient: row.patient,
                device_name,
            }))
        }
        // The view unions the two grant tables only, and a browser
        // pairing records no grant, so no row carries this tag.
        FlowType::BrowserPairing => Err(AuthorizationServerError::infrastructure(
            "grants view row tagged as a browser pairing, which records no grant",
            &row.id,
        )),
    }
}
}

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn create_and_fetch_round_trip(grant in arb_grant()) {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    match &grant {
        Grant::AuthorizationCode(g) => {
            store.write(|tx| tx.create_authorization_code_grant(g)).expect("create code grant");
        }
        Grant::DeviceCode(g) => {
            store.write(|tx| tx.create_device_grant(g)).expect("create device grant");
        }
    }
    let fetched = store
        .read(|tx| tx.grant_by_id(grant.id()))
        .expect("query")
        .expect("row present");
    prop_assert_eq!(fetched, grant);
}
}

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn code_and_device_grants_coexist_per_client() {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    let redirect = read("https://example.com/cb");
    let now = Utc::now();
    store
        .write(|tx| {
            tx.create_authorization_code_grant(&AuthorizationCodeGrant {
                id: Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
                client_id: "client-a".to_owned(),
                scopes: vec!["read".to_owned()],
                granted_at: now,
                last_used_at: None,
                patient: None,
                redirect_uri: redirect.clone(),
            })
        })
        .expect("code grant");
    store
        .write(|tx| {
            tx.create_device_grant(&DeviceGrant {
                id: Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
                client_id: "client-a".to_owned(),
                scopes: vec!["openid".to_owned()],
                granted_at: now,
                last_used_at: None,
                patient: None,
                device_name: "Ada's laptop".to_owned(),
            })
        })
        .expect("device grant");

    assert!(store
        .read(|tx| tx.grant_by_client_and_redirect("client-a", &redirect))
        .expect("query")
        .is_some());
    assert!(store
        .read(|tx| tx.device_grant_by_client_and_device_name("client-a", "Ada's laptop"))
        .expect("query")
        .is_some());
    // The device lookup never returns the code grant, and vice versa.
    assert!(store
        .read(|tx| tx
            .device_grant_by_client_and_device_name("client-a", "https://example.com/cb"))
        .expect("query")
        .is_none());
    assert_eq!(store.read(|tx| tx.all_grants()).expect("list").len(), 2);
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/db/grants/general.rs lines 162–170 · authorization-server in the code index

Revoking removes the concrete row — visible both through the view read and the concrete-table lookup — and, in the SAME transaction, expires the client’s refresh-token families (deadline pulled to the revocation instant, live token stamped consumed): standing consent and standing credentials die together. A second revoke of the same id reports the miss.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn revoke_removes_the_row_and_expires_the_clients_families() {
    use crate::domain::refresh_token::{RefreshToken, RefreshTokenFamily};

    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    store
        .write(|tx| {
            tx.create_device_grant(&DeviceGrant {
                id: Uuid::new_v4().to_string(),
                client_id: "client-a".to_owned(),
                scopes: vec!["openid".to_owned()],
                granted_at: Utc::now(),
                last_used_at: None,
                patient: None,
                device_name: "Ada's laptop".to_owned(),
            })
        })
        .expect("insert");
    let id = store.read(|tx| tx.all_grants()).expect("list")[0]
        .id()
        .to_owned();
    // A standing credential minted under this client, live at revoke time.
    let family = RefreshTokenFamily {
        family_id: "fam-1".to_owned(),
        client_id: "client-a".to_owned(),
        scopes: vec!["openid".to_owned()],
        patient: None,
        issued_at: Utc::now(),
        expires_at: Utc::now() + chrono::Duration::days(90),
        authorization_code_hash: None,
        grant_id: Some(id.clone()),
        sid: None,
    };
    let live = RefreshToken {
        token_hash: "live-token".to_owned(),
        family_id: "fam-1".to_owned(),
        issued_at: Utc::now(),
        consumed_at: None,
    };
    store
        .write(|tx| tx.insert_refresh_token_family_row(&family))
        .expect("insert family");
    store
        .write(|tx| tx.insert_refresh_token(&live))
        .expect("insert live token");

    let revoked_at = Utc::now();
    revoke_grant(&store, &id, "client-a", revoked_at).expect("revoke");
    assert!(store
        .read(|tx| tx.grant_by_id(&id))
        .expect("query")
        .is_none());
    assert!(store
        .read(|tx| tx.device_grant_by_client_and_device_name("client-a", "Ada's laptop"))
        .expect("query")
        .is_none());
    // The family died with the consent: deadline pulled back, live token
    // stamped at the same instant.
    let (token, family) = store
        .read(|tx| tx.refresh_token_with_family_by_hash("live-token"))
        .expect("query")
        .expect("row kept for auditability");

The GrantRecorder::record_code_grant action, driven end-to-end against the real SQLite adapter: a first approval inserts (via create_authorization_code_grant), a re-approval reads the standing grant, unions scopes (cumulative consent) and writes it back through update_authorization_code_grant — all inside the action’s BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction, against one row. The pure union decision is unit-tested against the fake in domain::capabilities::writers; this proves the same script lands correctly through diesel.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn upsert_action_inserts_then_unions_scopes_over_sqlite() {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    let redirect = read("https://example.com/cb");
    let now = Utc::now();

    upsert_code_grant(
        &store,
        "client-a",
        &redirect,
        &["read".to_owned()],
        Some("pat-1"),
        now,
    );
    let grant = store
        .read(|tx| tx.grant_by_client_and_redirect("client-a", &redirect))
        .expect("query")
        .expect("present");
    assert_eq!(grant.scopes, vec!["read".to_owned()]);
    assert_eq!(grant.patient.as_deref(), Some("pat-1"));

    // Re-approve with an overlapping + a new scope: union, not replace.
    upsert_code_grant(
        &store,
        "client-a",
        &redirect,
        &["read".to_owned(), "write".to_owned()],
        Some("pat-2"),
        Utc::now(),
    );
    let updated = store
        .read(|tx| tx.grant_by_client_and_redirect("client-a", &redirect))
        .expect("query")
        .expect("present");
    assert_eq!(
        updated.id, grant.id,
        "the same grant is updated, not duplicated"
    );
    assert_eq!(updated.scopes, vec!["read".to_owned(), "write".to_owned()]);
    assert_eq!(updated.patient.as_deref(), Some("pat-2"));
    assert_eq!(store.read(|tx| tx.all_grants()).expect("list").len(), 1);
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/db/grants/device.rs lines 214–247 · authorization-server in the code index

Authorization Codes

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/db/authorization_codes.rs

An authorization code lives in the authorization_codes table from the moment an approval issues it until the app redeems it at /oauth/token, a minute at most. A row is one AuthorizationCode: the code itself as the primary key, and everything it is bound to, the request, the app, the redirect URI, the PKCE challenge, the granted scopes, the patient, the browser session, the issue and expiry instants.

Two rules live in the schema and in one statement:

  • One code per request. A unique index on request_id makes a second code for the same request a hard error, so the status read always finds at most one.
  • A code is redeemed once. Redemption deletes the row and returns it in the same statement, so of two redemptions only one gets it.

The tests draw codes from arb_authorization_code.

The port is AuthorizationCodesTx.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn corrupt_redirect_uri_is_a_typed_read_error() {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    let now = chrono::Utc::now();
    let code = AuthorizationCode {
        code: "the-code".to_string(),
        request_id: "req-1".to_string(),
        client_id: "client-a".to_string(),
        redirect_uri: url::Url::parse("https://example.com/cb").expect("url"),
        code_challenge: "c".repeat(43),
        granted_scopes: vec!["read".to_string()],
        patient: None,
        issued_at: now,
        expires_at: now + chrono::Duration::seconds(60),
        sid: "sid-1".to_owned(),
    };
    store
        .write(|tx| tx.issue_authorization_code(&code))
        .expect("issue");
    let mut conn = store.pool().get().expect("check out a connection");
    diesel::sql_query(
        "UPDATE authorization_codes SET redirect_uri = 'not a url' WHERE code = 'the-code'",
    )
    .execute(&mut conn)
    .expect("tamper the stored row");
    drop(conn);
    assert!(
        store
            .read(|tx| tx.authorization_code_by_request_id("req-1"))
            .is_err(),
        "a corrupt redirect_uri must surface as a typed read error",
    );
}
}

authorization-server-rust/src/db/authorization_codes.rs lines 263–294 · authorization-server in the code index

redeem_authorization_code

Single use rests on this one statement. The row is gone whatever the redemption decides next: a code presented by the wrong app, late, or with the wrong verifier is already spent. What a miss sets off, ending the refresh families an earlier redemption started, is the redemption proof’s.

Atomically read-and-delete the authorization code so a /token redemption either gets the row exactly once or sees None. Wins the RFC 6749 §10.5 single-use race against any concurrent redeemer of the same code — DELETE … RETURNING runs under SQLite’s write lock, so only one caller’s Ok(Some) lands and any racer sees Ok(None).

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn redeem_authorization_code(
    &mut self,
    code: &str,
) -> Result<Option<AuthorizationCode>, AuthorizationServerError> {
    let conn = &mut *self.conn;
    diesel::delete(authorization_codes::table.find(code))
        .returning(AuthorizationCode::as_returning())
        .get_result(conn)
        .optional()
        .map_err(|e| {
            AuthorizationServerError::infrastructure("redeem_authorization_code failed", e)
        })
}
}

Redemption is destructive and single-winner: the first call returns the row, the second sees None (RFC 6749 §10.5).

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn redeem_returns_the_row_exactly_once() {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    let now = chrono::Utc::now();
    let code = AuthorizationCode {
        code: "the-code".to_string(),
        request_id: "req-1".to_string(),
        client_id: "client-a".to_string(),
        redirect_uri: url::Url::parse("https://example.com/cb").expect("url"),
        code_challenge: "c".repeat(43),
        granted_scopes: vec!["read".to_string()],
        patient: None,
        issued_at: now,
        expires_at: now + chrono::Duration::seconds(60),
        sid: "sid-1".to_owned(),
    };
    store
        .write(|tx| tx.issue_authorization_code(&code))
        .expect("issue");
    let first = store
        .write(|tx| tx.redeem_authorization_code("the-code"))
        .expect("redeem")
        .expect("first redemption wins");
    assert_eq!(first, code);
    assert!(
        store
            .write(|tx| tx.redeem_authorization_code("the-code"))
            .expect("redeem again")
            .is_none(),
        "second redemption must lose",
    );
}
}

The retention delete is a strict < on the cutoff the policy hands down: a code past it goes, one still inside the window stays, and an unexpired code is never in range. Only abandoned codes ever reach here — redemption deletes the row as it consumes it.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn delete_expired_codes_respects_the_cutoff() {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    let now = chrono::Utc::now();
    let sample = |name: &str, expires_at| AuthorizationCode {
        code: name.to_string(),
        request_id: format!("req-{name}"),
        client_id: "client-a".to_string(),
        redirect_uri: url::Url::parse("https://example.com/cb").expect("url"),
        code_challenge: "c".repeat(43),
        granted_scopes: vec!["read".to_string()],
        patient: None,
        issued_at: now - chrono::Duration::minutes(1),
        expires_at,
        sid: "sid-1".to_owned(),
    };
    for code in [
        sample("old", now - chrono::Duration::days(8)),
        sample("recent", now - chrono::Duration::days(6)),
        sample("live", now + chrono::Duration::minutes(1)),
    ] {
        store
            .write(|tx| tx.issue_authorization_code(&code))
            .expect("issue");
    }

    let purged = store
        .write(|tx| {

        .read(|tx| tx.authorization_code_by_request_id("req-old"))

        .read(|tx| tx.authorization_code_by_request_id("req-recent"))

authorization-server-rust/src/db/authorization_codes.rs lines 213–257 · authorization-server in the code index

Refresh Tokens

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/db/refresh_tokens.rs

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/db/refresh_tokens/tests.rs

A refresh family is two tables. refresh_token_families holds what every link in the chain shares, once per family: the app, the scopes, the patient, the deadline, the hash of the code that started it, the grant behind it, the browser session. refresh_tokens holds one row per link, keyed by the hash of the token; the token itself is never stored. A link’s family_id is a foreign key to its family, enforced, as the pool turns foreign_keys on for every connection, so no link can exist without its family.

Ending a family never deletes it. Each expiry below, for a replayed link, the app revoking its token, the Owner revoking a grant, or a replayed code, pulls the family’s expires_at back to the moment it ended and stamps its unspent link spent at the same moment. The rows stay, so a link presented later still resolves to its dead family and is refused for that reason. Only the retention sweep deletes, once a family has been dead long enough.

The family’s grant_id is a soft reference with no foreign key: revoking a grant deletes the grant and keeps its families. The family table is indexed on client_id and authorization_code_hash, which the bulk expiries match on, on sid, which the browser-session sweep asks about, and on grant_id; the link table on family_id. The methods that touch both tables run their two statements in a nested transaction, which inside a write scope’s BEGIN IMMEDIATE is a savepoint: both land or neither does.

The tests are in a file of their own, refresh_tokens/tests.rs, and each is shown under the primitive it holds. They draw families from arb_family and plant them with seed_family_with_token.

fn main() {
fn insert_refresh_token_rejects_orphan_without_family() {

        .write(|tx| tx.insert_refresh_token(&sample_token("orphan", "no-such-family")))
        .expect_err("orphan insert must violate the foreign key");
    assert!(
        matches!(
            &err,
            AuthorizationServerError::Infrastructure { source, .. }
                if source.to_uppercase().contains("FOREIGN KEY")
        ),
        "expected a foreign-key constraint violation, got {err:?}"
    );
}
}

(The three-state decision itself is tested against the action in domain::refresh_token.)

fn main() {
fn stamp_consumes_live_then_loses_the_guard_on_replay(

        .expect("second stamp"));
    prop_assert!(store
        .write(|tx| tx.has_refresh_token(&live.token_hash))
        .expect("exists probe"));

End a token family by pulling its expires_at back to now, and stamp its still-live token consumed at the same instant so no row in a dead family looks live. Used by reuse detection and by ClientTokenRevoker when a client revokes its own refresh token. #![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn expire_refresh_token_family(
    &mut self,
    family_id: &str,
    now: DateTime<Utc>,
) -> Result<(), AuthorizationServerError> {
    let conn = &mut *self.conn;
    conn.transaction(|conn| {
        diesel::update(refresh_token_families::table.find(family_id))
            .set(refresh_token_families::expires_at.eq(now))
            .execute(conn)?;

            refresh_tokens::table
                .filter(refresh_tokens::family_id.eq(family_id))
                .filter(refresh_tokens::consumed_at.is_null()),
        )
        .set(refresh_tokens::consumed_at.eq(now))
        .execute(conn)?;
        Ok(())
    })
    .map_err(|e: diesel::result::Error| {
        AuthorizationServerError::infrastructure("expire_refresh_token_family failed", e)
    })
}
}

Ending a family keeps its rows: its deadline moves to the moment it ended, its live token is stamped consumed then, a token redeemed earlier keeps its own stamp, and another family is untouched.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn expire_family_pulls_deadline_back_and_stamps_the_live_token() {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    seed_family_with_token(
        &store,
        &sample_family("family-a", "client-1"),
        &sample_token("token-1", "family-a"),
    );
    store
        .write(|tx| tx.insert_refresh_token(&sample_token("token-2", "family-a")))
        .expect("insert token-2");
    let untouched = sample_family("family-b", "client-1");
    seed_family_with_token(&store, &untouched, &sample_token("other", "family-b"));
    // token-1 was genuinely redeemed before the revocation — its stamp
    // must survive the family kill untouched.
    let redeemed_at = Utc::now();
    assert!(store
        .write(|tx| tx.stamp_refresh_token_consumed_if_live("token-1", redeemed_at))
        .expect("consume"));

    let revoked_at = Utc::now();
    store
        .write(|tx| tx.expire_refresh_token_family("family-a", revoked_at))
        .expect("expire");

    // Rows are kept — the lineage stays auditable — with the family's
    // deadline pulled back to the revocation instant.
    let (redeemed_token, family) = store
        .read(|tx| tx.refresh_token_with_family_by_hash("token-1"))
        .expect("query")
        .expect("row present");
    assert_eq!(family.expires_at, revoked_at);
    assert_eq!(redeemed_token.consumed_at, Some(redeemed_at));
    // The live token is stamped at the revocation instant, so nothing in
    // a dead family looks live.
    let (live_token, _) = store
        .read(|tx| tx.refresh_token_with_family_by_hash("token-2"))
        .expect("query")
        .expect("row present");
    assert_eq!(live_token.consumed_at, Some(revoked_at));
    // The sibling family is untouched.
    let (other_token, other_family) = store
        .read(|tx| tx.refresh_token_with_family_by_hash("other"))
        .expect("query")
        .expect("row present");
    assert_eq!(other_family.expires_at, untouched.expires_at);
    assert_eq!(other_token.consumed_at, None);
}
}

Signing Keys

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/db/signing_keys.rs

The signing_keys table holds the RSA keys the server signs its tokens with, one row per signing key, keyed by kid, the kid header of every token the key signs. The SigningKey domain type is the row, its values mapped to values_json through JsonSigningKeyValues, a json_text_column. The active key signs new tokens; every key in the table is published, so a token signed by a key no longer active still verifies.

Nothing in the table limits it to one active key. Boot-time seeding inserts an active key only when it finds none, and nothing else writes the table, so there is at most one.

The round-trip property draws keys from arb_signing_key.

fn insert_and_fetch_round_trip(key in arb_signing_key()) {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    store.write(|tx| tx.insert_signing_key(&key)).expect("insert");

    // A freshly-opened store holds exactly this one key.
    let all = store.read(|tx| tx.all_signing_keys()).expect("all");
    prop_assert_eq!(all, vec![key.clone()]);

    // `active_signing_key` mirrors the `is_active` flag.
    let active = store.read(|tx| tx.active_signing_key()).expect("active");
    let expected_active = if key.is_active { Some(key) } else { None };
    prop_assert_eq!(active, expected_active);
}
}

The JsonSigningKeyValues JSON TEXT mapping rejects a values_json that no longer parses as a typed read error, never a panic — a corrupt key can’t silently decode to garbage RSA material.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn corrupt_values_json_is_a_typed_read_error() {
    let store = SqliteGrantStore::open_in_memory().expect("open in-memory store");
    let key = SigningKey {
        kid: "k1".to_string(),
        kty: "RSA".to_string(),
        alg: "RS256".to_string(),
        values: SigningKeyValues {
            n: "n".to_string(),
            d: "d".to_string(),
            e: "e".to_string(),
            p: "p".to_string(),
            q: "q".to_string(),
        },
        is_active: true,
    };
    store
        .write(|tx| tx.insert_signing_key(&key))
        .expect("insert");
    let mut conn = store.pool().get().expect("check out a connection");
    diesel::sql_query("UPDATE signing_keys SET values_json = 'not json' WHERE kid = 'k1'")
        .execute(&mut conn)
        .expect("tamper the stored row");
    drop(conn);
    assert!(
        store.read(|tx| tx.all_signing_keys()).is_err(),
        "a corrupt values_json must surface as a typed read error",
    );
}
}

Test Fixtures

Covers authorization-server-rust/src/db/test_support.rs

The generators and helpers the adapter’s tests share, by the page whose tests use them. Every test runs against a real, freshly migrated SQLite database, in memory, so what the tests hold is the SQL itself: its guards, its constraints, its column mappings. The property tests write a generated row and read it back unchanged, so their generators draw only values that survive that trip.

Shared generators

A DateTime<Utc> drawn from a plausible recent epoch window (2000-01-01 to 2065-01-01). Built from a whole millisecond count so the value round-trips through SQLite’s text timestamp encoding without precision loss.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub fn arb_timestamp() -> impl Strategy<Value = DateTime<Utc>> {
    let window_start = Utc
        .with_ymd_and_hms(2000, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
        .single()
        .expect("valid window start")
        .timestamp_millis();
    let window_end = Utc
        .with_ymd_and_hms(2065, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0)
        .single()
        .expect("valid window end")
        .timestamp_millis();
    (window_start..window_end).prop_map(|millis| {
        Utc.timestamp_millis_opt(millis)
            .single()
            .expect("valid epoch ms")
    })
}
}
