fn main() {
async fn deciding_an_oauth_consent_clears_the_owner_prompt() {

            .router

                .header("host", "127.0.0.1")
                .header("authorization", format!("Bearer {owner_token}"))
                .header("content-type", "application/json"),
                Body::from(r#"{"approvedScopes":["read"],"acknowledgedRegistrationChange":true}"#),
            ))
            .await
            .expect("oneshot");
        assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK, "{decision} should succeed");

        assert_eq!(
            owner_prompt(&db),
            None,
            "{decision}: the request must clear once it is decided",

    }

the_pending_consent_watcher_sees_an_older_request_decided_under_a_newer_one

The host’s PendingConsentWatcher sees a request settle even when it isn’t the newest: denying an older request while a newer one waits leaves the Owner prompt unchanged, so nothing reaches the host through that.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn the_pending_consent_watcher_sees_an_older_request_decided_under_a_newer_one() {
    let (g, owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    seed_client_with_redirect(&db, "test-app", "https://app.example/cb", &["read"]);
    let older_id = parked_request_id(
        &get_authorize(
            &g.router,
            &db.paired_browser_token,
            &authorize_query("test-app", "read"),
        )
        .await,
    );
    let newer_id = parked_request_id(
        &get_authorize(
            &g.router,
            &db.paired_browser_token,
            &authorize_query("test-app", "read"),
        )
        .await,
    );
    let watcher = g.pending_consent_watcher.clone();
    let older_key = ConsentKey::AuthorizationCode {
        id: older_id.clone(),
    };
    let older_settled = tokio::spawn(async move { watcher.until_settled(older_key).await });
    tokio::time::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(50)).await;
    assert!(
        !older_settled.is_finished(),
        "the older request still waits"
    );

    let res = g
        .router
        .clone()
        .oneshot(build_request(
            Request::post(format!("/authorization/oauth-consents/{older_id}/deny"))
                .header("host", "127.0.0.1")
                .header("authorization", format!("Bearer {owner_token}"))
                .header("content-type", "application/json"),
            Body::from(r#"{"approvedScopes":["read"],"acknowledgedRegistrationChange":true}"#),
        ))
        .await
        .expect("oneshot");
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);

    tokio::time::timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5), older_settled)
        .await
        .expect("the watcher sees the older request settle")
        .expect("the watcher's task")
        .expect("the watcher's reads");
    assert_eq!(
        owner_prompt(&db),
        Some(OwnerPrompt::AuthorizationCode {
            id: newer_id,
            client_name: "Integration Test Client".to_owned(),
            decidable_in_requesting_browser: false,
        }),
        "the newer request is still the newest",
    );
}
}

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn a_fast_pathed_authorize_never_becomes_the_owner_prompt() {
    let (g, owner_token, db) = spin_up();

    seed_client_with_redirect(&db, "test-app", "https://app.example/cb", &["read"]);

        &g,
        &owner_token,
        &db.paired_browser_token,
        "test-app",
        "read",
        r#"{"approvedScopes":["read"],"acknowledgedRegistrationChange":true}"#,
    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(
        owner_prompt(&db),
        None,
        "the approved first request left nothing pending"
    );

    // Second pass: the grant now pre-approves every requested scope, so
    // /authorize issues a code and 302s straight back to the client.
    let res = get_authorize(
        &g.router,
        &db.paired_browser_token,
        &authorize_query("test-app", "read"),
    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::FOUND);
    let location = location_of(&res);
    assert!(
        location.starts_with("https://app.example/cb?code="),
        "expected the fast path's client redirect, got {location}"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        owner_prompt(&db),
        None,
        "a fully pre-approved request must never be published as pending",
    );
}
}

fn main() {
async fn authorize_refuses_a_bad_smart_launch_or_aud() {

    let other_clients_launch = g
        .launch_context_minter
        .mint("other-app")
        .expect("mint a launch");
    // The forged launch and the other client's read the same, so the redirect
    // tells the two apart no more than it says anything about the other
    // client's launch.
    let not_recognized = "https://app.example/cb?error=invalid_request&error_description=\
                          This+launch+isn%27t+recognized.+Open+the+app+again.&state=xyz";
    let wrong_server = "https://app.example/cb?error=invalid_request&error_description=\
                        The+app+asked+for+a+different+server+than+this+one.&state=xyz";
    for (smart_params, expected_location) in [
        ("launch=forged-launch".to_owned(), not_recognized),
        (format!("launch={other_clients_launch}"), not_recognized),
        (
            "aud=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.example%2Ffhir-r4".to_owned(),
            wrong_server,
        ),
    ] {
        let res = get_authorize(
            &g.router,
            &db.paired_browser_token,
            &smart_launch_query(&smart_params),
        )
        .await;
        assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::FOUND);
        assert_eq!(
            location_of(&res),
            expected_location,
            "{smart_params} is refused"
        );
    }

    parked_request_id(
        &get_authorize(
            &g.router,
            &db.paired_browser_token,
            &authorize_query("test-app", "read"),
        )
        .await,
    );
    parked_request_id(
        &get_authorize(

device_authorization_happy_path

A device-authorization start for a registered client answers the RFC 8628 §3.2 body: random device and user codes, this server’s own device page as verification_uri (and with the user code in verification_uri_complete), a five-minute expiry and a five-second poll interval. The user code is human-typeable.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn device_authorization_happy_path() {
    let (g, _owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    seed_test_client(&db);
    let body = "client_id=integration-test-app&scope=system%2F*.cruds";
    let req = build_request(
        Request::post("/oauth/device_authorization")
            .header("content-type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"),
        Body::from(body),
    );
    let res = g.router.oneshot(req).await.expect("oneshot");
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let body = body_json(res.into_body()).await;
    // device_code/user_code are random, so thread them through; the rest of
    // the RFC 8628 §3.2 body (verification_uri, verification_uri_complete,
    // expires_in, interval) is pinned by the whole-value comparison.
    let device_code = body["device_code"].clone();
    let user_code = body["user_code"].as_str().expect("user_code").to_string();
    assert_eq!(
        body,
        serde_json::json!({
            "device_code": device_code,
            "user_code": user_code,
            // This server's own device page, on its origin.
            "verification_uri": "https://ruth.relay.example/oauth/device",
            "verification_uri_complete": format!(
                "https://ruth.relay.example/oauth/device?user_code={user_code}"
            ),
            "expires_in": 300,
            "interval": 5,
        })
    );
    // The user_code is also a well-formed, human-typeable pairing code — a
    // relationship the opaque whole-value comparison above can't express.
    assert!(
        wildflowerhealthio_authorization_server::crypto_util::oauth_user_code::is_valid_oauth_user_code(
            &user_code
        )
    );
}
}

Session Required

Covers authorization-server-rust/tests/integration/session_required.rs

An app’s request starts in a browser, and the server asks about the browser before it asks about the app. A browser without a browser session gets nothing from /oauth/authorize but a trip to the pairing page, and it comes back to the same request once paired. A browser with one gets the whole flow. Every code its request earns is issued under that browser’s session, never the approver’s, and carries only what that session also holds.

These tests hold the server to both halves. They lean on the browser session, on the code request that records the sid it was made in, and on the launch context a SMART launch carries.

This file’s own helpers are on the Test Fixtures page, with the shared ones.

integration::session_required

a_browser_without_a_session_is_sent_to_pairing_even_with_a_standing_grant

A browser without a session is sent to the pairing page, never given a code, though a standing grant covers its request: the FHIR web UI’s client and a hosted app’s alike. Nothing is parked or raised for the Owner, its launch is left unspent, and the pairing page accepts the next that brings it back to the same request.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn a_browser_without_a_session_is_sent_to_pairing_even_with_a_standing_grant() {
    let (g, owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    seed_app(&db);
    for (query, approve_body) in [
        (fhir_ui_query(), APPROVE_FHIR_UI),
        (app_query(), APPROVE_APP),
    ] {
        park_and_approve(
            &g,
            &owner_token,
            &db.paired_browser_token,
            &query,
            approve_body,
        )
        .await;
    }
    let launch = g
        .launch_context_minter
        .mint("test-app")
        .expect("mint a launch");
    let launched_app_query = format!("{}&launch={launch}", app_query());
    let pending_before = owner_prompt(&db);

    let mut nexts = Vec::new();
    for query in [fhir_ui_query(), launched_app_query.clone()] {
        let res = get_authorize_without_session(&g.router, &query).await;
        assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::FOUND, "{query}");
        let next = pairing_next(&location_of(&res));
        assert_eq!(next, format!("/oauth/authorize?{query}"));
        nexts.push(next);
    }
    assert_eq!(owner_prompt(&db), pending_before, "nothing parked");

    for next in nexts {
        let started = start_pairing(&g, &next).await;
        assert_eq!(started.status(), StatusCode::OK);
        assert_eq!(body_json(started.into_body()).await["next"], next);
    }

    // The launch was left for the paired browser, which now takes the fast
    // path with it.
    let res = get_authorize(&g.router, &db.paired_browser_token, &launched_app_query).await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::FOUND);
    assert!(
        location_of(&res).starts_with("https://app.example/cb?code="),
        "{}",
        location_of(&res)
    );
}
}

a_paired_browser_takes_the_fast_path_under_its_own_session_until_it_is_revoked

A paired browser holding less than the app asks for stops at the limited page, then, going on, takes the fast path on a standing grant another browser earned, and the code, tokens and refresh family name its own session and carry only what that session holds of the grant. Revoking that session ends them, and the app can’t start again from a browser without a session: the revoked browser is sent to pairing.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn a_paired_browser_takes_the_fast_path_under_its_own_session_until_it_is_revoked() {
    let (g, owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    seed_app(&db);
    park_and_approve(
        &g,
        &owner_token,
        &db.paired_browser_token,
        &app_query(),
        APPROVE_APP,
    )
    .await;
    let (sid, session_token) =
        paired_browser_session_holding(&db, &["wildflower/launch", "patient/Patient.rs"]);

    let request_id =
        limited_request_id(&get_authorize(&g.router, &session_token, &app_query()).await);
    let callback = continue_past_session_shortfall(&g.router, &session_token, &request_id).await;
    let issued = redeem(&g, &code_of(&callback)).await;
    assert_eq!(issued["scope"], "patient/Patient.rs offline_access");
    let access_token = issued["access_token"].as_str().expect("an access token");
    let refresh_token = issued["refresh_token"].as_str().expect("a refresh token");
    assert_eq!(sid_of(access_token), sid);
    assert_eq!(
        family_sid(&db, refresh_token).as_deref(),
        Some(sid.as_str())
    );
    let res = post_token(
        &g,
        format!("grant_type=refresh_token&client_id=test-app&refresh_token={refresh_token}"),
    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let refreshed = body_json(res.into_body()).await;
    assert_eq!(
        refreshed["scope"], "patient/Patient.rs offline_access",
        "the refresh family keeps the code's bounded scopes"
    );
    let refresh_token = refreshed["refresh_token"]
        .as_str()
        .expect("a rotated refresh token");

    assert!(store_handle(&db)
        .write(|tx| tx.revoke_browser_session(&sid, Utc::now()))
        .expect("revoke"));
    let res = post_token(
        &g,
        format!("grant_type=refresh_token&client_id=test-app&refresh_token={refresh_token}"),
    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
    assert_eq!(body_json(res.into_body()).await["error"], "invalid_grant");
    for res in [
        get_authorize(&g.router, &session_token, &app_query()).await,
        get_authorize_without_session(&g.router, &app_query()).await,
    ] {
        assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::FOUND);
        pairing_next(&location_of(&res));
    }
}
}

    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::FOUND);

fn main() {
async fn the_wait_page_reads_the_status_after_the_owner_signs_in_in_the_same_browser() {
    let (g, _owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    seed_app(&db);
    let request_id =
        parked_request_id(&get_authorize(&g.router, &db.paired_browser_token, &app_query()).await);

    let code = g.same_device_sign_in_code_minter.mint();
    let next = format!("/oauth/authorize/{request_id}/consent");
    let sign_in_uri = format!(
        "/oauth/sign-in?{}",
        url::form_urlencoded::Serializer::new(String::new())
            .append_pair("code", code.as_str())
            .append_pair("next", &next)
            .finish()
    );
    let signed_in = g
        .router
        .clone()
        .oneshot(build_request(
            Request::get(sign_in_uri)
                .header("cookie", browser_session_cookie(&db.paired_browser_token)),
            Body::empty(),
        ))
        .await
        .expect("oneshot");
    let same_device_session_token = browser_session_token(&signed_in);
    assert_ne!(sid_of(&same_device_session_token), db.paired_browser_sid);
    let res = approve_oauth_consent(
        &g,
        &same_device_session_token,
        &request_id,
        APPROVE_APP.to_owned(),
    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);

    let res = get_authorization_status(&g.router, &same_device_session_token, &request_id).await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let status = body_json(res.into_body()).await;
    assert_eq!(status["status"], "approved");
    let callback = status["redirect"].as_str().expect("the approved redirect");
    assert!(
        callback.starts_with("https://app.example/cb?"),
        "{callback}"
    );
    let issued = redeem(&g, &code_of(callback)).await;
    let access_token = issued["access_token"].as_str().expect("an access token");
    assert_eq!(sid_of(access_token), db.paired_browser_sid);

    let unknown =
        get_authorization_status(&g.router, &same_device_session_token, "no-such-id").await;
    assert_eq!(unknown.status(), StatusCode::NOT_FOUND);
    let unknown_error = body_json(unknown.into_body()).await["error"].clone();
    let cannot_decide = signed_in_session_token_that_cannot_decide(&g, &db).await;
    for res in [
        get_authorization_status(&g.router, &cannot_decide, &request_id).await,
        g.router
            .clone()
            .oneshot(build_request(
                Request::get(format!("/oauth/authorize/{request_id}")),
                Body::empty(),
            ))
            .await
            .expect("oneshot"),
    ] {
        assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::NOT_FOUND);
        assert_eq!(body_json(res.into_body()).await["error"], unknown_error);
    }
}
}

Session Shortfall

Covers authorization-server-rust/tests/integration/session_shortfall.rs

A browser paired with read-only access may run an app that asks for more. The code it earns would carry only what its session holds, so the browser is told first, on the limited page, before anyone else is bothered. /oauth/authorize parks the request awaiting that page and sends the browser to /oauth/authorize/{id}/limited. The page reads what the session lacks (session_shortfall), then goes on (…/continue) or cancels (…/cancel).

Until the browser goes on, the Owner isn’t asked and nothing decides the request. Going on takes the branch the start would have taken: the fast path under a standing grant, the consent card, or the wait page. Only the browser that made the request can read, continue or cancel it. Once a browser session has gone on for an app, its later requests for that app skip the page. The request’s two limited-page transitions are CodeRequest::acknowledge_session_shortfall and CodeRequest::deny_on_limited_page.

This file’s own helpers are on the Test Fixtures page, with the shared ones.

integration::session_shortfall

the_fast_path_stops_at_the_limited_page_then_issues_the_narrowed_code

A standing grant covers the request, but the browser’s session falls short of it: the request parks on the limited page with nothing issued and nothing raised, the page reads the app and what the session lacks, and going on issues a code narrowed to the session.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn the_fast_path_stops_at_the_limited_page_then_issues_the_narrowed_code() {
    let (g, owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    seed_app(&db);
    approve_a_standing_grant(&g, &owner_token, &db).await;
    let (_, session_token) = limited_browser(&db);

    let request_id =
        limited_request_id(&get_authorize(&g.router, &session_token, &app_query()).await);
    assert_eq!(owner_prompt(&db), None, "the Owner isn't asked");
    assert_eq!(
        store_handle(&db)
            .read(|tx| tx.authorization_code_by_request_id(&request_id))
            .expect("read"),
        None,
        "no code yet"
    );

    let res = get_session_shortfall(&g.router, &session_token, &request_id).await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    assert_cache_suppressed(&res, "the limited page's read");
    assert_eq!(
        body_json(res.into_body()).await,
        serde_json::json!({
            "clientName": "Integration Test Client",
            "missingScopes": ["patient/Observation.rs"],
        })
    );

    let callback = continue_past_session_shortfall(&g.router, &session_token, &request_id).await;
    assert!(
        callback.starts_with("https://app.example/cb?code="),
        "{callback}"
    );
    let issued = redeem(&g, &code_of(&callback)).await;
    assert_eq!(issued["scope"], "patient/Patient.rs offline_access");
    assert_eq!(owner_prompt(&db), None);

    let res = post_session_shortfall(&g.router, &session_token, &request_id, "continue").await;
    assert_eq!(
        res.status(),
        StatusCode::NOT_FOUND,
        "a request goes on once"
    );
}
}

async fn a_session_that_went_on_for_an_app_skips_the_limited_page_for_it() {

the_owner_neither_sees_nor_decides_a_request_waiting_on_its_limited_page

A request waiting on its limited page isn’t the Owner’s to see or decide: the Owner prompt skips it, and the consent read, approve, deny and ask-owner all 404. Once the browser goes on, the Owner sees and approves it.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn the_owner_neither_sees_nor_decides_a_request_waiting_on_its_limited_page() {
    let (g, owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    seed_app(&db);
    let (_, session_token) = limited_browser(&db);
    let request_id =
        limited_request_id(&get_authorize(&g.router, &session_token, &app_query()).await);

    assert_eq!(owner_prompt(&db), None);
    let owner_request = |method: &str, action: &str| {
        let uri = format!("/authorization/oauth-consents/{request_id}{action}");
        build_request(
            Request::builder()
                .method(method)
                .uri(uri)
                .header("authorization", format!("Bearer {owner_token}"))
                .header("content-type", "application/json"),
            Body::from(if action == "/approve" {
                APPROVE_APP
            } else {
                ""
            }),
        )
    };
    for (method, action) in [
        ("GET", ""),
        ("POST", "/approve"),
        ("POST", "/deny"),
        ("POST", "/ask-owner"),
    ] {
        let res = g
            .router
            .clone()
            .oneshot(owner_request(method, action))
            .await
            .expect("oneshot");
        assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, "{method} {action}");
    }

    assert_eq!(
        continue_past_session_shortfall(&g.router, &session_token, &request_id).await,
        format!("/oauth/authorize/{request_id}/wait")
    );
    assert!(matches!(
        owner_prompt(&db),
        Some(OwnerPrompt::AuthorizationCode { ref id, .. }) if *id == request_id
    ));
    let res = approve_oauth_consent(&g, &owner_token, &request_id, APPROVE_APP.to_owned()).await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
}
}

fn main() {
async fn another_browser_can_neither_read_nor_continue_nor_cancel() {

            body_json(res.into_body()).await["error"],

            let res = post_session_shortfall(&g.router, token, &request_id, action).await;
            assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, "{action}");
        }
    }
    for (method, path) in [
        (
            "GET",
            format!("/oauth/authorize/{request_id}/session-shortfall"),
        ),
        ("POST", format!("/oauth/authorize/{request_id}/continue")),
        ("POST", format!("/oauth/authorize/{request_id}/cancel")),

            .clone()
            .oneshot(build_request(
                Request::builder().method(method).uri(&path),
                Body::empty(),
            ))
            .await
            .expect("oneshot");
        assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::NOT_FOUND, "{method} {path}");
    }

    let res = get_session_shortfall(&g.router, &session_token, &request_id).await;
    assert_eq!(
        res.status(),
        StatusCode::OK,
        "it still waits for its browser"
    );
}
}

Wait Page

Covers authorization-server-rust/tests/integration/wait_page.rs

When an app’s request is parked for the Owner and the browser that made it can’t decide it, /oauth/authorize sends that browser to the wait page. The person at the browser waits there while the Owner decides on their own device; the page polls the request’s status and follows wherever the decision sends it. These tests hold the server to how it sends the browser there and how it serves the page: on its own origin, beside the endpoint, the same static bytes for every request, locked to that origin.

The page’s script has no tests of its own; the_wait_page_checks_the_browser_session reads one line of it.

This file’s own helpers are on the Test Fixtures page, with the shared ones.

integration::wait_page

a_parked_request_waits_beside_the_authorize_endpoint

A parked request is sent to the wait page beside the endpoint it asked, named relatively, and no launcher address is involved.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn a_parked_request_waits_beside_the_authorize_endpoint() {
    let (g, _owner_token, db) = spin_up();

    let res = get_authorize(
        &g.router,
        &db.paired_browser_token,
        &authorize_query("ghost", "read"),
    )
    .await;
    let authorize_url = "http://127.0.0.1/oauth/authorize";
    let request_id = parked_request_id(&res);
    let resolved = Url::parse(authorize_url)
        .and_then(|authorize| authorize.join(&location_of(&res)))
        .expect("resolves");
    assert_eq!(
        resolved.as_str(),
        format!("{authorize_url}/{request_id}/wait"),
        "the wait page is beside the authorize endpoint"
    );
    assert!(!location_of(&res).contains(LAUNCHER_BASE));
}
}

the_wait_page_is_static_and_locked_down

The page is the same static bytes whatever request id the path names, so an id can never reach the markup, and it is served with the headers that keep it to its own origin and out of caches, frames and referrers.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn the_wait_page_is_static_and_locked_down() {
    let (g, _owner_token, _db) = spin_up();
    let hostile_id = "%3Cscript%3Ealert(1)%3C%2Fscript%3E";

    let ordinary = get(&g, "/oauth/authorize/req-1/wait").await;
    let hostile = get(&g, &format!("/oauth/authorize/{hostile_id}/wait")).await;

    assert_eq!(ordinary.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    assert_eq!(hostile.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    assert_eq!(
        header(&ordinary, "content-type"),
        "text/html; charset=utf-8"
    );
    let csp = header(&ordinary, "content-security-policy");
    for directive in [
        "default-src 'none'",
        "script-src 'self'",
        "style-src 'self'",
        "font-src 'self'",
        "connect-src 'self'",
        "frame-ancestors 'none'",
    ] {
        assert!(csp.contains(directive), "{directive} in {csp}");
    }
    assert_eq!(header(&ordinary, "referrer-policy"), "same-origin");
    assert_eq!(header(&ordinary, "x-content-type-options"), "nosniff");
    assert_eq!(header(&ordinary, "cache-control"), "no-store");

    let ordinary_body = body_string(ordinary.into_body()).await;
    let hostile_body = body_string(hostile.into_body()).await;
    assert_eq!(ordinary_body, hostile_body);
    assert!(!hostile_body.contains("alert(1)"));
}
}

Consent Card

Covers authorization-server-rust/tests/integration/consent_card.rs

When the person at the browser is the Owner, there’s no one to wait for. /oauth/authorize sends a browser signed in as the Owner to the consent card, /oauth/authorize/{id}/consent, where the request is decided in place. Any other browser with a session goes to the Wait Page, and a browser without one goes to pairing.

The card decides through the same /authorization/oauth-consents/{id} API the host’s popup uses, on the browser session’s own token as its bearer. In the running server the host’s cookie-to-bearer layer presents that token for the card; these tests send it as the bearer themselves. Which page a request goes to is recorded on the CodeRequest as decidable_in_requesting_browser, and shown to the host on the OwnerPrompt.

This file’s own helpers are on the Test Fixtures page, with the shared ones.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn approving_on_the_owner_s_bearer_sends_the_code_to_the_client_and_settles_the_wait_page() {
    let (g, _host_owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    seed_client_with_redirect(
        &db,
        "test-app",
        "https://app.example/cb",
        &["patient/Observation.rs", "openid"],

        &g,

        "approve",

    .await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let decision = body_json(res.into_body()).await;
    assert_eq!(decision["status"], "approved");
    let redirect = Url::parse(decision["redirect"].as_str().expect("a redirect")).expect("a URL");
    assert_eq!(
        redirect.as_str().split('?').next(),
        Some("https://app.example/cb")
    );
    let query: std::collections::HashMap<_, _> = redirect.query_pairs().into_owned().collect();
    assert_eq!(query.get("state").map(String::as_str), Some("xyz"));
    assert!(query.contains_key("code"), "{redirect}");

    // A wait page left open on the request settles on the same callback.
    let status = status_of(&g, &same_device_session_token, &request_id).await;
    assert_eq!(status["status"], "approved");
    assert_eq!(status["redirect"], decision["redirect"]);
}

Approval Scopes

Covers authorization-server-rust/tests/integration/approval_scopes.rs

The Owner can approve anything. A paired browser, one whose browser session holds less than the Owner’s, may approve a request too, but only if it could create everything the approval creates. Those are the request’s approval scopes:

  • wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.u, because every approval decides a request.
  • wildflower/Grant.c, because a code or device approval records a standing grant.
  • Both wildflower/Client.c and wildflower/Client.u for a code approval for a client trusted on first use, because it creates or widens the client’s registration. It takes both whatever the row looks like when the approval lands, so an approval never turns on whether the row exists yet.
  • The resource scopes a code-flow request asks for, because the approval approves the request as asked and the approver must hold what it passes on.

A refused approval is 403 InsufficientScope, naming the scopes it lacks, and the request stays pending for the Owner. The same list is shown in three places, from one function (ApprovableScopes::missing_approval_scopes), so they never disagree: the approve call refuses on it (DelegatedScopes::clamp), the consent read reports it as missingApprovalScopes, and /oauth/authorize sends the browser to the Consent Card only when it lacks none, and to the Wait Page otherwise.

This file’s own helpers are on the Test Fixtures page, with the shared ones.

    let res = approve_oauth_consent(

        &request_id,

    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    assert_eq!(body_json(res.into_body()).await["status"], "approved");

asking_the_owner_raises_a_request_decidable_in_the_requesting_browser

“Ask the server’s owner” really raises the request: one made by a browser that could decide it there stops counting as decidable in that browser, so the host notifies the Owner, and it stays pending. A browser that can only read requests may ask; once decided, there’s nothing to ask about.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn asking_the_owner_raises_a_request_decidable_in_the_requesting_browser() {
    let (g, owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    let deciding_browser = approved_browser_token(&g, &db, APPROVER_SCOPES).await;
    let res = g
        .router
        .clone()
        .oneshot(build_request(
            Request::get(format!(
                "/oauth/authorize?{}",
                authorize_query("new-app", REQUESTED_SCOPES)
            ))
            .header(
                "cookie",
                format!("__Host-browser_session={deciding_browser}"),
            ),
            Body::empty(),
        ))
        .await
        .expect("oneshot");
    let location = location_of(&res);
    assert!(location.ends_with("/consent"), "{location}");
    let request_id = location
        .trim_start_matches("authorize/")
        .trim_end_matches("/consent")
        .to_owned();
    assert!(matches!(
        owner_prompt(&db),
        Some(OwnerPrompt::AuthorizationCode {
            decidable_in_requesting_browser: true,
            ..
        })
    ));

    let reading_browser =
        approved_browser_token(&g, &db, &["wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.r"]).await;
    assert_eq!(
        ask_owner(&g, &reading_browser, &request_id).await,
        StatusCode::NO_CONTENT
    );
    assert!(matches!(
        owner_prompt(&db),
        Some(OwnerPrompt::AuthorizationCode {
            decidable_in_requesting_browser: false,
            ..
        })
    ));
    let res = get_authorization_status(&g.router, &deciding_browser, &request_id).await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    assert_eq!(body_json(res.into_body()).await["status"], "pending");

    let res =
        approve_oauth_consent(&g, &owner_token, &request_id, APPROVE_REQUESTED.to_owned()).await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    assert_eq!(
        ask_owner(&g, &reading_browser, &request_id).await,
        StatusCode::NOT_FOUND
    );
}
}

Device Code

Covers authorization-server-rust/tests/integration/device_code.rs

The device-code flow (RFC 8628) is for a device with no browser of its own to send to /oauth/authorize: a TV, a watch, a command line. The device asks at /oauth/device_authorization, shows its user a short code, and polls /oauth/token. The Owner enters the code on the Device Page and approves. Until then the device hears “not yet”.

The request is a DeviceRequest, one of the polled requests. The Owner’s approval is recorded twice. The request carries the approval the poll redeems (DeviceRequest::approve). A standing DeviceGrant is what the Owner’s list of authorized devices shows.

The file also holds the token endpoint’s refresh-token promises, for both flows: rotation, the family’s deadline, binding to the client, and what revoking a grant does to its client’s refresh tokens.

integration::device_code

device_grant_pending_then_slow_down

First poll on a still-pending request returns authorization_pending; an immediate second poll trips the slow-down rate limit (last_polled_at is within DEVICE_CODE_POLL_INTERVAL).

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn device_grant_pending_then_slow_down() {
    let (g, _owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    seed_test_client(&db);
    plant_device_request(
        &store_handle(&db),
        TEST_CLIENT_ID,
        "dev-pending",
        &[TEST_CLIENT_SCOPE],
        RequestStatus::Pending,
        Utc::now() + Duration::minutes(5),
    );
    let body = "grant_type=urn%3Aietf%3Aparams%3Aoauth%3Agrant-type%3Adevice_code&\
                client_id=integration-test-app&device_code=dev-pending";
    let first = post_form(&g.router, "/oauth/token", body).await;
    assert_eq!(first.status(), StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
    assert_eq!(
        body_json(first.into_body()).await,
        serde_json::json!({ "error": "authorization_pending" })
    );
    let second = post_form(&g.router, "/oauth/token", body).await;
    assert_eq!(second.status(), StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
    assert_eq!(
        body_json(second.into_body()).await,
        serde_json::json!({ "error": "slow_down" })
    );
}
}

device_grant_single_use_then_expired_token

An approved device request mints a token exactly once: the first exchange succeeds and expires the request, so a second exchange sees expired_token (single-use, RFC 8628 §3.4).

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn device_grant_single_use_then_expired_token() {
    let (g, _owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    seed_test_client(&db);
    plant_device_request(
        &store_handle(&db),
        TEST_CLIENT_ID,
        "dev-approved",
        &[TEST_CLIENT_SCOPE],
        RequestStatus::Approved,
        Utc::now() + Duration::minutes(5),
    );
    let body = "grant_type=urn%3Aietf%3Aparams%3Aoauth%3Agrant-type%3Adevice_code&\
                client_id=integration-test-app&device_code=dev-approved";
    let first = post_form(&g.router, "/oauth/token", body).await;
    assert_eq!(first.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let token = body_json(first.into_body()).await;
    assert_eq!(token["token_type"], "Bearer");
    assert_eq!(token["scope"], TEST_CLIENT_SCOPE);

    let second = post_form(&g.router, "/oauth/token", body).await;
    assert_eq!(second.status(), StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
    assert_eq!(
        body_json(second.into_body()).await,
        serde_json::json!({ "error": "expired_token" })
    );
}
}

device_consent_clamps_granted_scopes_to_client_allowed

Device-flow consent clamps the granted scopes to the client’s current allowed_scopes, not just to what the request asked for: a request that asked for write while it was permitted grants no write once the client’s registration no longer allows it.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn device_consent_clamps_granted_scopes_to_client_allowed() {
    let (g, owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    // The client permits only `read`.
    seed_client_with_redirect(&db, "device-client", "https://app.example/cb", &["read"]);
    // A pending device request that asks for the disallowed `write` too.
    plant_device_request(
        &store_handle(&db),
        "device-client",
        "dev-clamp",
        &["read", "write"],
        RequestStatus::Pending,
        Utc::now() + Duration::minutes(5),
    );

    // The Owner approves both scopes; the handler must drop `write`.
    let approve = build_request(
        Request::post("/authorization/devices/WILD-FLWR/approve")
            .header("host", "127.0.0.1")
            .header("authorization", format!("Bearer {owner_token}"))
            .header("content-type", "application/json"),
        Body::from(r#"{"approvedScopes":["read","write"]}"#),
    );
    let res = g.router.clone().oneshot(approve).await.expect("oneshot");
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    assert_eq!(
        body_json(res.into_body()).await,
        serde_json::json!({ "status": "approved" })
    );

    // The issued token carries only the still-allowed `read`, never `write`.
    let body = "grant_type=urn%3Aietf%3Aparams%3Aoauth%3Agrant-type%3Adevice_code&\
                client_id=device-client&device_code=dev-clamp";
    let res = post_form(&g.router, "/oauth/token", body).await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let token = body_json(res.into_body()).await;
    assert_eq!(token["scope"], "read");
}
}

fn main() {
async fn device_consent_threads_patient_onto_request() {
    let (g, owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    seed_client_with_redirect(&db, "device-client", "https://app.example/cb", &["read"]);

        "device-client",
        "dev-patient",
        &["read"],
        RequestStatus::Pending,
        Utc::now() + Duration::minutes(5),
    );

        Request::post("/authorization/devices/WILD-FLWR/approve")
            .header("host", "127.0.0.1")
            .header("authorization", format!("Bearer {owner_token}"))
            .header("content-type", "application/json"),

        serde_json::json!({ "status": "approved" })
    );

    let request = store_handle(&db)
        .read(|tx| tx.device_request_by_id("dev-patient"))
        .expect("query request")
        .expect("request present");

            .approval()
            .and_then(|approval| approval.patient.as_deref()),

device_consent_allows_expansion_beyond_requested

Device-flow consent is expandable: the Owner approving a device may grant scopes the device never requested, up to the client’s allowed_scopes. The code flow stays clamped to the requested scopes, so a third-party app can’t widen its own grant; device_consent_clamps_granted_scopes_to_client_allowed holds the allowed-scopes ceiling.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn device_consent_allows_expansion_beyond_requested() {
    let (g, owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    // The client is allowed both read and write.
    seed_client_with_redirect(
        &db,
        "device-client",
        "https://app.example/cb",
        &["read", "write"],
    );
    // ...but the device requested only `read`.
    plant_device_request(
        &store_handle(&db),
        "device-client",
        "dev-expand",
        &["read"],
        RequestStatus::Pending,
        Utc::now() + Duration::minutes(5),
    );

    let approve = build_request(

            .header("host", "127.0.0.1")

    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    assert_eq!(
        body_json(res.into_body()).await,
        serde_json::json!({ "status": "approved" })
    );

    // The expansion is persisted onto the grant — `write` was never requested.
    let request = store_handle(&db)
        .read(|tx| tx.device_request_by_id("dev-expand"))
        .expect("query request")

        .state
        .approval()
        .expect("granted scopes")
        .granted_scopes;

device_approval_mints_durable_grant_and_links_refresh_family

Approving a device-code consent records a standing device grant, the record the Owner’s list of authorized devices shows, and the family the device’s offline_access token starts links back to that grant. This is the device half of “a refresh family names the grant that earned it”; offline_access_issues_rotating_refresh_token is the code-flow half.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn device_approval_mints_durable_grant_and_links_refresh_family() {
    let (g, owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    seed_client_with_redirect(
        &db,
        "device-client",
        "https://app.example/cb",
        &["read", "offline_access"],
    );
    plant_device_request(
        &store_handle(&db),
        "device-client",
        "dev-durable",
        &["read", "offline_access"],
        RequestStatus::Pending,
        Utc::now() + Duration::minutes(5),
    );

    // Approve, naming the device.
    let approve = build_request(
        Request::post("/authorization/devices/WILD-FLWR/approve")
            .header("host", "127.0.0.1")
            .header("authorization", format!("Bearer {owner_token}"))
            .header("content-type", "application/json"),
        Body::from(r#"{"approvedScopes":["read","offline_access"],"deviceName":"Reception iPad"}"#),
    );
    let res = g.router.clone().oneshot(approve).await.expect("oneshot");
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);

    // The standing device grant shows in the access index as the `device_code`
    // union variant, titled by its deviceName.
    let res = g
        .router
        .clone()
        .oneshot(build_request(
            Request::get("/authorization/grants")
                .header("host", "127.0.0.1")
                .header("authorization", format!("Bearer {owner_token}")),
            Body::empty(),
        ))
        .await
        .expect("oneshot");
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let grants = body_json(res.into_body()).await;
    let device_grant = grants
        .as_array()
        .expect("grants array")
        .iter()
        .find(|grant| grant["grantType"] == "device_code")
        .expect("a device grant was minted");
    assert_eq!(device_grant["deviceName"], "Reception iPad");
    assert_eq!(device_grant["clientId"], "device-client");
    let scopes = device_grant["scopes"].as_array().expect("scopes array");
    assert!(scopes.iter().any(|scope| scope == "read"));
    assert!(scopes.iter().any(|scope| scope == "offline_access"));

    // Redeeming the device_code issues the offline_access refresh token, whose
    // family links back to the device grant just minted.
    let body = "grant_type=urn%3Aietf%3Aparams%3Aoauth%3Agrant-type%3Adevice_code&\
                client_id=device-client&device_code=dev-durable";
    let res = post_form(&g.router, "/oauth/token", body).await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let refresh = body_json(res.into_body()).await["refresh_token"]
        .as_str()
        .expect("offline_access refresh token")
        .to_string();

    let (_, family) = store_handle(&db)
        .read(|tx| tx.refresh_token_with_family_by_hash(&token_storage_hash(&refresh)))
        .expect("family query")
        .expect("family present");
    assert_eq!(
        family.grant_id.as_deref(),
        Some(device_grant["id"].as_str().expect("grant id")),
    );
}
}

            .header("host", "127.0.0.1")

        .router

            )),

        .await
        .as_str()
        .expect("lastUsedAt is set")
        .parse()
        .expect("an RFC 3339 instant");
    assert!(stamped >= before && stamped <= Utc::now());

offline_access_issues_rotating_refresh_token

Granting offline_access issues a rotating refresh token, and the full rotation contract holds: redeeming swaps generations, replaying a consumed generation revokes the whole family (OAuth 2.1 rotation semantics), so the rotated-to token dies with it. The family records the app’s standing grant.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn offline_access_issues_rotating_refresh_token() {
    let (g, owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    seed_client_with_redirect(
        &db,
        "test-app",
        "https://app.example/cb",
        &["read", "offline_access"],
    );
    let request_id = authorize_and_approve(
        &g,
        &owner_token,
        &db.paired_browser_token,
        "test-app",
        "read%20offline_access",
        r#"{"approvedScopes":["read","offline_access"],"acknowledgedRegistrationChange":false}"#,
    )
    .await;

    // Pull the redeemable code off the status poll, then redeem it.
    let res = get_authorization_status(&g.router, &db.paired_browser_token, &request_id).await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let status = body_json(res.into_body()).await;
    let redirect = status["redirect"].as_str().expect("redirect");
    let code = Url::parse(redirect)
        .expect("redirect url")
        .query_pairs()
        .find(|(k, _)| k == "code")
        .map(|(_, v)| v.into_owned())
        .expect("code param");
    let body = format!(
        "grant_type=authorization_code&client_id=test-app&code={code}&\
         code_verifier={CODE_VERIFIER}&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.example%2Fcb"
    );
    let res = g
        .router
        .clone()
        .oneshot(build_request(
            Request::post("/oauth/token")
                .header("content-type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"),
            Body::from(body),
        ))
        .await
        .expect("oneshot");
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let token = body_json(res.into_body()).await;
    assert_eq!(token["scope"], "read offline_access");
    let first_refresh = token["refresh_token"]
        .as_str()
        .expect("refresh_token present with offline_access")
        .to_string();

    // The minted family records the authorization-code grant that authorized
    // it, as a device family records its device grant.
    {
        let store = store_handle(&db);
        let grant = store
            .read(|tx| {
                tx.grant_by_client_and_redirect(
                    "test-app",
                    &Url::parse("https://app.example/cb").unwrap(),
                )
            })
            .expect("grant query")
            .expect("code grant minted at approval");
        let (_, family) = store
            .read(|tx| tx.refresh_token_with_family_by_hash(&token_storage_hash(&first_refresh)))
            .expect("family query")
            .expect("family present");
        assert_eq!(family.grant_id.as_deref(), Some(grant.id.as_str()));
    }

    // Redeem the refresh token: fresh access token + the next generation.
    let body = format!("grant_type=refresh_token&client_id=test-app&refresh_token={first_refresh}");
    let res = g
        .router
        .clone()
        .oneshot(build_request(
            Request::post("/oauth/token")
                .header("content-type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"),
            Body::from(body.clone()),
        ))
        .await
        .expect("oneshot");
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let refreshed = body_json(res.into_body()).await;
    assert_eq!(refreshed["token_type"], "Bearer");
    assert_eq!(refreshed["scope"], "read offline_access");
    assert!(!refreshed["access_token"]
        .as_str()
        .expect("access_token")
        .is_empty());
    let second_refresh = refreshed["refresh_token"]
        .as_str()
        .expect("rotated refresh_token")
        .to_string();
    assert_ne!(second_refresh, first_refresh);

    // Replaying the consumed generation is treated as theft …
    let res = g
        .router
        .clone()
        .oneshot(build_request(
            Request::post("/oauth/token")
                .header("content-type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"),
            Body::from(body),
        ))
        .await
        .expect("oneshot");
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
    assert_eq!(
        body_json(res.into_body()).await,
        serde_json::json!({
            "error": "invalid_grant",
            "error_description": "Refresh token has been revoked",
        })
    );

    // … which kills the whole family: the rotated-to token is dead too. The
    // family is expired in place (not deleted), so it reports as expired.
    let body =
        format!("grant_type=refresh_token&client_id=test-app&refresh_token={second_refresh}");
    let res = g
        .router
        .clone()
        .oneshot(build_request(
            Request::post("/oauth/token")
                .header("content-type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"),
            Body::from(body),
        ))
        .await
        .expect("oneshot");
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
    assert_eq!(
        body_json(res.into_body()).await,
        serde_json::json!({
            "error": "invalid_grant",
            "error_description": "Refresh token has expired",
        })
    );
}
}

A refresh token presented by a different registered client is rejected exactly like an unknown token (RFC 6749 §6 client binding) — and the mismatch does NOT revoke the rightful owner’s family.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn refresh_token_is_bound_to_issuing_client() {
    let (g, _owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    seed_client_with_redirect(&db, "owner-app", "https://app.example/cb", &["read"]);
    seed_client_with_redirect(&db, "other-app", "https://other.example/cb", &["read"]);
    let store = store_handle(&db);
    plant_refresh_token(
        &store,
        "owned-token",
        "owner-app",
        Utc::now() + Duration::days(30),
    );

    let res = post_form(
        &g.router,
        "/oauth/token",
        "grant_type=refresh_token&client_id=other-app&refresh_token=owned-token",
    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
    assert_eq!(
        body_json(res.into_body()).await,
        serde_json::json!({
            "error": "invalid_grant",
            "error_description": "Invalid refresh_token parameter",
        })
    );
    // The rightful owner's token is untouched — still live.
    let (row, _family) = store
        .read(|tx| tx.refresh_token_with_family_by_hash(&token_storage_hash("owned-token")))
        .expect("query")
        .expect("row present");
    assert_eq!(row.consumed_at, None);
}
}

revoking_grant_revokes_refresh_tokens

Revoking a grant on the Owner surface also kills the client’s refresh tokens: every refresh family of that client has its deadline pulled back to the revocation and its live token stamped consumed, and the rows stay for the audit trail.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn revoking_grant_revokes_refresh_tokens() {
    let (g, owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    seed_client_with_redirect(
        &db,
        "test-app",
        "https://app.example/cb",
        &["read", "offline_access"],
    );
    authorize_and_approve(
        &g,
        &owner_token,
        &db.paired_browser_token,
        "test-app",
        "read",
        r#"{"approvedScopes":["read"],"acknowledgedRegistrationChange":false}"#,
    )
    .await;
    let store = store_handle(&db);
    plant_refresh_token(
        &store,
        "standing-token",
        "test-app",
        Utc::now() + Duration::days(30),
    );

    // Find the grant id on the Owner surface, then revoke it.
    let res = g
        .router
        .clone()
        .oneshot(build_request(
            Request::get("/authorization/grants")
                .header("host", "127.0.0.1")
                .header("authorization", format!("Bearer {owner_token}")),
            Body::empty(),
        ))
        .await
        .expect("oneshot");
    let grants = body_json(res.into_body()).await;
    let grant_id = grants[0]["id"].as_str().expect("grant id").to_string();
    let res = g
        .router
        .clone()
        .oneshot(build_request(
            Request::delete(format!("/authorization/grants/{grant_id}"))
                .header("host", "127.0.0.1")
                .header("authorization", format!("Bearer {owner_token}")),
            Body::empty(),
        ))
        .await
        .expect("oneshot");
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::NO_CONTENT);

    // Soft-revoked: the rows survive for audit, but the family's deadline is
    // pulled back and the live token is stamped consumed — and redeeming it
    // reports the family as expired.
    let (token, family) = store
        .read(|tx| tx.refresh_token_with_family_by_hash(&token_storage_hash("standing-token")))
        .expect("query")
        .expect("rows kept");
    assert!(family.expires_at <= Utc::now());
    assert!(token.consumed_at.is_some());
    let res = post_form(
        &g.router,
        "/oauth/token",
        "grant_type=refresh_token&client_id=test-app&refresh_token=standing-token",
    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
    assert_eq!(
        body_json(res.into_body()).await,
        serde_json::json!({
            "error": "invalid_grant",
            "error_description": "Refresh token has expired",
        })
    );
}
}

Device Page

Covers authorization-server-rust/tests/integration/device_page.rs

The device page is where a person types, or follows a link with, a device’s user code and approves it. /oauth/device_authorization points the device’s user at it as verification_uri_complete: /oauth/device on the server’s own origin. The page is the same bytes whatever the code: it reads the code from its own URL. It decides the request through the same /authorization/devices/{userCode} API the Device Code tests drive, on the bearer of the browser session that opened it.

Turning the page’s browser session cookie into that bearer is the host’s job (wildflower-server-rust), not this crate’s, so these tests send the browser session’s token as the bearer themselves.

This file’s own helpers are on the Test Fixtures page, with the shared ones.

integration::device_page

verification_uri_complete_serves_the_device_page_on_the_server_origin

verification_uri_complete names a page on the server’s own origin, and that page is served as HTML, uncached, under a content security policy.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn verification_uri_complete_serves_the_device_page_on_the_server_origin() {
    let (g, _host_owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    seed_test_client(&db);
    let started = start_device_flow(&g).await;

    let page_url = Url::parse(&started.verification_uri_complete).expect("a URL");
    assert_eq!(page_url.origin().ascii_serialization(), SERVER_ORIGIN);
    let res = g
        .router
        .clone()
        .oneshot(build_request(
            Request::get(format!(
                "{}?{}",
                page_url.path(),
                page_url.query().expect("the code")
            )),
            Body::empty(),
        ))
        .await
        .expect("oneshot");

    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    assert_eq!(
        res.headers()["content-type"].to_str().expect("ascii"),
        "text/html; charset=utf-8"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        res.headers()["cache-control"].to_str().expect("ascii"),
        "no-store"
    );
    assert!(res
        .headers()
        .contains_key(axum::http::header::CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY));
}
}

Browser Pairing

Covers authorization-server-rust/tests/integration/browser_pairing.rs

A browser that isn’t the Owner’s gets a browser session by pairing. It opens /oauth/pair, whose page starts a pairing (POST /oauth/pair/start), shows a code, and polls (POST /oauth/pair/poll). The Owner approves that code at the Device Page’s API, /authorization/devices/{userCode}, unticking whatever the browser shouldn’t have. The poll that finds the pairing approved hands the browser its paired session as the browser session cookie.

Pairing is no OAuth flow. No client redeems it at /oauth/token, and it records no grant. What it starts is a paired browser session, lasting a day, holding exactly what the Owner approved. The pairing itself is a PairingRequest, driven by BrowserPairing.

This file’s own helpers are on the Test Fixtures page, with the shared ones.

integration::browser_pairing

a_browser_pairs_and_holds_a_day_long_session_with_the_approved_scopes

The whole pairing: the Owner is notified of a remote browser by name, sees it on the device page with the Owner’s scopes all ticked, unticks some, and approves; the browser’s next poll hands it a 24 h paired session holding exactly the approved scopes, which the gates accept and which writes no grant. A pending poll sets no cookie and renames the browser to the name the page gives; the pairing starts one session only, so the poll after that reads expired.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn a_browser_pairs_and_holds_a_day_long_session_with_the_approved_scopes() {
    let (g, _owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    let started = start_pairing(&g).await;
    assert_eq!(
        owner_prompt(&db),
        Some(OwnerPrompt::BrowserPairing {
            user_code: started.user_code.clone(),
            browser_name: "Firefox on Linux".to_owned(),
        })
    );

    let (status, cookies) = poll_status(&g, &started.pairing_code, "Ruth's laptop").await;
    assert_eq!(status, "pending");
    assert!(cookies.is_empty(), "no cookie while pending");

    let same_device_session_token = signed_in_same_device_session_token(&g).await;
    let res = g
        .router
        .clone()
        .oneshot(build_request(
            Request::get(format!("/authorization/devices/{}", started.user_code)).header(
                "authorization",
                format!("Bearer {same_device_session_token}"),
            ),
            Body::empty(),
        ))
        .await
        .expect("oneshot");
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let card = body_json(res.into_body()).await;
    assert_eq!(card["kind"], "browser");
    assert_eq!(card["deviceName"], "Ruth's laptop", "the poll renamed it");
    assert_eq!(card["clientId"], BROWSER_SESSION_CLIENT_ID);
    assert_eq!(
        card["startingScopes"],
        serde_json::json!(wildflowerhealthio_authorization_server::owner_scopes()),
        "the Owner's card opens with everything ticked"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        card["allowedScopes"],
        serde_json::json!(wildflowerhealthio_authorization_server::owner_scopes())
    );

    let res = approve(
        &g,
        &same_device_session_token,
        &started.user_code,
        &["wildflower/launch", "system/Patient.rs"],
    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    assert_eq!(body_json(res.into_body()).await["status"], "approved");
    assert_eq!(owner_prompt(&db), None);

    let (status, cookies) = poll_status(&g, &started.pairing_code, "Ruth's laptop").await;
    assert_eq!(status, "approved");
    let session_token = paired_session_token(&cookies);
    let claims = decode_jwt_payload(&session_token);
    assert_eq!(claims["sub"], BROWSER_SESSION_CLIENT_ID);
    assert_eq!(claims["scope"], "wildflower/launch system/Patient.rs");
    assert_eq!(
        claims["exp"].as_i64().expect("exp") - claims["iat"].as_i64().expect("iat"),
        24 * 60 * 60
    );
    let sid = claims["sid"].as_str().expect("names its session");
    let session = store_handle(&db)
        .read(|tx| tx.browser_session_by_sid(sid))
        .expect("read")
        .expect("the paired session is stored");
    assert_eq!(session.kind.as_ref(), "paired");
    assert_eq!(session.name.as_deref(), Some("Ruth's laptop"));
    assert_eq!(session.scopes, ["wildflower/launch", "system/Patient.rs"]);
    assert_eq!(session.expires_at - session.created_at, Duration::hours(24));

    // The gates accept the session's token, with exactly its scopes.
    let res = g
        .router
        .clone()
        .oneshot(build_request(
            Request::get("/authorization/session")
                .header("authorization", format!("Bearer {session_token}")),
            Body::empty(),
        ))
        .await
        .expect("oneshot");
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    assert_eq!(
        body_json(res.into_body()).await["scopes"],
        serde_json::json!(["wildflower/launch", "system/Patient.rs"])
    );

    // Pairing recorded no grant.
    assert!(store_handle(&db)
        .read(|tx| tx.all_grants())
        .expect("grants")
        .is_empty());

    // The pairing starts one session: the next poll finds it spent.
    let (status, cookies) = poll_status(&g, &started.pairing_code, "").await;
    assert_eq!(status, "expired");
    assert!(cookies.is_empty());
}
}

async fn an_approval_grants_nothing_past_the_owner_s_scopes_or_the_approver_s() {

    let device_code_poll = |client_id: &str| {
        format!(
            "grant_type=urn%3Aietf%3Aparams%3Aoauth%3Agrant-type%3Adevice_code&\
             client_id={client_id}&device_code={}",
            started.pairing_code
        )
    };
    let token_request = |body: String| {
        g.router.clone().oneshot(build_request(
            Request::post("/oauth/token")
                .header("content-type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"),
            Body::from(body),
        ))
    };
    for approved in [false, true] {
        if approved {
            let res = approve(
                &g,
                &same_device_session_token,
                &started.user_code,
                &["wildflower/launch"],
            )
            .await;
            assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
        }
        let res = token_request(device_code_poll(BROWSER_SESSION_CLIENT_ID))
            .await
            .expect("oneshot");
        assert_eq!(
            res.status(),
            StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
            "approved: {approved}"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            body_json(res.into_body()).await["error"],
            "unauthorized_client",
            "approved: {approved}"
        );
        let res = token_request(device_code_poll(TEST_CLIENT_ID))
            .await
            .expect("oneshot");
        assert_eq!(
            res.status(),
            StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST,
            "approved: {approved}"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            body_json(res.into_body()).await["error"],
            "invalid_grant",
            "approved: {approved}"
        );
    }
    let (status, _) = poll_status(&g, &started.pairing_code, "").await;
    assert_eq!(status, "approved", "the token endpoint claimed nothing");
}
}

Browser Sessions

Covers authorization-server-rust/tests/integration/browser_sessions.rs

A browser session is the server’s record of one signed-in browser. Everything minted under it names it as sid: the browser’s own token, and every code, access token and refresh family an app earns there. Revoking the session ends all of them, wherever they are checked: on the /authorization surface, at the in-process verifier the FHIR server uses, and at refresh. /authorization/browser-sessions lists the live sessions and revokes one, and /oauth/sign-out revokes the session a browser’s cookie holds.

This file’s own helpers are on the Test Fixtures page, with the shared ones.

integration::browser_sessions

a_sign_in_starts_a_same_device_session_its_token_names

A sign-in starts a same-device session that lasts the eight hours its token does, unnamed and holding the Owner’s scopes, and the token names it. A second sign-in gets a different sid.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn a_sign_in_starts_a_same_device_session_its_token_names() {
    let (g, _owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    let same_device_session_token = signed_in_same_device_session_token(&g).await;
    let sid = sid_of(&same_device_session_token);

    let session = store_handle(&db)
        .read(|tx| tx.browser_session_by_sid(&sid))
        .expect("read")
        .expect("the sign-in stored its session");
    assert_eq!(session.kind, BrowserSessionKind::SameDevice);
    assert_eq!(session.name, None);
    assert_eq!(
        session.scopes,
        wildflowerhealthio_authorization_server::owner_scopes()
    );
    assert_eq!(session.expires_at - session.created_at, Duration::hours(8));
    assert_eq!(session.revoked_at, None);
    let token_expires_at = decode_jwt_payload(&same_device_session_token)["exp"]
        .as_i64()
        .expect("exp");
    assert!(
        (token_expires_at - session.expires_at.timestamp()).abs() <= 1,
        "the token ends with its session"
    );

    let other = signed_in_same_device_session_token(&g).await;
    assert_ne!(sid_of(&other), sid, "each sign-in starts its own session");
}
}

revoking_a_session_stops_its_authorization_and_fhir_requests

Revoking a session stops its token at the /authorization gate and at the in-process verifier the FHIR server checks bearers with, while another session’s token keeps working on both.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn revoking_a_session_stops_its_authorization_and_fhir_requests() {
    let (g, _owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    let revoked = signed_in_same_device_session_token(&g).await;
    let standing = signed_in_same_device_session_token(&g).await;
    let grants_status = |token: String| {
        let router = g.router.clone();
        async move {
            router
                .oneshot(owner_grants_probe(&token))
                .await
                .expect("oneshot")
                .status()
        }
    };
    assert_eq!(grants_status(revoked.clone()).await, StatusCode::OK);
    assert!(g.in_process_token_verifier.verify(&revoked).is_ok());

    assert!(store_handle(&db)
        .write(|tx| tx.revoke_browser_session(&sid_of(&revoked), Utc::now()))
        .expect("revoke"));

    assert_eq!(
        grants_status(revoked.clone()).await,
        StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED
    );
    assert!(matches!(
        g.in_process_token_verifier.verify(&revoked),
        Err(AccessTokenVerifyError::Revoked)
    ));
    assert_eq!(grants_status(standing.clone()).await, StatusCode::OK);
    assert!(g.in_process_token_verifier.verify(&standing).is_ok());
}
}

an_app_authorized_in_a_session_is_ended_with_it

An app authorized from a browser signed in as the Owner is issued its code, tokens and refresh family under that browser’s session: they all name its sid, its refresh marks the session seen, and once the session is revoked the family can’t be refreshed and the app’s access token is refused.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn an_app_authorized_in_a_session_is_ended_with_it() {
    let (g, owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    let same_device_session_token = signed_in_same_device_session_token(&g).await;
    let sid = sid_of(&same_device_session_token);

    let res = g
        .router
        .clone()
        .oneshot(build_request(
            Request::get(format!(
                "/oauth/authorize?{}",
                authorize_query("brand-new-app", "read%20offline_access")
            ))
            .header(
                "cookie",
                format!("__Host-browser_session={same_device_session_token}"),
            ),
            Body::empty(),
        ))
        .await
        .expect("oneshot");
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::FOUND);
    let consent_card = location_of(&res);
    let request_id = consent_card
        .strip_prefix("authorize/")
        .and_then(|rest| rest.strip_suffix("/consent"))
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("a consent-card redirect, got {consent_card}"))
        .to_owned();

    let res = approve_oauth_consent(
        &g,
        &owner_token,
        &request_id,
        r#"{"approvedScopes":["read","offline_access"],"acknowledgedRegistrationChange":true}"#
            .to_string(),
    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let redirect = Url::parse(
        body_json(res.into_body()).await["redirect"]
            .as_str()
            .expect("approve redirect"),
    )
    .expect("redirect URL");
    let code = redirect
        .query_pairs()
        .find(|(name, _)| name == "code")
        .map(|(_, code)| code.into_owned())
        .expect("a code");

    let res = post_token(
        &g,
        format!(
            "grant_type=authorization_code&client_id=brand-new-app&code={code}&\
             code_verifier={CODE_VERIFIER}&redirect_uri=https%3A%2F%2Fapp.example%2Fcb"
        ),
    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let issued = body_json(res.into_body()).await;
    let access_token = issued["access_token"].as_str().expect("access token");
    assert_eq!(sid_of(access_token), sid);
    let refresh_token = issued["refresh_token"]
        .as_str()
        .expect("offline_access earns a refresh token");

    let refresh = |refresh_token: String| {
        post_token(
            &g,
            format!(
                "grant_type=refresh_token&client_id=brand-new-app&refresh_token={refresh_token}"
            ),
        )
    };
    let refreshed_at = Utc::now();
    let res = refresh(refresh_token.to_owned()).await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let refreshed = body_json(res.into_body()).await;
    let last_seen_at = store_handle(&db)
        .read(|tx| tx.browser_session_by_sid(&sid))
        .expect("read")
        .expect("stored")
        .last_seen_at;
    assert!(
        last_seen_at >= refreshed_at,
        "the app refreshing marks the session seen, at {last_seen_at}"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        sid_of(refreshed["access_token"].as_str().expect("access token")),
        sid,
        "a refreshed token names the family's session"
    );
    let successor = refreshed["refresh_token"]
        .as_str()
        .expect("a successor")
        .to_owned();

    assert!(store_handle(&db)
        .write(|tx| tx.revoke_browser_session(&sid, Utc::now()))
        .expect("revoke"));

    let res = refresh(successor).await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
    assert_eq!(
        body_json(res.into_body()).await,
        serde_json::json!({
            "error": "invalid_grant",
            "error_description": "Refresh token has been revoked",
        })
    );
    assert!(matches!(
        g.in_process_token_verifier.verify(access_token),
        Err(AccessTokenVerifyError::Revoked)
    ));
}
}

the_browsers_list_shows_live_sessions_and_revokes_one

The list holds the live sessions, newest first, each row carrying the session’s columns and the caller’s marked. Revoking one through the API takes it off the list and ends its token; revoking it again is a 404. A fresh session’s lastSeenAt equals its createdAt.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn the_browsers_list_shows_live_sessions_and_revokes_one() {
    let (g, _owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    let caller = signed_in_same_device_session_token(&g).await;
    let other = signed_in_same_device_session_token(&g).await;
    let (caller_sid, other_sid) = (sid_of(&caller), sid_of(&other));

    let res = authorization_request(&g, "GET", "/authorization/browser-sessions", &caller).await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let rows = body_json(res.into_body()).await;
    let caller_row = rows
        .as_array()
        .expect("a list")
        .iter()
        .find(|row| row["sid"] == caller_sid.as_str())
        .expect("the caller's session is listed");
    assert_eq!(caller_row["kind"], "same_device");
    assert_eq!(caller_row["name"], Value::Null);
    assert_eq!(caller_row["heldByCaller"], true);
    assert_eq!(
        caller_row["lastSeenAt"], caller_row["createdAt"],
        "signing in is the session's first use"
    );
    for column in ["createdAt", "expiresAt"] {
        assert!(caller_row[column].is_string(), "{column}");
    }
    assert_eq!(
        listed_browser_sessions(&g, &caller).await,
        vec![
            (other_sid.clone(), false),
            (caller_sid.clone(), true),
            (db.paired_browser_sid.clone(), false),
        ]
    );

    let path = format!("/authorization/browser-sessions/{other_sid}");
    let res = authorization_request(&g, "DELETE", &path, &caller).await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::NO_CONTENT);
    assert_eq!(
        listed_browser_sessions(&g, &caller).await,
        vec![
            (caller_sid.clone(), true),
            (db.paired_browser_sid.clone(), false),
        ]
    );
    assert_eq!(
        g.router
            .clone()
            .oneshot(owner_grants_probe(&other))
            .await
            .expect("oneshot")
            .status(),
        StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED,
        "the revoked session's token is ended"
    );

    let res = authorization_request(&g, "DELETE", &path, &caller).await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::NOT_FOUND);
    assert_eq!(
        body_json(res.into_body()).await,
        serde_json::json!({ "error": "BrowserSessionNotFound", "sid": other_sid })
    );
}
}

Token Revocation

Covers authorization-server-rust/tests/integration/token_revocation.rs

POST /oauth/revoke (RFC 7009) is how an app gives up a token it holds, say when its user signs out of it. The app authenticates as it does at /oauth/token: a public client by its client_id, a confidential one with its secret too. Then:

  • A refresh token ends its whole family, whichever generation is presented.
  • An access token is denylisted by its jti until it expires, if this server minted it for that client.
  • Anything else is answered alike and left alone: a token the server never issued, one already dead, another server’s, and another client’s. The answer is always 200 with an empty body, so an app learns nothing about a token that isn’t its own.

The server tells the token’s type from the token itself and never reads token_type_hint. The revoker is ClientTokenRevoker::revoke. The file’s last two tests hold refresh redemption to the client’s revocation epoch, which Revocation introduces: a family begun before its client’s epoch no longer refreshes.

This file’s own helpers are on the Test Fixtures page, with the shared ones.

integration::token_revocation

an_app_revokes_its_own_refresh_token

An app revokes its own refresh token: the whole family ends, so neither that token nor its successor refreshes again.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn an_app_revokes_its_own_refresh_token() {
    let (g, _owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    seed_public_clients(&db);
    plant_refresh_token(
        &store_handle(&db),
        "app-refresh",
        APP_CLIENT_ID,
        Utc::now() + Duration::days(30),
    );
    let res = refresh(&g, APP_CLIENT_ID, "app-refresh").await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let successor = body_json(res.into_body()).await["refresh_token"]
        .as_str()
        .expect("a successor")
        .to_owned();

    assert_revocation_answered(
        revoke(&g, APP_CLIENT_ID, &successor).await,
        "revoking the app's own refresh token",
    )
    .await;

    assert_refresh_revoked(refresh(&g, APP_CLIENT_ID, &successor).await).await;
}
}

an_app_revokes_its_own_access_token

An app revokes its own access token: its jti is denylisted, so the token no longer authenticates anywhere.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn an_app_revokes_its_own_access_token() {
    let (g, _owner_token, db) = spin_up();
    seed_public_clients(&db);
    let access_token = mint_client_token(&db, APP_CLIENT_ID, &["openid"]);
    let gate_status = |token: String| {
        let router = g.router.clone();
        async move {
            router
                .oneshot(owner_grants_probe(&token))
                .await
                .expect("oneshot")
                .status()
        }
    };
    assert_eq!(
        gate_status(access_token.clone()).await,
        StatusCode::FORBIDDEN,
        "live, though it reaches no /authorization scope"
    );

    assert_revocation_answered(
        revoke(&g, APP_CLIENT_ID, &access_token).await,
        "revoking the app's own access token",
    )
    .await;

    assert!(revocation_store_handle(&db)
        .is_revoked_by_jti(&jti_of(&access_token))
        .expect("query"));
    assert_eq!(
        gate_status(access_token).await,
        StatusCode::UNAUTHORIZED,
        "the revoked token no longer authenticates"
    );
}
}

Cache Suppression

Covers authorization-server-rust/tests/integration/cache_suppression.rs

Consent prompts, device prompts and the grants list are the Owner’s private data. No browser or shared cache may keep them: every response carries Cache-Control: no-store and Pragma: no-cache, once each. On /authorization one layer, cache_suppress, wraps every response, so handler output, the session gate’s 401 and a handler’s 404 all carry the headers. The /oauth handlers wrap their own responses in the same CacheSuppressed.

This file’s own helpers are on the Test Fixtures page, with the shared ones.

Authorization Start Limit

Covers authorization-server-rust/tests/integration/authorization_start_limit.rs

Anyone who knows the server’s domain can start an authorization request, and every request raised for the Owner pops up on the Owner’s device. So the host keeps a limit, its AuthorizationStartGate. Every start that may bother the Owner spends from the limit once; a start the limit refuses is 429, uncached, and parks nothing.

The layer limit_authorization_starts sits on /oauth/authorize and /oauth/device_authorization only. When a start asks depends on what it carries:

  • A live browser session that can decide consents, at /oauth/authorize, asks only when its request is to be raised for the Owner (CodeRequest::raise_for_owner) or parked for the limited page. One it decides on its own Consent Card spends nothing, and going on past the limited page (CodeRequest::acknowledge_session_shortfall) asks nothing more.
  • No live browser session, at /oauth/authorize, never asks: the browser is only sent to pairing.
  • Anything else, and every device-authorization start, asks at once, before the request is parsed.

Asking the Owner about a request already parked (…/ask-owner) spends from the same limit, when it raises the request.

This file’s own helpers are on the Test Fixtures page, with the shared ones.

integration::authorization_start_limit

a_refused_start_is_429_uncached_before_it_is_parsed_on_either_route

A refused start is 429, uncached, on either route, before the request is parsed: both requests here are malformed, and admitted each would be a 400.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn a_refused_start_is_429_uncached_before_it_is_parsed_on_either_route() {
    let gate = CountingGate::refusing();
    let (g, _owner_token, db) = spin_up_with_authorization_start_gate(gate.clone());
    let paired_browser_cookie = browser_session_cookie(&db.paired_browser_token);

    // Neither request is well-formed: admitted, each would be a `400`.
    for (method, path, cookie) in [
        (
            Method::GET,
            "/oauth/authorize",
            Some(paired_browser_cookie.as_str()),
        ),
        (Method::POST, "/oauth/device_authorization", None),
    ] {
        let res = send(&g, method, path, cookie).await;
        assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, "{path}");
        assert_eq!(
            res.headers()
                .get(header::CACHE_CONTROL)
                .and_then(|value| value.to_str().ok()),
            Some("no-store"),
            "{path}"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            body_string(res.into_body()).await,
            "too many authorization requests; try again later"
        );
    }
    assert_eq!(gate.asked(), 2);
}
}
