a_browser_without_a_session_is_sent_to_pairing_without_asking_the_gate

A browser without a session, or whose cookie holds no live session, is only sent to pairing by /oauth/authorize, so it passes without asking the gate: a flood of them can’t spend the allowance a paired browser’s requests need. A device authorization without a session still asks.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn a_browser_without_a_session_is_sent_to_pairing_without_asking_the_gate() {
    let gate = CountingGate::refusing();
    let (g, _owner_token, db) = spin_up_with_authorization_start_gate(gate.clone());
    seed_client_with_redirect(
        &db,
        "test-app",
        "https://app.example/cb",
        &["patient/Observation.rs", "openid"],
    );
    let authorize = format!(
        "/oauth/authorize?{}",
        authorize_query("test-app", REQUESTED_SCOPES)
    );

    for cookie in [None, Some("__Host-browser_session=not-a-token")] {
        let res = send(&g, Method::GET, &authorize, cookie).await;
        assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::FOUND, "{cookie:?}");
        assert!(
            location_of(&res).starts_with("pair?next="),
            "{cookie:?} is sent to pairing"
        );
    }
    assert_eq!(gate.asked(), 0);

    let res = send(&g, Method::POST, "/oauth/device_authorization", None).await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS);
    assert_eq!(gate.asked(), 1);
}
}

no_other_route_asks_the_gate

No other route asks the gate: the token endpoint, the request and wait pages, and the JWKS are never limited.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn no_other_route_asks_the_gate() {
    let gate = CountingGate::refusing();
    let (g, _owner_token, _db) = spin_up_with_authorization_start_gate(gate.clone());

    for (method, path) in [
        (Method::POST, "/oauth/token"),
        (Method::GET, "/oauth/authorize/request-id"),
        (Method::GET, "/oauth/authorize/request-id/wait"),
        (Method::GET, "/.well-known/jwks.json"),
    ] {
        let res = send(&g, method, path, None).await;
        assert_ne!(res.status(), StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, "{path}");
    }
    assert_eq!(gate.asked(), 0);
}
}

fn main() {
async fn a_deciding_browser_s_request_raised_for_the_owner_asks_the_gate() {

        .as_str()
        .expect("a browser session's token names its sid")

            "wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.u",

    );

        Method::GET,
        &format!(
            "/oauth/authorize?{}",

        ),

    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS);
    assert_eq!(gate.asked(), 1);

a_deciding_browser_s_request_parked_for_the_limited_page_asks_the_gate

A deciding browser whose session falls short of the request asks the gate, which its start deferred, before the request parks for the limited page; admitted, going on past the page raises the request for the Owner without asking again. Refused, a request for another app parks nothing.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn a_deciding_browser_s_request_parked_for_the_limited_page_asks_the_gate() {
    let gate = Arc::new(CountingGate {
        admitted: 1,
        asked: AtomicUsize::new(0),
    });
    let (g, _owner_token, db) = spin_up_with_authorization_start_gate(gate.clone());
    seed_client_with_redirect(
        &db,
        "test-app",
        "https://app.example/cb",
        &["patient/Observation.rs", "openid"],
    );
    let same_device_session_token = signed_in_same_device_session_token(&g).await;
    let sid = decode_jwt_payload(&same_device_session_token)["sid"]
        .as_str()
        .expect("a browser session's token names its sid")
        .to_owned();
    let deciding_scopes = [
        "wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.r",
        "wildflower/AuthorizationRequest.u",
    ];
    let session_token = mint_browser_session_token(&db, &sid, &deciding_scopes);
    narrow_browser_session_of(&db, &session_token, &deciding_scopes);
    let query = authorize_query("test-app", REQUESTED_SCOPES);

    let request_id = limited_request_id(&get_authorize(&g.router, &session_token, &query).await);
    assert_eq!(gate.asked(), 1);
    let location = continue_past_session_shortfall(&g.router, &session_token, &request_id).await;
    assert_eq!(location, format!("/oauth/authorize/{request_id}/wait"));
    assert_eq!(gate.asked(), 1, "going on asks nothing");

    seed_client_with_redirect(
        &db,
        "other-app",
        "https://app.example/cb",
        &["patient/Observation.rs", "openid"],
    );
    let res = get_authorize(
        &g.router,
        &session_token,
        &authorize_query("other-app", REQUESTED_SCOPES),
    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::TOO_MANY_REQUESTS);
    assert_eq!(gate.asked(), 2);
}
}

Test Fixtures

The helpers the integration tests build their servers, requests and tokens with. The shared ones live in common.rs, which every test file brings in with use crate::common::*;, along with the crate’s own types and axum, chrono, serde_json and url. A file’s own helpers follow, by file. Each test links the fixtures it is the first on its page to use.

Covers authorization-server-rust/tests/integration/common.rs

integration::common

Almost every test starts from spin_up: a fresh server over a fresh in-memory database, an Owner token, and the TestDb the test reaches that database through. setup_authorization_server runs the same bootstrap as the host: migrations, the signing key, the essential clients.

TestDb

The two database handles the running router uses, kept so tests can open second store handles onto the SAME databases: the diesel pool behind the SqliteGrantStore and the rusqlite connection behind the shared RevocationStore (which stays rusqlite-backed — it is a separate crate).

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub struct TestDb {
    /// The diesel pool behind the router's `SqliteGrantStore`.
    pool: DieselPool,
    /// The rusqlite connection behind the router's `RevocationStore`.
    revocation_conn: Connection,
    /// Live receiver on the Owner prompt the server publishes — the
    /// same channel the Tauri host notifies from. Held (not dropped) so tests
    /// can assert *what the host would notify* after a request lands,
    /// which is the only observable difference between "parked a request" and
    /// "parked a request and asked the Owner about it".
    pending_consent_rx: watch::Receiver<Option<OwnerPrompt>>,
    /// The browser session token of a browser the Owner paired, which holds
    /// `wildflower/launch` and every FHIR scope (`system/*.cruds`): a browser
    /// `/oauth/authorize` accepts, whose session falls short of no FHIR
    /// request, but can't decide consents, so its requests park on the wait
    /// page.
    /// Every helper that makes a request in "the app's browser" uses it.
    pub paired_browser_token: String,
    /// The `sid` of [`TestDb::paired_browser_token`]'s browser session.
    pub paired_browser_sid: String,
}
}

spin_up_with_authorization_start_gate

spin_up, asking authorization_start_gate whether a request may start an authorization request.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub fn spin_up_with_authorization_start_gate(
    authorization_start_gate: Arc<dyn AuthorizationStartGate>,
) -> (AuthorizationServer, String, TestDb) {
    // One shared in-memory diesel pool, built once and handed to the slice —
    // mirrors how the host wires the app-wide `wildflowerhealthio_persistence::open_pool`
    // pool into each diesel-backed slice. `db.pool` is that shared handle;
    // `store_handle` clones it to reach the same database.
    let pool = wildflowerhealthio_persistence::open_in_memory_pool().expect("open in-memory pool");
    let (pending_consent_tx, pending_consent_rx) = watch::channel::<Option<OwnerPrompt>>(None);
    // The shared revocation store lives on the rusqlite connection the host
    // wires into both the authorization server and the FHIR server (#269). A second handle on
    // the same connection (see `revocation_store_handle`) lets tests
    // plant/observe rows.
    let revocation_conn = Connection::open_in_memory().expect("open revocation db");
    let g = set_up_over(
        pool.clone(),
        revocation_conn.clone(),
        pending_consent_tx,
        authorization_start_gate,
        &[],
    );
    let mut db = TestDb {
        pool,
        revocation_conn,
        pending_consent_rx,
        paired_browser_token: String::new(),
        paired_browser_sid: String::new(),
    };
    (db.paired_browser_sid, db.paired_browser_token) = paired_browser_session(&db);
    let owner_token = mint_owner_token(&db);
    (g, owner_token, db)
}
}

set_up_over

Set up the authorization server over pool and the revocation database revocation_conn, publishing its Owner prompt on pending_consent_tx, asking authorization_start_gate whether a request may start an authorization request, and keeping the sessions open_views_sign_in_codes signed in.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn set_up_over(
    pool: DieselPool,
    revocation_conn: Connection,
    pending_consent_tx: watch::Sender<Option<OwnerPrompt>>,
    authorization_start_gate: Arc<dyn AuthorizationStartGate>,
    open_views_sign_in_codes: &[SameDeviceSignInCode],
) -> AuthorizationServer {
    let config = AuthorizationServerConfig {
        server_origin: Url::parse(SERVER_ORIGIN).expect("SERVER_ORIGIN is a valid URL"),
        host_app_client_scopes:
            wildflowerhealthio_authorization_server::default_host_app_client_scopes(),
        fhir_ui_client_id: "fhir-ui-client".to_string(),
        launcher_base: LauncherBase::parse(LAUNCHER_BASE).expect("LAUNCHER_BASE is a valid URL"),
        authorization_app_base: AuthorizationAppBase::parse(AUTHORIZATION_APP_BASE)
            .expect("AUTHORIZATION_APP_BASE is a valid URL"),
        launcher_url: Url::parse(LAUNCHER_URL).expect("LAUNCHER_URL is a valid URL"),
        authorization_url: Url::parse(AUTHORIZATION_URL).expect("AUTHORIZATION_URL is a valid URL"),
    };
    let revocation_store =
        wildflowerhealthio_token_revocation::RevocationStore::new(revocation_conn)
            .expect("revocation store");
    setup_authorization_server(
        pool,
        revocation_store,
        &config,
        pending_consent_tx,
        authorization_start_gate,
        open_views_sign_in_codes,
    )
    .expect("setup")
}
}

seed_client_with_redirect

Register an OAuth client with an allowlisted redirect_uri through a second store handle on the same shared connection. The redirect-back error tests (RFC 6749 §4.1.2.1) need a client whose redirect_uri validates, which the seeded host app’s client (empty allowlist) cannot provide.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub fn seed_client_with_redirect(
    db: &TestDb,
    client_id: &str,
    redirect_uri: &str,
    scopes: &[&str],
) {
    let store = store_handle(db);
    store
        .write(|tx| {
            tx.upsert_client(&Client {
                client_id: client_id.to_string(),
                name: "Integration Test Client".to_string(),
                kind: ClientKind::Public,
                redirect_uris: vec![Url::parse(redirect_uri).expect("redirect url")],
                allowed_scopes: scopes.iter().map(ToString::to_string).collect(),
                allowed_grant_types: AllowedGrantType::ALL.to_vec(),
                secret_hash: None,
                registered_at: Utc::now(),
                disabled_at: None,
                registration_source: RegistrationSource::TrustedOnFirstUse,
            })
        })
        .expect("register client");
}
}

authorization-server-rust/tests/integration/common.rs lines 883–908 · authorization-server in the code index

Rows a flow would write, written straight to the store and moved through the domain’s own transitions, with deadlines the caller picks.

plant_authorization_code

Plant an Approved code-flow request plus its redeemable AuthorizationCode straight in the store, made in the browser session sid. expires_at (shared by both rows) lets a caller force an already-expired code without sleeping. The challenge is the real S256 digest of CODE_VERIFIER.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub fn plant_authorization_code(
    store: &SqliteGrantStore,
    sid: &str,
    client_id: &str,
    redirect_uri: &Url,
    scopes: &[&str],
    code: &str,
    expires_at: chrono::DateTime<Utc>,
) {
    let request_id = format!("req-{code}");
    let scope_vec: Vec<String> = scopes.iter().map(ToString::to_string).collect();
    let challenge = compute_code_challenge(CODE_VERIFIER);
    let now = Utc::now();
    let requested_at = expires_at.min(now) - Duration::seconds(1);
    let request = CodeRequest::new(
        NewCodeRequestArgs {
            id: request_id.clone(),
            client_id: client_id.to_string(),
            requested_scopes: scope_vec.clone(),
            ttl: expires_at - requested_at,
            redirect_uri: redirect_uri.clone(),
            code_challenge: challenge.clone(),
            client_state: "state".to_string(),
            sid: sid.to_owned(),
            launch: None,
            launch_bound_patient: None,
            pre_approved_scopes: Vec::new(),
            decidable_in_requesting_browser: false,
            awaits_limited_page: false,
        },
        requested_at,
    )
    .approve(
        Approval {
            granted_scopes: scope_vec.clone(),
            patient: None,
        },
        requested_at,
    )
    .expect("a pending request approves");
    store
        .write(|tx| tx.insert_code_request(&request))
        .expect("insert request");
    store
        .write(|tx| {
            tx.issue_authorization_code(&AuthorizationCode {
                code: code.to_string(),
                request_id,
                client_id: client_id.to_string(),
                redirect_uri: redirect_uri.clone(),
                code_challenge: challenge,
                granted_scopes: scope_vec,
                patient: None,
                issued_at: now,
                expires_at,
                sid: sid.to_owned(),
            })
        })
        .expect("issue code");
}
}

authorization-server-rust/tests/integration/common.rs lines 457–516 · authorization-server in the code index

plant_device_request

Plant a device-flow request directly, keyed by WILD-FLWR. status and expires_at are caller-controlled so the device state-machine tests can stand up approved or expired rows the public surface can’t mint on demand: the request starts pending just before it would expire (or now) and moves to status, an approval granting the requested scopes.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub fn plant_device_request(
    store: &SqliteGrantStore,
    client_id: &str,
    device_code: &str,
    scopes: &[&str],
    status: RequestStatus,
    expires_at: chrono::DateTime<Utc>,
) {
    let scope_vec: Vec<String> = scopes.iter().map(ToString::to_string).collect();
    let requested_at = expires_at.min(Utc::now()) - Duration::seconds(1);
    let pending = DeviceRequest::new(
        NewDeviceRequestArgs {
            id: device_code.to_string(),
            client_id: client_id.to_string(),
            requested_scopes: scope_vec.clone(),
            ttl: expires_at - requested_at,
            user_code: "WILD-FLWR".to_string(),
            device_name: None,
        },
        requested_at,
    );
    let approve = |request: &DeviceRequest| {
        request
            .approve(
                Approval {
                    granted_scopes: scope_vec.clone(),
                    patient: None,
                },
                None,
                requested_at,
            )
            .expect("a pending request approves")
    };
    let request = match status {
        RequestStatus::Pending => pending,
        RequestStatus::Approved => approve(&pending),
        RequestStatus::Denied => pending
            .deny(requested_at)
            .expect("a pending request denies"),
        RequestStatus::Claimed => approve(&pending)
            .claim(requested_at)
            .expect("an approved request is claimed"),
        RequestStatus::AwaitingLimitedPage => panic!("a device request has no limited page"),
    };
    store
        .write(|tx| tx.insert_device_request(&request))
        .expect("insert device request");
}
}

fn main() {
pub fn browser_session_token(res: &axum::response::Response) -> String {

        panic!("exactly one cookie, got {cookies:?}");

    cookie
        .strip_prefix("__Host-browser_session=")

}
}

fn main() {
pub fn polling_request_id(wait_page_location: &str) -> String {

        .and_then(|authorize| authorize.join(wait_page_location))
        .expect("the wait-page location resolves");

}
}

) -> axum::response::Response {

        .clone()
        .oneshot(build_request(
            Request::post(format!(
                "/authorization/oauth-consents/{request_id}/approve"
            ))
            .header("host", "127.0.0.1")
            .header("authorization", format!("Bearer {owner_token}"))

authorization-server-rust/tests/integration/common.rs lines 767–786 · authorization-server in the code index

authorize_and_approve

Drive /authorize → Owner consent approve for one request, made in the browser holding session_token, returning the pending request id. Callers assert on the consequences (grant rows, fast-path behaviour, refresh issuance); the flow itself is proven by auth_code_grant_happy_path_end_to_end. Uses the shared https://app.example/cb redirect and CODE_VERIFIER’s challenge.

approve_body carries acknowledgedRegistrationChange like any real approval; callers seed a client whose registration already covers the request, so the flag is ignored.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub async fn authorize_and_approve(
    g: &AuthorizationServer,
    owner_token: &str,
    session_token: &str,
    client_id: &str,
    scope_query: &str,
    approve_body: &'static str,
) -> String {
    let res = get_authorize(
        &g.router,
        session_token,
        &authorize_query(client_id, scope_query),
    )
    .await;
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::FOUND);
    let polling = res
        .headers()
        .get("location")
        .and_then(|v| v.to_str().ok())
        .expect("location")
        .to_string();
    let request_id = polling_request_id(&polling);
    let approve = build_request(
        Request::post(format!(
            "/authorization/oauth-consents/{request_id}/approve"
        ))
        .header("host", "127.0.0.1")
        .header("authorization", format!("Bearer {owner_token}"))
        .header("content-type", "application/json"),
        Body::from(approve_body),
    );
    let res = g.router.clone().oneshot(approve).await.expect("oneshot");
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    request_id
}
}

assert_cache_suppressed

Assert res carries both cache-suppression headers — Cache-Control: no-store and Pragma: no-cache — each exactly once. what names the response in the failure message.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
pub fn assert_cache_suppressed(res: &axum::response::Response, what: &str) {
    let values = |name: &str| -> Vec<&str> {
        res.headers()
            .get_all(name)
            .iter()
            .map(|v| v.to_str().expect("ascii header"))
            .collect()
    };
    assert_eq!(
        values("cache-control"),
        ["no-store"],
        "{what} must carry exactly one Cache-Control: no-store"
    );
    assert_eq!(
        values("pragma"),
        ["no-cache"],
        "{what} must carry exactly one Pragma: no-cache"
    );
}
}

pub fn jti_of(token: &str) -> String {
    let payload_b64 = token.split('.').nth(1).expect("jwt has a payload segment");
    let payload = base64::url_safe_no_pad_decode(payload_b64).expect("payload is base64url");
    let claims: Value = serde_json::from_slice(&payload).expect("payload is json");

        .expect("minted token carries a jti")

}
}

parked_page

The page a parked request’s Location names (wait or consent), and the request id before it.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn parked_page(res: &axum::response::Response) -> (String, String) {
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::FOUND);
    let location = location_of(res);
    let resolved = Url::parse("https://ruth.relay.example/oauth/authorize")
        .and_then(|authorize| authorize.join(&location))
        .expect("the location resolves");
    let mut segments = resolved.path_segments().expect("an absolute path");
    let page = segments.next_back().expect("a page").to_owned();
    let request_id = segments.next_back().expect("a request id").to_owned();
    (page, request_id)
}
}

                .header("content-type", "application/x-www-form-urlencoded"),
            Body::from("client_id=integration-test-app&scope=system%2F*.cruds"),
        ))
        .await
        .expect("oneshot");
    assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::OK);
    let body = body_json(res.into_body()).await;
    let field = |name: &str| body[name].as_str().expect(name).to_owned();
    DeviceAuthorization {
        device_code: field("device_code"),
        user_code: field("user_code"),
        verification_uri_complete: field("verification_uri_complete"),
    }
}
}

async fn start_pairing(g: &AuthorizationServer) -> StartedPairing {
    let res = post_json(

    assert_eq!(body["expiresIn"], 300);
    assert_eq!(body["interval"], 5);

        pairing_code: body["pairingCode"]
            .as_str()
            .expect("pairingCode")
            .to_owned(),
        user_code: body["userCode"].as_str().expect("userCode").to_owned(),
    }
}
}

paired_session_token

The paired session’s token a poll’s Set-Cookie carries, checked to last a day.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
fn paired_session_token(cookies: &[String]) -> String {
    let [cookie] = cookies else {
        panic!("exactly one cookie, got {cookies:?}");
    };
    let token = cookie
        .strip_prefix("__Host-browser_session=")
        .and_then(|rest| rest.split(';').next())
        .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("the browser session cookie, got {cookie}"))
        .to_owned();
    assert_eq!(
        cookie,
        &format!(
            "__Host-browser_session={token}; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; \
             Max-Age=86400"
        )
    );
    token
}
}

owner_decided_request

A browser signed in as the Owner starts a code request for new-app, which it decides on its own consent card: the session’s token and the request’s id.

#![allow(unused)]
fn main() {
async fn owner_decided_request(g: &AuthorizationServer) -> (String, String) {
    let same_device_session_token = signed_in_same_device_session_token(g).await;
    let res = send(
        g,
        Method::GET,
        &format!(
            "/oauth/authorize?{}",
            authorize_query("new-app", REQUESTED_SCOPES)
        ),
        Some(&format!(
            "__Host-browser_session={same_device_session_token}"
        )),
    )
    .await;
    let location = location_of(&res);
    assert!(location.ends_with("/consent"), "{location}");
    let request_id = location
        .trim_start_matches("authorize/")
        .trim_end_matches("/consent")
        .to_owned();
    (same_device_session_token, request_id)
}
}
